reference.title: Reference
reference.intro: Everything the books settle before you roll: correction dice, what a class costs and what each catalog holds.

classDescription.fighter: Heavy weapons and armour — the party's front line and its main damage dealer.
classDescription.grappler: Wrestling and unarmed combat; Chain Attack; its own weapon category; wears the same armour as a Fencer.
classDescription.fencer: A finesse fighter: halves a weapon's Required Strength (rounded up) and crits more often with any weapon.
classDescription.marksman: Ranged combat; unlike the other warrior classes its level does not add to Evasion.
classDescription.battle-dancer: +1 Evasion, Accuracy and damage per level; dance manoeuvres; Grappler weapons and armour; an extra feat from a short list at level 1.
classDescription.sorcerer: The damage school: spells arrive on their own with each level (~4 per level); needs a voice and free hands.
classDescription.conjurer: Summoning and puppet animation for scouting, undead and golems at higher levels; focuses through a magical artefact.
classDescription.priest: Healing, turning undead and blessings; you pick a deity when you take the class; focuses through a Holy Symbol.
classDescription.artificer: Magitech: magispheres become tools; the only class with guns and bullets; focuses through a magisphere of the right size.
classDescription.fairy-tamer: Calls fairies through gems by colour and type — earth, fire, water, wind, light, dark and 'fairy'; movement is limited while casting.
classDescription.druid: Calls the spirits of nature, ~59 spells; Symbols of Beneficence give powerful once-a-day blessings.
classDescription.daemonologist: Gate Imp and Abyss Gate: summons and banishes daemons through the Daemon Action Chart, ~46 spells.
classDescription.abyss-gazer: ~27 spells with an Enhancement system — an extra effect paid for with Daemon's Blood or an Abyss Shard. A separate class, not a Daemonologist under another name.
classDescription.bibliomancer: Spells are bought and found one at a time rather than granted by level, then prepared into a grimoire through slots.
classDescription.scout: Initiative: the class level is added to the roll. Perception: hidden threats, danger sense, locks, pockets, disguise and traps.
classDescription.ranger: Herbalism, first aid, survival and knowledge of terrain.
classDescription.sage: Monster knowledge and the weak points that come with it, plus general knowledge, research and appraisal.
classDescription.enhancer: Techniques: physical enhancement of the body — the Bard's trick turned on yourself.
classDescription.bard: Spellsongs in combat, rhythm banked as a resource, and Finales that spend it.
classDescription.rider: Handles a mount (animal, mythical beast or magitech), ~30 stunts, hired through the Rider's Guild. Riding rolls AGI; finding a mount's weak point rolls INT.
classDescription.alchemist: Evocations (~28 of them, and not magic) are paid for with Material Cards instead of MP: five colours across four ranks.
classDescription.tactician: Stratagems buff allies without spending MP and bank Edge, which pays for personal Maneuvers. Needs a voice and a Strategist Insignia.
classDescription.geomancer: A Geograph banks Qi points that turn into Aspects — a random effect over a zone; no MP, a Minor Action.
classDescription.heritor: Only helps characters with multiple sections — Diablos, Drakes, Basilisks, Scissorscorpions — whose other sections it drives: one Infusion per level, plus Defense, Max HP and Max MP for those sections. Barbarous Rage, a book outside files/; those races are not in the catalog yet.
classDescription.dark-hunter: Essence Weavings (28 of them): steering thrown weapons and buffing yourself at the cost of HP. Mental Power = class level + SPR modifier.

reference.featEffectsNote: Effect text is being transcribed feat by feat, starting with Core Rulebook I. A feat without it yet still lists its name and source book above.

combatFeatEffect.guardian-i: When declaring [Cover], multiple targets can be arbitrarily specified up to 3 maximum. As long as the target character is in the proper position, it will be covered by a melee attack, a ranged attack, or any other similar attack (effect "Evasion/Neg"). As a result, a character may be covered more than once in one round.
combatFeatEffect.dodge: The shield can be used to intercept the attack while gaining a favorable position for oneself and aiming for a fatal blow. The master of this feat should note the number of successful Evasion checks made against enemy melee attacks during a round. Then, on the first melee attack of his turn, the Critical Threshold is reduced by a number of successes (minimum of 8). If the attack deals damage to multiple targets, only one master's damage decision gains this effect. Even if the player makes a second or later melee attack on their turn, they do not gain this effect. To gain this effect, the player must have a shield equipped at the time of the Evasion check, but they do not need to have a shield equipped when they make their own attack.
combatFeatEffect.evasive-maneuvers-i: The master gets a +1 bonus to Evasion checks.
combatFeatEffect.tenacity: The master's Maximum HP increases by +15.
combatFeatEffect.twin-strike: In the case of two attacks with [Dual Wielding], after checking the result of the first attack, the master can choose whether to attack the same target further or choose another target to attack.
combatFeatEffect.targeting: The master's shots do not risk straying when making a ranged attack targeting a character in the skirmish or when performing an "Area: Shot" spell or effect.
combatFeatEffect.hawk-eye: The master can see beyond the shielded area, including that caused by hostile characters and skirmish, and can make ranged attacks and use magic through the shielded area.
combatFeatEffect.improved-throw-i: When the master performs a Throw, the power of the Throw is increased by +10. The Throw is no longer limited to bipedal characters or their method of movement and can be used on any character with up to 2 sections. Two section characters will need only one Accuracy to hit. The attacked target may choose any section to perform an Evasion check, and if the Evasion check fails, the target will be hit (if a melee attack is not possible in either section due to an [Attack Obstacle] or some other reason, the target will be unaffected by the Throw attack). All sections will be thrown, and at the same time, the attacker may inflict damage on each section.
combatFeatEffect.dual-technique: The penalty to the Accuracy check for two attacks from [Dual Wielding] is eliminated.
combatFeatEffect.weapon-proficiency-a: Master must choose a weapon category for **, such as Swords or Axes, when they acquire this feat. When they wield a weapon of that category, they deal +1 damage with it. In addition, they can wield A rank weapons of that category. [Weapon Proficiency A/**], which has different categories, can be learned several times by using separate learning slots.
combatFeatEffect.weapon-proficiency-s: Master must choose a weapon category for ** when they acquire this feat for which they have [Weapon Proficiency A/**]. When they wield a weapon of that category, they deal +2 damage (+3 total) with it. In addition, they can wield S rank weapons of that category.
combatFeatEffect.stomp: When the master successfully makes a Throw, the target can be additionally attacked with a Kick. When [Improved Throw] simultaneously throws more than one section, the Kick can be made at any one section of this target. [Chain Attack] cannot be added to this Kick attack.
combatFeatEffect.ever-changing-i: The master may declare the active combat feat twice per round, either by declaring two different feats in one attack and applying them both together, or by declaring one feat in each of the different attacks (to allow for multiple attacks). In the latter case, the same feat may be declared twice. If the declared feats have risks, they are all applied cumulatively, even if the same feat is declared multiple times.
combatFeatEffect.armor-proficiency-a: Master must choose an armor category for **, such as Metal Armor or Shield, when they acquire this feat. When the master is equipped with the armor of the corresponding category, they gain +1 to Defense. The master may also equip A-rank armor of the corresponding category. It is possible to learn [Armor Proficiency A/**] for different categories by using separate learning slots. In this case, if both categories of armor are equipped, the increase in Defense will be cumulative.
combatFeatEffect.armor-proficiency-s: Master must choose an armor category for ** when they acquire this feat for which they have [Armor Proficiency A/**]. When the master is equipped with the armor of the corresponding category, they gain +2 (+3 total) to Defense. The master may also equip S-rank armor of the corresponding category.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-master: The master can declare [Universal Metamagic] and combine [Metamagic/Targets] with other [Metamagic/**], and can decide which one is combined with which Metamagic for each target separately. The MP consumption of the target is added up after the target's declaration. For example, one character's target may not be specifically affected by Metamagic, but another may be affected simultaneously by [Metamagic/Power Assurance] and [Metamagic/Distance]. If this is [Energy Bolt] (costs originally 5 MP), the MP consumption would be (5)+(5x2x3)=35 points.
combatFeatEffect.dual-wielding: The master can have one "Stance: 1H (1H# is not allowed)" weapon with a minimum strength of 20 or less in each arm and can make one attack with each of them in one Major Action. Each of these attacks will have a -2 penalty on the Accuracy check. Which arm is used for the attack is arbitrary, and each may perform Accuracy checks and damage decisions with different Warrior-Type Classes. The target cannot be changed between the first and second attacks, but the second attack can be canceled after checking the result of the first attack.
combatFeatEffect.mp-save: Choose one Wizard class for ** when acquiring this feat, such as Sorcerer or Priest. Whenever you use magic with the corresponding class, the MP consumption is reduced by 1 point (minimum 1 MP). When using [Metamagic/**], the MP consumption by this combat feat is reduced first, and then multiplied to calculate the final MP consumption. This combat feat may be acquired for different classes using separate learning slots.
combatFeatEffect.infight-i: This feat must be declared on a single character at the time of declaration. Also, it cannot be declared on a turn when a melee attack or ranged attack is performed on any other character. If a melee attack is made using the Grappler class against the given character for a period of 10 seconds (1 round), the master gains a +2 bonus to Accuracy checks. However, the user may not attack any other character until the beginning of their next turn (but may attack other sections of a multi-section character). Also, as a risk, all Evasion checks are subject to a -2 penalty.
combatFeatEffect.decoy-attack-i: An overtly large attack to draw attention and aid the attacker's allies. It is declared when a melee attack is made and is active for that one attack. It cannot be declared when attacking multiple targets at the same time. Accuracy checks are penalized by -2, but the damage is increased by +2 on a hit. If the declared attack is evaded, the enemy receives a -1 penalty to Evasion checks for the next 10 seconds (1 round). This effect is cumulative up to -4, but if the target fails an Evasion check even once, the penalty is removed.
combatFeatEffect.cover-i: When declaring this feat, the user can specify any one willing character. During the following 10 seconds (1 round), if the specified character becomes the target of a melee attack, ranged attack, or similar unique skill (an Evasion/Neg effect), the user becomes a target instead, and it always hits as the user cannot make an Evasion check. For this effect to take effect, the character and the user must be in the same area. If an effect occurs as part of an attack, the user receives the effect immediately after substitution. The effect of [Cover] is automatically applied only once per round when the target is targeted.
combatFeatEffect.repeated-strike-i: This feat can be declared when performing a melee attack with a weapon with "Stance: 2H" and is valid for one attack. If the declared attack is evaded, another melee attack can be made immediately afterward with the same weapon on the same target. If multiple attacks are made simultaneously, another accuracy check can be performed on all targets evading them. If either the first or second attack hits, a damage decision is made for each.
combatFeatEffect.aimed-attack-i: When a melee attack or ranged attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If multiple attacks are made at the same time, the effect is applied to all of them. Declared attacks gain a +1 bonus to the Accuracy check, but the critical threshold is increased by +1 for the damage decision. A critical threshold of 13 or more will never result in a critical hit.
combatFeatEffect.power-strike-i: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, its damage is increased by +4. As a risk, any Evasion checks take a -2 penalty. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, the user needs to select one character at random from among that hit. Then, the damage to that one character will be increased by +4 points. This target selection is made before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.taunting-strike-i: When a melee attack or ranged attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If multiple attacks are made at the same time, the effect is applied to all of them. The target hit by the declared attack is provoked and must attack the user as much as possible during the following 10 seconds (1 round) (the method of attack is unrestricted). [Taunting Strike I] has no effect on characters with an intellect of 18 or more, or on monsters with an intellect of "High." It also has no effect if the provoked target is unable to attack the user or if the target is in a different area. The damage dealt by an attack with this declaration is reduced by -2 points; even if the applied damage is 0, the provocation still will be effective.
combatFeatEffect.defensive-stance: This feat must be declared before any Skill Check is performed on the turn. If the user is under the continuous effect of any check at the beginning of their turn, they may declare it immediately before that check. The user should choose one of "Evasion check," "Fortitude," or "Willpower" and get a +4 bonus until the beginning of their next turn. Each time they declare, they can choose a different check. As a risk, all other checks except the two not selected above and the Death Check suffer a -4 penalty. However, if this combat feat is declared during Combat Preparation, the Initiative check and Monster Knowledge check at the time of Combat Preparation are exempt from this risk. This combat feat is limited to Normal Move or Limited Move. It cannot be declared if a Full Move is performed on this turn.
combatFeatEffect.cleave-i: When a melee attack is made with a non-wrestling Stance: 2H weapon, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. The user can attack up to 3 targets within the user's reach. Only one Accuracy check can be made against them. If more than one hits, the damage is determined individually, but all are reduced by -3.
combatFeatEffect.violentcast-i: It can be declared at the time of the cast spell and is valid for the one time of the cast. If the spell only deals damage to the target, the user gains a +2 bonus to the success value of the Spellcasting check. This feat does not have any effect on spells that do not deal damage or have effects other than dealing damage.
combatFeatEffect.lethal-strike-i: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, the damage roll is increased by +1 if the roll is 3-11. Double 1s and double 6s work as is. The same is true for all criticals for this damage decision. As a risk, any Evasion check is subject to a -2 penalty. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, the user needs to select one character at random from among that hit. The above process is then used to calculate the damage to that one character. This target selection is made before the damage is determined.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-power-assurance: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they must spend twice as much MP as they would normally spend and gain the following benefits. If the 2d roll when using the power table for spell damage is 4 or less, the roll can only be rerolled once and use either result.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-accuracy: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they must spend twice as much MP as they would normally spend and gain the following benefits. Spellcasting checks can be performed by rolling 2d twice and selecting the desired roll.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-targets: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they gain the following benefits. Increases the number of targets for the spell with "Target: 1 character (including 1 Entire Character and 1 Character X)", "Target: One Object," and "Target: 1 spell". However, a spell with "Range: Caster" or "Range: Touch" cannot be affected. Each additional target multiplies the MP consumed (2x for 2 targets, 3x for 3 targets, etc.). The Spellcasting check should be done once for all targets.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-distance: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they gain the following benefits. Increases the spell's distance. However, a spell with "Range: Caster" or "Range: Touch" cannot be affected. For every 2x or 3x the range distance increase, the MP to be consumed is doubled or tripled, etc. The multiplier can only be chosen in integer multiples. In Simplified Combat, "Range: 1" can be changed to "Range: 2" by doubling the MP cost.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-time: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they gain the following benefits. Extends the duration of the spell. Spells with "Duration: Instant" and "Duration: Permanent" cannot be affected. The portion can be extended in the case of "Duration: Instant/X". The MP consumed is doubled or tripled for every doubling or tripling of time. The multiplier can only be chosen in integer multiples.
combatFeatEffect.metamagic-area: In the turn in which the user declares this feat, they may choose whether or not to perform this Metamagic on all spell casts. If the user chooses to use this Metamagic, they gain the following benefits. The effect area of a spell whose target is "1 area (XX radius)/Space", "1 area (XX radius)/All", or "1 area (XX radius)/Y", and whose radius is 2 to 5 meters, will be expanded. +1m doubles the MP cost, +2m triples it, etc. However, the radius can only be expanded to a maximum of 6m. If the spell has a maximum number of targets (i.e., "1 area (XX radius)/Y"), the maximum number of targets is also increased by +5 for each 1m increase in radius. In Simplified Combat, only the maximum number of targets can be increased.
combatFeatEffect.universal-metamagic: At the turn of the user who declared this combat feat, the player can choose whether or not to obtain the effect of any of the [Metamagic/**] for all spell casts. The user doesn't need to know all [Metamagic/**] to use them in any combination. In addition, multiple effects may be combined. In that case, the MP consumption is calculated by multiplying all the coefficients determined for each Metamagic. For example, if the user selects [Metamagic/Targets] to target 2 characters and [Metamagic/Time] to extend the duration by 3 times, they have to spend 2x3=6 times the MP.
combatFeatEffect.magic-convergence: Affects the next spell to be cast on this turn. The spell with "Target: 1 area (XX radius)/Y" can be cast as a "Target: 1 Character".
combatFeatEffect.magic-control: Affects the next spell to be cast on this turn. When the declared spell has "Area: Line" or "Target: 1 area (XX radius)/Y", any character within the range can be excluded from the targets of the spell in advance.
combatFeatEffect.mana-strike: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, the damage is increased by the attacker's Magic Power. The risk is a -2 penalty to any Fortitude or Willpower check of the user. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, the user needs to select one character at random from among that hit. Then, the damage to that one character will be increased. This target selection is made before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.multi-action: Allows the master to make a melee attack and cast a spell with one Major Action. If a character declares a melee attack, they can cast a spell immediately afterward. Conversely, if a character casts a spell, they may perform a melee attack immediately thereafter. Even if the character has the ability to declare multiple combat feats in one round, they cannot declare an additional [Multi-Action] for an additional melee attack or spell cast. The conditions for casting spells must be met, and movement is limited to Limited Move.
combatFeatEffect.armor-piercer-i: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, the attack target's Defense is treated as half (rounded up), but the critical threshold is increased by +1 in the damage determination. A critical hit will never occur if the critical threshold is 13 or more. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, the user needs to select one character at random from among that hit. The above process is then performed when applying damage to that one character. This target selection is made before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.snipe: The archer who uses this combat feat specifies a target with which the shooting attack is possible at the time of use, and the Total damage is doubled if the archer makes a shooting attack on that target in their next Major Action and hits with a success value that is 3 or higher than the target's Evasion check success value. If the user's success value is 1 or 2 higher than the target's success value, the target will be hit, but the Total Damage will not be doubled. Of course, if the user's success value is not equal to or higher than the target's success value, the attack fails. The user must be able to attack the target without causing a stray shot, both when using the combat feat and when executing a shooting attack. Movement when using the combat feat is also limited to Limited Move. If another Major Action is performed after the combat feat instead of a shooting attack, its effect will be lost. The user cannot overlap the effects of this skill with abilities, magic, "ammunition", etc., that can attack multiple enemies at the same time. If they use them, the effects of this skill do not occur.
combatFeatEffect.wordbreak: With "Range: Touch" and "Target: 1 spell", one sustained spell or effect will be released. Only spells or unique skills with a duration of more than 10 seconds (1 round) can be canceled. Effects that are "Permanent" in duration, effects that are "Instant" in duration, effects that result in a fall prone (e.g., a Throw), and effects that are continuous (e.g., being grabbed and rendered immobile) cannot be canceled. The effect "Duration: Instant/X seconds/minutes (rounds)" can be canceled. To remove the effect, the user must perform a Skill Check using their own Magic Power as the standard value, and compare the success value with the effect to be removed. The effect is canceled if the user's success value is higher than the standard value. Please follow the rules for forced removal (Core I, p. 166).
combatFeatEffect.chain-attack: When a melee attack is made with a wrestling weapon with "Stance: 1H," an additional melee attack can be made again on the same target with a wrestling weapon with "Stance: 1H". The weapon used for the initial attack may be different from the weapon used for the additional attack. Only one additional attack is allowed when two attacks are made with [Dual Wielding]. This additional attack does not incur the -2 penalty to the Accuracy check.
combatFeatEffect.treasure-hunt: The master gains +1 to the roll when making a Loot Determination. This effect is cumulative with other effects that increase the roll of loot decisions. Vagrant characters may choose [Plunder] or [Crude Take] instead of [Treasure Hunt] when they reach level 5 in the Scout class; if they do, they will never have the chance to take [Treasure Hunt].
combatFeatEffect.survivability: In the natural environment, when performing a Fortitude or Willpower check, the master can automatically succeed without rolling any dice (declared before rolling the dice for the check). This effect can be used only once per day. Vagrant characters may choose the automatic combat feat [Crude Take] instead of [Survivability] when they reach level 5 in the Ranger class; if they do, they will never have the chance to get [Survivability].
combatFeatEffect.keen-eyes: The master gains +1 to the roll when making a Loot Determination. This effect is cumulative with other effects that increase the roll of loot decisions. Vagrant characters may choose [Plunder] instead of [Keen Eyes] when they reach level 5 in the Sage class; if they do, they will never have the chance to get [Keen Eyes].
combatFeatEffect.footwork: Can move up to 10m with Limited Move. However, if the character's movement is less than 10, it is limited to that movement. In Simplified Combat, a character can move one area with Limited Move.
combatFeatEffect.guardian-ii: The same as [Guardian I], but the master can declare up to 1 to 5 targets when declaring [Cover].
combatFeatEffect.evasive-maneuvers-ii: The master always gets a +2 bonus to Evasion checks that use the Fencer class as the standard value.
combatFeatEffect.archer-s-grace: Master may calculate Evasion using their Marksman Class Level + Agility Modifier.
combatFeatEffect.intense-finale: The power of damage and recovery effects of the Finale is increased by 10.
combatFeatEffect.additional-songs-i: The mastery of this Combat Specialty will allow the mastery of +1 Spellsong or Finale. In other words, they can learn up to a total of "Bard Level +1" Spellsong and Finale in total.
combatFeatEffect.additional-songs-ii: The number of Spellsong and Finale that can be learned is increased by an additional +1 (total +2) from [Additional Songs I].
combatFeatEffect.throwing-i: A potion can be placed in the Potion Ball, which can be used as a thrown weapon. The range is "1 (10m)," and the target is always hit unless there is an automatic failure on the Accuracy check. If the target is hit, the potion's effect is given to the target. In this case, it is considered "Resistance: Optional" (if the target does not wish to be hit, it will not be affected). Also, the master always gets a +1 bonus to Accuracy checks on any thrown attacks.
combatFeatEffect.throwing-ii: In addition to the effects of [Throwing I], all thrown weapon attacks that have a "Range: 1 (10m)" (including the thrown weapon of the Potion Ball) will now have a "Range: 2 (20m)".
combatFeatEffect.super-tenacity: Master's Maximum HP increases by +15 (30 points in total with [Tenacity]).
combatFeatEffect.special-instrument-proficiency: This feat allows the master to equip and use items classified as Special Instruments. However, equipping items that can be used as weapons or armor does not increase Extra Damage or Defense as other proficiency feats do.
combatFeatEffect.flying-kick: The master may attack a target with a Kick only after performing a Normal Move and moving at least 1 area (Simplified Combat) or 10 meters (Standard Combat). This attack does not activate [Chain Attack]. The master may then perform a normal Major Action.
combatFeatEffect.improved-throw-ii: When the master performs a Throw, the power of the Throw is increased by +20. Throw can be used against any character with up to 3 sections, regardless of movement method or the number of legs. When attacking a character with multiple sections, an Accuracy check is performed only once. The attacked target may choose any section to complete an Evasion check. If the Evasion check fails, the target will be thrown (if a melee attack is not possible in any section due to an [Attack Obstacle] or other reason, the target cannot be affected with the Throw). All sections will be thrown, and at the same time, the attacker can deal damage to each section.
combatFeatEffect.harmony: A Bard with this Combat Feat can start another Spellsong while their Pet is still performing a Spellsong, compounding its effect and causing both to occur simultaneously. In this case, the Pet's Spellsong is also treated as having the same effect range as its owner and the same Success Value as its owner's Performance check. If the Bard does not make a Performance check, or if the Performance check is an Automatic Failure, the Pet's Spellsong will still continue, but with a Success Value of 0. If a Finale is used, the Pet's Spellsong will instead copy the same Success Value of the Finale. The Pet's Spellsong still does not generate any Rhythm.
combatFeatEffect.block: The master treats themself as twice as many characters (number of sections) in a situation where a movement blocking or a withdrawal from the skirmish occurs. This affects all of the following cases: when the master moves, when a friendly character passes through or leaves the skirmish, when they block the movement of a hostile character, and when a hostile character attempts to withdraw from the skirmish. In addition, a character initially placed in the frontline in Simplified Combat is treated as having twice the number of characters (number of sections) as itself, regardless of whether they go first or second.
combatFeatEffect.mako-stones-master: Master can use up to two mako stones simultaneously to cast a spell using their combined MP values. The number of MP consumed from either stone can be allocated freely, and it is possible to use a combination of both stones and one's own MP.
combatFeatEffect.marionette: When the master gives "Obey Command" to a golem, undead or fairy, its turn is not fixed immediately after the master's turn but can be any turn within the allies' turn. The limitation of one "Obey Command" per turn for golem and undead, and one for fairy, remains unchanged. For example, if a player orders a fairy to act before their turn and then summons another fairy, the newly summoned fairy cannot be given a command and act in the same round.
combatFeatEffect.powerful-magic-i: The master gains +1 to the Magic Power of any magic system they have mastered.
combatFeatEffect.pinpoint-attack-i: Increase the master's Accuracy checks by +1.
combatFeatEffect.muscle-mystery: It triples the duration of all Techniques. This does not work on Techniques whose duration is "Instant."
combatFeatEffect.infight-ii: Same as [Infight I], but it not only gains a +2 bonus to Accuracy checks, but it also gains +4 damage points on a hit.
combatFeatEffect.decoy-attack-ii: Same as [Decoy Attack I], but the damage on a hit is +8. In addition, the penalty to the Evasion check given when the declared attack is evaded is -2, and it accumulates up to -8.
combatFeatEffect.rhythm-conversion: This particular move can be declared at any time during the turn. When declaring this feat, one Rhythm that has already accumulated "1" or higher is chosen, and its accumulation is reduced by -1. At the same time, it can also increase the accumulation of any other Rhythm by +1. Whether or not a Spellsong with effect generation conditions generates an effect depends on the timing of the Performance check. Even if the Rhythm is changed after the check and the condition is satisfied, the effect will not be generated. Conversely, if the effect is generated and the condition is not met after conversion with this technique, the effect will not disappear.
combatFeatEffect.mirage-arrow: The attack is declared to be made with a thrown weapon or bow and is valid for one attack of that category. The attack declared with this feat will use the same two thrown weapons or ammunition for shooting at the same time. The weapon is treated as if the two can be thrown together without needing to change weapons, except in the case of a thrown weapon. Accuracy checks may be made twice, taking the better of the two rolls. Only one attack will hit the target.
combatFeatEffect.cover-ii: The effect of this combat feat is exactly the same as [Cover I]. This feat is not a declaration and doesn't count toward several active combat feats per turn. In other words, other active combat feat declarations can be made even if this is used. If a character can have multiple declarations, it can be declared separately from this feat that number of times. The feat itself may only be declared once per round. The same is true for a character with multiple declarations.
combatFeatEffect.nerve-strike: Declared at the time of a melee attack, it is valid for that single attack. It cannot be declared when attacking multiple targets at the same time. If that attack hits, for the next 10 seconds (1 round), the target's physical damage caused by the enemy (section) will be reduced by -8 damage.
combatFeatEffect.repeated-strike-ii: Same as [Repeated Strike I], except that if the declared attack hits on the first Accuracy check, the damage is increased by +4 points. If multiple attacks are made simultaneously, another Accuracy check can be performed on all targets that evaded them. The player may choose any one of the characters hit by the first attack to increase damage by +4 points (the choice should be made before the damage is determined).
combatFeatEffect.critical-cast-i: Declared when the spell is cast and is valid for one cast. If the spell uses the Power Table to determine damage, the Critical Threshold is reduced by -1 (minimum 8).
combatFeatEffect.aimed-attack-ii: Same as [Aimed Attack I], except the bonus to the Accuracy check is +2, and there is no increase (or decrease) of the Critical Threshold.
combatFeatEffect.confident-performer: This combat feat can be declared using a Finale that has "Resistance: Half." If the declaration is made, the Finale is treated as "Resistance: Can't," but at the same time its Critical Threshold is changed to "None." Only a change in the type of resistance and type of immunities can negate the Finale's effect.
combatFeatEffect.skillful-play: This Combat Feat is declared when using a Spellsong or Finale. In the use of a Spellsong or Finale where the declaration has been made, the Performance check is made twice, and either result can be used. If a comparison of Success Values is required, the player performs this process first, and then the passive side rolls the result only once.
combatFeatEffect.power-strike-ii: Same as [Power Strike I], but the damage is increased by +12 on hit.
combatFeatEffect.double-cast: This feat can be declared with a spell cast with Major Action. After the spell is cast with the Major Action while declaring this feat, an additional spell may be cast one more time immediately afterward. The spell that can be cast additionally is limited to "1/2 of the maximum level or rank (rounded up) of the second spell's magic system." Its Magic Power will be reduced by -10 (minimum 0).
combatFeatEffect.taunting-strike-ii: The same as [Taunting Strike I], but with limited effect on characters with an intellect of 18 or more and monsters with "Intellect: High." They are not forced to attack the character who performed [Taunting Strike II] but will be given a -2 penalty to their success value in Accuracy checks, Spellcasting checks, and other unique skill checks. The effect of [Taunting Strike II] is applied for 10 seconds (1 round) after the attack hits.
combatFeatEffect.tail-swing-i: This feat can only be declared when a melee attack is made with the wrestling weapon Tail and works for one attack. With a Tail attack, the attacker attacks up to 3 characters who share the same coordinates or are within the skirmish. The attacker's Accuracy check is made only once, with a -1 penalty. The damage should be determined individually if the attacker hits more than one character.
combatFeatEffect.tail-swing-ii: The same as [Tail Swing I], but up to 5 characters can be attacked with the Tail, and there is no penalty to the Accuracy check.
combatFeatEffect.cleave-ii: Same as [Cleave I], but the user can make a melee attack on up to 5 characters, and there is no reduction in damage.
combatFeatEffect.lethal-strike-ii: Same as [Lethal Strike I], but with a reduced penalty modifier of -1 to the Evasion check risk.
combatFeatEffect.armor-piercer-ii: Same as [Armor Piercer I]; when a critical hit occurs in the damage decision, the attack target's Defense is treated as "0".
combatFeatEffect.toughness: Master's maximum HP increases by +15 points.
combatFeatEffect.counter: When hit by a melee attack, the player can try to avoid the enemy's attack while attempting to hit with their own attack. The decision to do this can be made after checking the success value of the enemy's Accuracy check. In this case, instead of an Evasion check, an Accuracy check is made with any weapon equipped by the player, and the success values are compared with each other. In this case, contrary to a normal Evasion check, the side attempting the [Counter] is the active side, and the side that attempted a melee attack first is the passive side. If the active side is favored, the passive side's melee attack is canceled, and at the same time, the damage and effects associated with the attack are processed as if the passive side had been hit by the weapon used by the active side. If the passive side is favored, its melee attack will hit. Still, the roll of 2d for power table reference and damage determination will be considered "12" in determining the total damage. The second and subsequent rounds should be handled as normal if a critical hit occurs. [Counter] may only be attempted once per round, regardless of its success or failure.
combatFeatEffect.fast-action: In the Initiative check, if the player's success value is greater than the maximum value of the enemy's success value (or greater than or equal to the Initiative monster data), the player can take one additional Major Action in the first round.
combatFeatEffect.shadow-sneak: The master's movement cannot be blocked. They may also leave the skirmish by moving at will without preparing to withdraw from the melee.
combatFeatEffect.indomitable: If the master succeeds in making a Death Check, even if their HP is 0 or less, they will not be unconscious and can continue to perform actions; if they fail the Death Check, they die.
combatFeatEffect.potion-master: The master may use an item classified as a Potion during Combat Preparation or with Minor Action only when used on themself. This feat is limited to one potion during Combat Preparation or one Minor Action per round.
combatFeatEffect.weakness-exploit: If the master performs a Monster Knowledge check with the Sage class and obtains a success value greater than or equal to the monster's weakness, the bonus generated by the weak point and the increment of damage is doubled for the master. For example, if the weak point is "Accuracy +1", the bonus to Accuracy will become +2, and if the weak point is "Fire damage +3 points", the damage will be increased by +6. This effect only applies to the master; other allied characters will only benefit from the normal effect of the weak point.
combatFeatEffect.mana-save: When using MP for any reason, reduce the MP spent by -1. This cannot reduce an MP cost lower than 1 (at least 1 point is consumed). When the MP consumption is doubled by [Metamagic/**], the reduction is calculated first and then doubled. [Mana Save] has no effects that damage MP or reduce MP instead of consuming MP as regular spells do.
combatFeatEffect.capacity: Maximum MP increased by +15 points. Grassrunner characters cannot acquire this combat feat.
combatFeatEffect.additional-songs-iii: The number of Spellsong and Finale that can be learned is increased by an additional +1 (total +3) from [Additional Songs II].
combatFeatEffect.peerless-double-swords: Removes the minimum strength limitation of the weapons that can be equipped from [Dual Wielding].
combatFeatEffect.weapon-master: The master will be able to equip all rank weapons (including SS rank) of all categories. However, class restrictions still apply.
combatFeatEffect.enhanced-evocations-i: The master gets a +1 bonus to the success value of any Evocation check they perform.
combatFeatEffect.enhanced-evocations-ii: The master gets a +2 bonus to the success value of any Evocation check they perform.
combatFeatEffect.distant-evocations: The master treats the Evocation of "Range/Area: Touch/-" as "Range/Area: 1(10m)/Shot". If their Evocation is "Target: 1 Character", they can select multiple targets simultaneously by doubling the number of material cards they consume.
combatFeatEffect.ever-changing-ii: The master may declare the active combat feat three times per round, either by declaring three different feats in one attack and applying them each together, or by declaring one feat in each of the different attacks (to allow for multiple attacks). How the master divides the three declarations is optional. If the declared feats have risks, they are all applied cumulatively, even if the same feat is declared multiple times.
combatFeatEffect.armor-master: The master will be able to equip all rank armor (including SS rank) of all categories.
combatFeatEffect.powerful-magic-ii: The master gains +2 to the Magic Power of any magic system they have mastered.
combatFeatEffect.pinpoint-attack-ii: Increase the master's Accuracy checks by +2.
combatFeatEffect.consecutive-evocation: When using an Evocation with a Major Action, the master may use two different Evocations once with each Major Action. An Evocation check is performed for each Evocation, and the target is defined separately for each Evocation.
combatFeatEffect.aimed-attack-iii: Melee Attack and Ranged Attack should be declared simultaneously and effective for one attack. If multiple attacks are made simultaneously, the effect is applied to all of them. The declared attack gains a +3 bonus to Accuracy checks.
combatFeatEffect.critical-cast-ii: Declared when the spell is cast and is valid for one cast. The following effects are also applied in addition to the effects of [Critical Cast I]. The target's critical immunity and Critical Threshold modification abilities are all ignored, and for spells with "Resistance: Half," a critical hit will occur when using the power table even if the target resists. In this case, the total damage is determined with criticals, and then it is halved.
combatFeatEffect.power-strike-iii: Declared at the time of a melee attack and valid for one attack. If the declared attack hits, the damage is increased by +20 points. At risk, any Evasion check is modified by a -2 penalty. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, one of the hit characters should be chosen randomly. Then, the damage to that one character will be increased by +20 points. This target selection should be made before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.violentcast-ii: It can be declared at the time of the cast spell and is valid for the one time of the cast. If the spell only damages the target, the user gains a +3 bonus to the success value of the Spellcasting check. This feat does not affect spells that do not deal damage or have effects other than dealing damage. This feat even works for spells that increase damage based on specific conditions, such as the target's classification.
combatFeatEffect.lethal-strike-iii: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, the target's critical immunity and Critical Threshold modification abilities are all ignored. The damage roll is increased by +1 if the roll is 3-11. Double 1s and double 6s work as is. The same is true for all criticals for this damage decision. When attacking multiple characters simultaneously, the user must select one character randomly from among that hit. The above process is then used to calculate the damage to that one character. This target selection is made before the damage is determined.
combatFeatEffect.armor-piercer-iii: When a melee attack is made, this feat can be declared at the time of the attack and is effective for that single attack. If the declared attack hits, the attack target's Defense is treated as half (rounded up). The target's critical immunity and Critical Threshold modification abilities are all ignored. When a critical occurs, Defense is treated as 0. It does not increase (or worsen) the Critical Threshold. When attacking multiple characters simultaneously, the user must select one character randomly from among that hit. Then, the above process is performed when applying damage to that character. This target selection is made before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.battle-master: The master may declare two active combat feats in one round. The same active combat feat may not be declared more than once per action. It is possible to declare the same active combat feat for two different actions or to combine two different active combat feats for one action. If the declared feats have risk, they are all cumulative.
combatFeatEffect.rune-master: The master may declare two active combat feats per round. However, at least one of them must be of "Use: Wizard-Type Class," and the same active combat feat may not be declared more than once in a single turn.
combatFeatEffect.treasure-master: The master gains +1 to the roll of the Loot Determination. This effect accumulates with other Loot Determination-increasing effects.
combatFeatEffect.skill-master: Once per check, the Scout may reroll 2d after seeing the 2d result of a skill check using Scout Class Level for standard value calculation. This reroll can be done only once per Skill Check. If there is any other reroll effect, it is assumed that the number of rerolls increases only by +1.
combatFeatEffect.shukuchi: The master may perform the actions that can be performed during a Normal Move on the round in which the Full Move is performed. The type of move itself does not change, and the penalty to the Evasion check (-4) must also be taken.
combatFeatEffect.run-and-gun: The master can perform the actions that can be performed during a Limited Move in the round in which the Normal Move is performed. The type of move itself does not change.
combatFeatEffect.mana-resistance: Reduce all Magic Damage the master receives by -5.
combatFeatEffect.sage-s-wisdom: Once per check, the Sage may reroll 2d after seeing the 2d result of a skill check using Sage Class Level for standard value calculation. This reroll can be done only once per Skill Check. If there is any other reroll effect, it is assumed that the number of rerolls increases only by +1.
combatFeatEffect.spreading-triad: When the Aspect is activated, two targets are selected at random within the range. It is important that the two targets are different from each other. When canceling the effect of the Aspect, the master can choose to cancel both targets or cancel only one of the two targets and affect the remaining character.
combatFeatEffect.dividing-triad: Once the targets of the Aspects have been determined, the master can cancel any undesired effects of the Aspect to be given by the Geomancer. Then, apply the remaining effects of the other Aspects to the target.
combatFeatEffect.frontline-mastermind: The user of this feat accumulates +2 points of Edge if their own Initiative success value is greater than the maximum value of the enemy's Initiative (or greater than or equal to the Initiative of the monster data).
combatFeatEffect.additional-stratagem-maneuver-i: This Combat Feat mastery allows for an additional +1 Stratagem or Maneuver to be acquired, resulting in a total of "Tactician class level +1" Stratagems and Maneuvers that can be learned.
combatFeatEffect.additional-stratagem-maneuver-ii: The number of Stratagem or Maneuver that can be learned is increased by an additional +1 (total +2) from [Additional Stratagem/Maneuver I].
combatFeatEffect.additional-stratagem-maneuver-iii: The number of Stratagem or Maneuver that can be learned is increased by an additional +1 (total +3) from [Additional Stratagem/Maneuver II].
combatFeatEffect.versatile: The user can declare this feat immediately after using a Stratagem of two or more Ranks lower than the one used in the previous round. For example, if the user used Rank 3 in the previous round, they can declare this feat if they start at Rank 1. If Rank 4 is used immediately before, they can declare this feat if they start at Rank 1 or 2. If Rank 5 is used immediately before, they can declare this feat if they start at Rank 1, 2, or 3. Using this feat will earn the user 2 points of Edge.
combatFeatEffect.follow-up: When the master attacks with [Shield Bash] and the target falls prone, the master can make an additional melee attack on the target. When making an additional melee attack under the effect of this Combat Feat, the weapon must be with "Stance: 1H" or its equivalent.
combatFeatEffect.enhanced-resistance-i: The master gains the will to survive. Whenever they make a Fortitude, Willpower, or Death Check, they gain a +1 bonus modifier.
combatFeatEffect.enhanced-resistance-ii: When making Fortitude, Willpower or Death Checks, always get an additional +1 bonus modifier (+2 total).
combatFeatEffect.cheat-cast-i: When a spell that has already been cast is cast again, its Success Value is increased. During combat, if the user has already made a Spellcasting check of the same name on previous turns, the user gains a +2 bonus to the Success Value of the Spellcasting check after the declaration. If the spell has already been cast, it is valid even if the target was changed at the time of casting or if the result of the first Spellcasting check was an automatic failure.
combatFeatEffect.desperate-strike-i: This feat allows the user to deal a large amount of damage to the target while disregarding their own injuries. It is declared when performing a melee attack and is valid for one attack. If the attack hits, the damage is increased by +5 points. However, immediately after determining the damage, the attacker receives 5 fixed damage to their HP. This damage cannot be reduced by any effect since it is fixed. If the declared attack misses, the user does not receive any damage. When attacking multiple characters at the same time, the damage is increased by +5 for one of the characters at random. The target selection is done before determining the damage.
combatFeatEffect.card-reduction: If an Evocation requires a variable number of Material Cards to use, it now requires one less, to a minimum of one (i.e., an Evocation cannot use 0 Material Cards). If the Alchemist wishes to increase the number of targets of that Evocation, first reduce the number of Material Cards needed via this Combat Feat, then multiply by the number of intended targets.
combatFeatEffect.cheat-cast-ii: Same as [Cheat Cast I], but the bonus to the Success Value is +3.
combatFeatEffect.shield-bash-i: The equipped shield is treated as a weapon. The shield that becomes a weapon by this Combat Feat has the following data and is treated as a blunt weapon: Accuracy +2, Power equal to the shield's minimum Strength, unchanged Critical Threshold, no Extra Damage. If the target of this attack is a character with only one bipedal section, it falls prone after taking damage; however, if the character has other modes of movement and is not walking, it does not fall prone, even if it is bipedal. If a shield is used as this weapon in a melee attack, the shield's Defense and Evasion bonuses are not applied, and the shield is not considered armor, though any negative effects, such as reduced Evasion, still apply. If a shield with its own weapon data is used to attack with this Combat Feat, the attack uses the weapon data specified by the feat, not the shield's own.
combatFeatEffect.shield-bash-ii: As in [Shield Bash I], if a character is hit by a shield attack and has only one section, it can be made to fall prone, regardless of its movement method or the number of legs it has. Also, the shield's Defense and Evasion modifiers remain effective and can be used.
combatFeatEffect.shadow-step-i: The user stands for a moment on the battlefield, taking advantage of their position to attack or evade. When this Combat Feat is declared, the player chooses one of two effects; once declared, the effect cannot be changed until the next turn. Effect 1: if the user fails an Evasion check or any skill check based on Evasion, they may discard the result once and reroll the check with the same Standard Value; this effect lasts until the user fails such a check once, after which it is lost. Effect 2: declared when making a melee attack and effective for one attack, it increases the damage of the user's melee attack by +2 points, but only while the number of characters (sections) on the user's side in their skirmish area exceeds that of the opposing side; a character with [Block] is treated as having twice its number of sections for this comparison.
combatFeatEffect.shadow-step-ii: The same as [Shadow Step I]. However, if the user selects Effect 1 and rerolls the check, they receive a +1 bonus to the check. If Effect 2 is chosen instead, the additional damage increases by +2 (+4 total).
combatFeatEffect.desperate-strike-ii: The effect is the same as [Desperate Strike I], but it deals +5 more damage (+10 total) and 5 more fixed damage to the user's own HP (10 total).
combatFeatEffect.desperate-strike-iii: The effect is the same as [Desperate Strike II], but it deals +20 more damage (+30 total) and 20 more fixed damage to the user's own HP (30 total).
combatFeatEffect.herald-strike: The user assumes an attack stance and displays their weapon to lower-ranked opponents, breaking their balance and exposing their vital points. Upon declaring a melee or ranged attack, the Accuracy check is fixed at "5" without rolling dice. If the attack hits with this fixed roll and the power table roll is 3-11, it is treated as "+1"; double 1s and double 6s work as usual, with double 1s still causing no damage. This bonus applies to critical rolls as well. Effects that change or manipulate rolls do not affect the Accuracy check while this feat is declared. When attacking multiple targets at once, the fixed "5" Accuracy applies to all of them, and the +1 power table bonus is applied to one hit target chosen before damage is determined. [Herald Strike]'s power table bonus does not stack with other feats (such as [Lethal Strike I]) that increase the power table roll against the same target.
combatFeatEffect.wild-strike-i: Wielding a one-handed weapon, the user attacks multiple enemies around them. This feat must be declared when making a melee attack, is valid for one attack, and can only be declared with a "Stance: 1H" weapon or equivalent. The user selects up to three characters within reach of a melee weapon and attacks all of them with a single Accuracy check, which takes a -2 penalty; damage is determined individually for each character hit. This feat can be declared only once per round, even if the user has mastered [Ever-Changing I].
combatFeatEffect.wild-strike-ii: The same as [Wild Strike I], but the penalty to the Accuracy check is removed.
combatFeatEffect.plunder: When the attacker successfully frightens their opponent, the user can loot the opponent's pocket or a part of their body. This feat can only be declared when making a melee attack with a "Stance: 1H" weapon or equivalent, and is valid for one attack. If that attack results in a critical hit, the damage process is completed without the extra power table damage a critical would normally add; once damage is applied, a Loot Determination is performed automatically on the target, yielding not an "Always" loot but a "(Monster's Name)'s Precious Thing" of equal value, which cannot become a crude material card and can only be sold. If the target has no loot (such as a fairy), the critical process is still interrupted but nothing is gained. This effect triggers only once per round for the same target, even if nothing was gained; if the attack misses or is not a critical, the feat can be declared again next turn. A character affected this way can still be looted normally afterward. This feat is exempt from the limit on active combat feat declarations and can be declared alongside any other active combat feat, but only once per round.
combatFeatEffect.crude-take: The master uses their experience to search for items and loot. During the Loot Determination at the end of combat, the master rolls "1d multiplied by 2" instead of 2d to acquire loot; any effects that modify the roll are applied after doubling the 1d result.
combatFeatEffect.quick-cast: Mana consumption can be reduced by simplifying the process when casting a spell. Declared just before casting a spell, this feat halves the MP cost (rounded up) of the spell being cast. It only works for spells with "Resistance: Neg." Even if the Spellcasting check fails automatically, the MP consumption is still halved.
combatFeatEffect.cleansing-dance: When the master is targeted by an effect with "Area: Shot" and "Target: 1 Character", "Area: Line", or "Area: Breakthrough", they may substitute an Evasion check by the Battle Dancer to reduce or negate the effect (this mainly applies where a resistance check would otherwise be made). If the Evasion check succeeds, the result is the same as a successful resistance check would be. This feat cannot be used against "Area: Target" or "Area: Shot" effects that cover a large area, and it has no effect against "Resistance: Can't" effects that require no resistance check at all.
combatFeatEffect.grimoire-proficiency-a: Allows the Bibliomancer to equip and use A-rank grimoires. Prerequisite for [Grimoire Proficiency S].
combatFeatEffect.grimoire-proficiency-s: Allows the Bibliomancer to equip and use S-rank grimoires; requires [Grimoire Proficiency A] and Bibliomancer level 5 or higher. Prerequisite for [Grimoire Mastery].
combatFeatEffect.grimoire-mastery: Allows the Bibliomancer to equip and use SS-rank grimoires; requires [Grimoire Proficiency S] and Bibliomancer level 11 or higher.

artEffect.antibody: The user of this Technique strengthens their immune system, driving off poisons and diseases. When rolling a Fortitude or Willpower check for a Poison-type or Disease-type effect, the user gets a +4 bonus to that check.
artEffect.owl-sight: The user's eyes radiate gold, like that of an owl. This allows the user to see through darkness as though it were daylight.
artEffect.gazelle-feet: The user's leg muscles become much more active, like that of a gazelle bouncing away from a predator. This increased reaction time gives the user a +1 bonus to Evasion checks.
artEffect.cat-s-eyes: The user's pupils stretch vertically, allowing them to watch an opponent more carefully. This increased observation gives the user a +1 bonus to Accuracy checks.
artEffect.scale-leggings: Pale scales sprout from the user's body, allowing underwater free movement. The user is no longer affected by movement penalties in the water, can move freely, and does not receive any penalties for being in the water. However, this technique does not allow for breathing while underwater.
artEffect.strong-blood: By keeping a consistent body temperature, the user can stay cool in hot environments and vice versa. When taking any fire or water/ice-type damage, reduce the total damage taken by -5.
artEffect.chic-chick: A small bird's wings sprout from the user's back, aiding them in aerial movement. When making Jump checks, the user receives a +5 bonus for those checks. Additionally, reduce any fall damage the user takes by -20. This technique does not allow the user to fly.
artEffect.dragon-tail: The user grows a long, thick Tail that can be used as a Wrestling weapon. If the user already has a tail, then they can use this technique to increase their Accuracy by +1 or their Extra Damage by +2. This Technique's effects are cumulative, to a total of +2 Accuracy and +4 bonus damage. This technique can be used once per round.
artEffect.beetleskin: The user's skin becomes hardened like the shell of a beetle, granting a +2 bonus to Defense.
artEffect.bear-muscle: Revitalizes the user's muscles and reinforces them, giving the user the strength of a bear. This increases the user's strength modifier by +2 but does not affect the user's strength score.
artEffect.meditation: The user stabilizes their thoughts and strengthens their ego, making their mind less susceptible to ill effects. If the user makes a Willpower check against a Psychic-type effect, they receive a +4 bonus to that check.
artEffect.rabbit-ears: The user can more accurately detect incoming danger by making their ears bigger and more flexible. The user gains a +2 bonus to Listen and Danger Sense checks.
artEffect.centaur-legs: The muscles in the user's lower body stiffen and thicken, becoming incredibly powerful. The agility of the user is increased by +6. Fixed-value characters gain +1 to Initiative and Evasion. The GM is free to make other modifications at its discretion.
artEffect.animal-shape: The user transforms into an animal common in society, such as a horse, pig, cat, or dog. The user cannot transform while wearing weapons, armor, or costumes. After the transformation, the user's ability scores remain the same. The user can still speak and use skills but cannot hold items or weapons nor wear armor or clothing, and can only attack with Punch. This Technique does not allow the user to communicate with animals.
artEffect.giant-arms: The user's arms swell immensely, barely able to contain the newfound power inside. The user increases their Strength score by +12. For fixed-value characters, instead, they gain +2 bonus damage. The GM is free to make other modifications at its discretion.
artEffect.sphinx-knowledge: The user becomes as intelligent as a sphinx. The user's Intelligence is increased by +6. Instead, fixed-value characters gain +1 to Magic Power or another value that the GM determines to be based on Intelligence.
artEffect.daemonfinger: The user's hands become incredibly flexible and supple like a daemon. The user increases their Dexterity score by +6. For fixed-value characters, instead, their Accuracy increases by +1. The GM is free to make other modifications at its discretion.
artEffect.fire-breath: During the effect's duration, it is possible to attack by spitting fire with a Major Action. The same check as the Spellcasting check is performed with "Enhancer class level + Intelligence modifier" as the Standard Value. This fire has "Range/Area: 1(10m)/Shot", "Target: 1 area (3m Radius)/5", "Resistance: Half", and deals "Power 10 + Enhancer class level + Intelligence modifier" fire magic damage. If the user has the Combat Feats [Magic Convergence] or [Magic Control], they can apply them to this technique. However, the Combat Feat [Metamagic/Area] has no effect.
artEffect.recovery: The user can refresh themselves and recover an amount of HP equal to their Enhancer Level. This technique can be used once per round.
artEffect.wide-wings: An extensive set of eagle-like wings sprouts from the user's back, allowing the user to fly. When flying, the user's movement speed is 10 meters per round. If the user can already fly, this Technique increases the user's movement speed by 20m. This extra movement speed accumulates up to a 30m bonus. This Technique can be used once per round.
artEffect.early-bird: This jaunty melody awakens any sleeping characters. Those asleep naturally wake up without issue, but if a character was put to sleep by some other effect, the Bard's Performance check Success Value needs to exceed the effect's Success Value. While the Bard is playing this Spellsong, characters in the Area of Effect cannot naturally fall asleep. Spells, spellsongs, and other abilities that try to put characters within the Area of Effect to sleep must pass an opposed check against the Bard's Performance check.
artEffect.ambience: This slow, droning melody calms the nerves and makes one unwilling to fight. The target takes a -1 penalty on Accuracy checks.
artEffect.summon-small-animals: This pleasant melody arouses the interest of nearby small animals and calls them to the Bard. The Bard can only call mammals and birds of a size that would fit in both hands cupped together. The spellsong begins to take effect immediately, but the small animals gradually come together, and the assembly is complete after 3 minutes (18 rounds). If these small animals are harmed, the effect ends immediately, and all of the gathered animals flee.
artEffect.summon-fish: This Spellsong must be used near water. It plays a melody that sounds like flowing water, attracting and calling harmless fish nearby. The song begins to take effect immediately, but the fish gradually come together, and the assembly is complete after 3 minutes (18 rounds). If any of these fish are harmed, the effect ends immediately, and all of the gathered fish flee.
artEffect.cacophony: This horrible racket disrupts the concentration of all within it, making it very difficult to cast any magic. Characters receive a -1 penalty for all Spellcasting checks.
artEffect.ballad: This sad, melancholy song brings down the mood of all who hear it. Characters receive a -1 penalty to their Evasion.
artEffect.morale: A heroic tune that inspires courage in all who hear it. Characters affected by the Spellsong receive a +1 bonus to their Accuracy.
artEffect.requiem: A mournful melody to remember the dead, this Spellsong only works on Undead monsters. Affected Undead receive a -2 penalty for all actions and checks.
artEffect.resistance: This repetitive sonata toughens the listener's body and mind, allowing them to shrug off ill effects. Characters affected by this Spellsong receive a +1 bonus for their Fortitude and Willpower checks.
artEffect.elements: This irregular rhythm calls on elemental faeries for aid. When playing this Spellsong, the Bard specifies one of the following types: Fire, Water/Ice, Earth, Wind, or Lightning. All physical and magical damage of the chosen type is increased by +2.
artEffect.curiosity: The Bard sings and plays a song that evokes strong curiosity. If the Bard is not visible to the target, the target cannot control its desire to see the Bard and tries to move to an arbitrary position (area or coordinate) where it can see the Bard. If the target cannot reach a visible place, the target moves as close as possible. If the Bard is already visible, this spellsong has no effect.
artEffect.charming: The target is mesmerized by the Bard's singing and cannot bring themselves to harm the Bard. In Contested Checks where the Bard is on the passive side, the Bard automatically gets a favorable result.
artEffect.trance: This is a clear melody that sharpens the mind of the listener. Those affected by this Spellsong gain a +1 bonus modifier to Spellcasting Checks.
artEffect.nostalgia: A wistful tune, this Spellsong invokes feelings of days long past in the hearts of its listeners, causing them to wish to go back home. If in combat, those affected by the Spellsong attempt to retreat from the battlefield and escape. This Spellsong has no effect if the listener is already at home or is unable to escape. Once affected, listeners will be under the effects of this Spellsong for 1 hour. After 1 hour, or if the listener manages to return home, the Spellsong's effect ends.
artEffect.break: The melody is jarring and distracts the listener's concentration. The target receives a -1 penalty to Fortitude and Willpower Checks.
artEffect.love-song: This buoyant ballad stimulates romance, causing "love to be in the air." Affected listeners will look to be with the closest partner of their choice, with current lovers/spouses taking precedence over random people. If current partners are not nearby, the closest available partner for the listener's orientation will be subject to these magically enhanced feelings, regardless of race. If no applicable partners are within the area of effect, the Spellsong has no effect. Those with budding romantic feelings will attempt to see if the partner reciprocates these feelings, while current partners will attempt to retire to act on these feelings. The effects of this Spellsong last 1 hour, even if the Bard stops performing.
artEffect.lullaby: An inviting melody that gently lulls listeners into a state of drowsiness. The subjects are dizzy and unable to move or take any active action. If forced to make an Action Check, the target takes a -4 penalty. The Duration of this Spellsong is 10 seconds (1 round), as usual. After that time, the drowsiness automatically disappears.
artEffect.clap: Anyone hearing the Bard's rhythmic clapping has the urge to clap along. The Spellsong causes all weapons, shields, and items held or equipped in hand by targets to drop to the ground when the effect is activated. They can use only weapon attacks with non-hand weapons such as Kicks, Tails, Bites, and so on. They also cannot use Stance items.
artEffect.chorus: The target sings with the Bard. The target can only perform Limited Move as a type of movement and cannot cast spells that require vocalization, give commands or instructions to golems, or say a password.
artEffect.dare: The melody is so jarring that it makes targets lose their ability to make calm decisions. The target will no longer be able to declare any active combat feats or unique skills that use them.
artEffect.dance: The target receives a -2 penalty on Accuracy and Evasion checks. However, the target does not receive this penalty if these checks are performed using the Grappler class.
artEffect.fall: If still in the air at the time of the effect, the target will be forced to fall to the ground; see "Forced Fall Effect" for the treatment of falling. While under the effect, the target cannot fly again. [Sword's Grace/Wings Of The Wind] cannot be used, and the [Flying] unique skill is lost. A character whose movement method is only airborne, such as "Flying" or "Floating," cannot move.
artEffect.reduction: A peaceful tune, this Spellsong reduces MP consumption of spells within range by -1 (but cannot reduce it to 0 or lower). While using [Metamagic/**] combat feats, the cost is reduced before the use of Metamagic. This spell doesn't affect any MP consumption except spells, like techniques or items that require MP.
artEffect.lazy: The target's actions are interfered with by a melody that causes fatigue. The target takes a -1 penalty to all Skill Checks.
artEffect.spring-breeze: Deals "Power 10 + Bardic Power" magic damage to 1 target character.
artEffect.summer-vitality: Restores one target character's HP by "Power 20 + Bardic Power" points. The effect of [Finale: Summer Vitality] can only be received once per hour per target. Also, Undead, Magitech, and Constructs cannot be affected by this Finale.
artEffect.autumn-harvest: Restores one target character's MP by "Power 0 + Bardic Power" points. The effect of [Finale: Autumn Harvest] can only be received once per target per day. Also, Undead, Magitech, and Constructs cannot be affected by this Finale.
artEffect.winter-s-chill: One target character is dealt "Power 10 + Bardic Power" magic damage.
artEffect.beast-s-roar: Up to 3 target characters are dealt "Power 20 + Bardic Power" magic damage.
artEffect.breath-of-the-meadows: It restores the HP of up to 3 target characters by "Power 30 + Bardic Power" points. The effect of [Finale: Breath of the Meadows] can only be received once per hour per target. Also, Undead, Magitech, and Constructs cannot be affected by this Finale.
artEffect.banquet-of-flowers: The MP of up to 3 target characters will be restored by "Power 10 + Bardic Power" points. The effect of [Finale: Banquet of Flowers] can be received only once per target per day. Also, Undead, Magitech, and Constructs cannot be affected by this Finale.
artEffect.screaming-snake-pit-symphony: Up to 3 target characters are dealt "Power 20 + Bardic Power" magic damage.
artEffect.dance-of-the-fire-dragon: Up to 5 target characters are dealt "Power 30 + Bardic Power" magic damage.
artEffect.roar-of-the-water-dragon: Up to 5 target characters are dealt "Power 30 + Bardic Power" magic damage.
artEffect.blue-moon-light: The MP of up to 5 target characters will be restored by "Power 20 + Bardic Power". The effect of [Finale: Blue Moon Light] can be received only once per target per day. This effect does not affect Undead, Construct, and Magitech characters.
artEffect.bright-sunshine: The HP of up to 5 target characters will be restored by "Power 40 + Bardic Power". The effect of [Finale: Bright Sunshine] can be received only once per target per day. This effect does not affect Undead, Construct, and Magitech characters.

schoolSecretEffect.angry-bear-strike: With a mighty roar, the user drives forward and puts their entire upper body strength into the strike. If the attack hits, add +6 to your melee damage. Additionally, the target is staggered and, for 10 seconds (1 round), suffers a -1 penalty to its Accuracy. This effect is treated as a Psychic type (weak), with its Resistance being 'Can't'. When compared to the Success Value of the effect for the purpose of removing with magic, it is treated as a Success Value of 0. To use this Secret, you must be able to vocalize — the language spoken is irrelevant. When you declare this Secret, you receive a -2 penalty to your Evasion check. [Taunting Strike I] is a prerequisite for learning this Secret, though the Secret itself does not also carry the effect of [Taunting Strike]. However, if the user is able to declare multiple Combat Feats, it is possible to simultaneously declare both this Secret and [Taunting Strike] (or any of its variants).
schoolSecretEffect.enraged-bear-strike: An evolved version of [Angry Bear Strike], releasing an even more terrifying roar and launching a ferocious attack. Like its predecessor, if you are not able to speak, this Secret cannot be used. Its effects are identical to [Angry Bear Strike], but instead, add +15 to your melee damage. The risk and stun effects are unchanged, and the same usage ruling applies for [Taunting Strike].
schoolSecretEffect.furious-bear-strike: The ultimate form of the school's Secret. The user lets out a roar that can shake mountains and lets loose an attack that can shatter the earth. Like the other Secrets, it cannot be used if you cannot speak and has the same effects (stagger et al.), except the bonus melee damage is +24.
schoolSecretEffect.disperse: By relaxing and controlling breath rhythm at the moment of impact, this technique 'scatters' the damage inflicted, reducing any physical or magical damage inflicted during the duration of the Secret's use by -2 points. However, as the user's attention is entirely focused on this, all other actions become neglected. All Skill Checks except Evasion, Fortitude and Willpower or Death Checks suffer a -4 penalty. Like [Defensive Stance], it must be declared before any Skill Check is performed, and the type of Movement the user is able to perform is limited to Limited Move or Normal Move.
schoolSecretEffect.disrupt: An offensive strike that focuses on disrupting the opponent's stance and controlling their movement. The Secret user provokes the enemy's attack and prepares their guard to receive it. An attack with this Secret is reduced by -4 points, and the target is provoked for 10 seconds (1 round) or until the user's next Evasion check against the target. While provoked, the target's next attack must be against the Secret user with a melee attack or similar ability (such as Range: Touch). If they can make multiple simultaneous attacks, they must also attack the Secret user. On a successful Evasion check against this target, the damage is instead reduced by -4 points and any Combat Feat or Secret with the effect of '1 melee attack' is not applied. On a failed Evasion check, the enemy's damage is not reduced and any declared Combat Feats or Secrets are applied as normal. The target of this Secret is provoked regardless of their intelligence but are not required to make any attacks on their turn. If the target is able to make multiple attacks (with a choice of targets) on their turn, they are not required to attack the Secret user again.
schoolSecretEffect.disengage: With flowing movements, the user slips through a dangerous skirmish. This Secret has the same effect as Prepare to Withdraw (see CR I, p. 139). However, when using this Secret, the user does not suffer the -4 penalty to the Evasion Check normally associated with that action.
schoolSecretEffect.iron-fist-dull-shine: The Wrestling-type weapon Iron Sand Fist can be equipped. Additionally, the Iron Sand Steel Fist weapon can be equipped by learning [Weapon Proficiency A/Wrestling], and the Iron Sand Adamantine Fist weapon can be equipped by learning [Weapon Proficiency S/Wrestling].
schoolSecretEffect.iron-sand-reverberating-fist: As a Major Action, perform a melee attack with any Iron Sand Fist weapon. If this attack hits, the character's Grappler class level is added to the damage dealt. Attacks using this Secret do not trigger [Chain Attack], and even if the fighter possesses the [Dual Wielding] feat, only one attack may be made. Furthermore, this Secret cannot be used in the same turn in which the [Flying Kick] feat is performed, nor can you declare the use of [Multi-Attack], [Wild Strike], or any feat that increases the number of targets in the attack or allow you to perform additional attacks. It is, however, possible to declare this Secret in conjunction with 'Appl.: 1 melee attack' applicable feats that do not fall into the above restrictions. This Secret is incompatible with any other Major Action. If you can perform multiple Major Actions in your turn, you can perform all of them as this Secret, but you cannot perform this Secret and any other Major Action in the same turn.
