When using this Secret, the character must be standing on the ground with their feet and cannot be Flying, Floating, Mounted, Prone, etc.
schoolSecretEffect.one-strike-absolute-defeat-iron-sand-dem: This Secret can only be declared when attacking with an [Iron Sand Reverberating Fist]. Attacks utilizing this Secret cannot cause criticals. If the attack hits, it "destroys" the target's armor, reducing their Defense. Damage is calculated and applied using this reduced total. The Defense value is decreased as follows below: In all cases, the effect is cumulative, with the minimum value being 1 or 2 points. If the target is a PC character: Amongst the armor (armor, shield, accessories) worn by the target, the one with the highest Defense currently is selected, and the value is reduced by half (rounded up). The damage can be repaired at the cost of 10% of the item value per point (up to the maximum of 90% total value). Additionally, one day's time is required for each point of Defense to be restored. For example, an 'Imperial' with a base cost of 100,000G suffers 13 points of damage, it will require 90,000G and 13 days to repair. If the target is a monster: The target's Defense is reduced by two thirds (rounded up). Lost Defense points are automatically restored at the rate of one point a day.
schoolSecretEffect.leaping-vine-entanglement-grapevine-hold: This Secret must be used in a situation where the Secret user can use the 'Throw' action, but the Secret itself is not a throw. Weapons and Accessories that enhance Throws still grant Accuracy bonus. However, since the Secret is a non-damaging attack, any change in Power is considered irrelevant. This Secret has Target: 1 Character as its effect, regardless of whether or not the Secret user has mastered [Improved Throw] or not. A multi-section character can be targeted as if it were a single character regardless of the number of sections it possesses. With this Secret, the user leaps at the opponent, entangling and binding its entire body. This prevents movement and exposes weak points in the target's defenses. If the attack is successful, no damage is inflicted, but for 1 round (10 seconds) until the beginning of the Secret user's next turn, both the target's Evasion and Defense receive a -2 penalty (minimum 0). Success with this attack does not grant an additional kick attack via [Stomp], as another Secret exists within the school that is dedicated to granting an additional attack in tandem with this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.entwining-vine-gap-strike-abrupt-slap: The user strikes a victim entangled by [Leaping Vine Entanglement] with a small, short punch. The user of this Secret can make a single Punch attack against the character (or a section of a character) that has been hit with [Leaping Vine Entanglement].
schoolSecretEffect.thunderclap-spinning-lariat-warthunder: Like the Combat Feat [Flying Kick], this Secret allows the user to make an attack immediately after moving, though in this case it is a spinning fist strike rather than a leaping kick. When attacking with this Secret, 'Kick' attacks from the Flying Kick Feat cannot be made, and vice versa. The user moves normally, and immediately after moving 1 area (Simple Combat) or 10m or more (Standard or Advanced Combat), the user may attack up to two targets with a 'Punch'. This attack does not trigger the [Chain Attack] feat. After this, Major Actions can be performed normally.
schoolSecretEffect.parry-and-break: This Secret can only be declared while holding a shield with the Flex Grip enhancement. Holding the shield in front of them and meeting the opponent's strike with a forceful sweeping motion, the user attempts to disrupt the enemy's stance and push them off balance. If the Secret user is the subject of a melee attack during the Secret's active time, the result of the Evasion check affects the attacker. This only occurs on the first melee attack received by the Secret user and does not apply to any additional attacks. If the Success Value of the Secret User's Evasion check is equal to or greater than the Attacker's roll, the attack not only fails, but the attacker is forced off balance, and the attacker receives a penalty to their Evasion check until their next turn. This is normally a -1 penalty, but should the Success Value of the Evasion check be 4 or greater than the attacker's Accuracy Check, the penalty to the attacker's Evasion becomes -2. If the attacker's Accuracy Check is higher than the user's Evasion Check, the Attacker suffers no ill effects. Even if a character can make multiple declarations on one turn, they cannot declare this Secret more than once. In addition, the Secret [Stop and Stagger] cannot be declared at the same time as this Secret, and vice versa.
schoolSecretEffect.stop-and-stagger: This Secret can only be declared while holding a shield with the Flex Grip enhancement. The Secret user holds their shield in front of themselves to deflect the attacker's strike and then shoves, disorienting the attacker and pushing them off balance. [Stop & Stagger] triggers when the user is targeted by a melee attack and makes an Evasion check against it, or when the user suffers damage from a melee attack through the use of the [Cover] feat or a Secret of the same type. Its effect then occurs when the user takes either physical or magical damage from a melee attack. This effect only occurs on the first instance of the user taking melee damage, even if they were to take additional melee attacks. If the amount of damage received by the user is equal to or less than their own Fortitude (Adventurer Level + Vitality modifier), the attacker is thrown off balance and receives a -1 penalty to their Evasion Checks until their next turn. If the applied damage received by the user is 0, the attacker's Evasion Check penalty is -2. If the damage received by the Secret user is greater than their Fortitude, or the user is successful in their Evasion Check, this Secret's effects do not trigger. Even if a character can make multiple Declarations on one turn, they cannot declare this Secret more than once. In addition, the Secret [Parry and Break] cannot be declared at the same time as this Secret, and vice versa.
schoolSecretEffect.planned-riposte: With this Secret, the user strikes at an enemy who has been thrown off balance by one of the other Secrets of the Narzaland Flexible Shield style. Melee attacks made by this Secret user against targets who have been unbalanced by the successful use of either the [Parry & Break] or [Stop & Stagger] Secrets deal +4 Damage. This effect is applied only to the first melee attack made in the turn, and if that attack fails, the bonus will be unavailable for any other attacks that turn. This bonus effect does not require a shield with the Flex Grip enhancement to be used.
schoolSecretEffect.overhead-swing: The user swings their weapon around, using centrifugal force as a counterweight aid. If this Secret is declared, the user may use a weapon with up to 5 points higher Minimum Strength than their own Strength score. However, aiming with precision becomes more difficult as a result, and the Critical Threshold is increased by +1.
schoolSecretEffect.bracing-shot: By placing the stock on the ground and utilizing the legs to support the draw, the user is able to make use of heavy shooting weapons that they would otherwise not be strong enough to fire. If this Secret is declared, the user may use a weapon with up to 10 points higher Minimum Strength than their own Strength score. This makes precision aiming difficult, and as a result, the Critical Threshold of the attack is increased by +2. Additionally, since this Secret places the user in an awkward stance, they suffer a -2 penalty to their Evasion roll.
schoolSecretEffect.sidelong-glance-shot: The user performs a ranged attack against a target while pretending to aim at a second target. To use this Secret, there must be at least two enemies in separate areas (Simplified Combat) or coordinates (Standard/Advanced Combat), and both must be eligible targets for the attack. When this Secret is declared on a ranged attack that targets one of these available targets, the attack gains a +2 bonus to its Accuracy roll. This Secret cannot be declared on an Accuracy check that is subject to the effect of [Snipe].
schoolSecretEffect.sword-magic-resolute-strike: This Secret, like the base feat, allows for the use of melee attacks and spellcasting simultaneously. The melee attack is performed as the initial action, with the spell immediately following it in enhanced form; in this case, the Secret user sets up their movement on the premise that the attack will hit. The declaration of this Secret must always be made at the time the melee attack is performed with the Major Action, and spellcasting occurs immediately after the melee attack is resolved. If the melee attack hits, the user gains a +1 bonus to their Spellcasting check. However, should the attack miss, the user receives a -1 penalty to their check instead.
schoolSecretEffect.sword-magic-flux-strike: This Secret, like the base feat, allows for the use of melee attacks and spellcasting simultaneously. The melee attack is performed as the initial action, with the spell immediately following it in enhanced form; in this case, the Secret user sets up their movement on the premise that the attack will be avoided. The declaration of this Secret must always be made at the time the melee attack is performed with the Major Action, and spellcasting occurs immediately after the melee attack is resolved. If the melee attack is avoided, the user gains a +2 bonus to their Spellcasting check. However, should the attack hit, the user receives a -2 penalty to their check instead.
schoolSecretEffect.sword-of-truth-mystic-surveilling-eye: The user sharpens their mind through the use of magic, allowing them to anticipate the enemy's movements. When this Secret is declared at the time of a melee attack, the Intelligence modifier of the Secret user is added to the Accuracy check. Unlike [Mana Strike], there is no additional increase to damage. However, the risk — a -2 penalty to Fortitude and Willpower checks — is the same as the base feat.
schoolSecretEffect.battlefield-sorcery-annamaria: This Secret allows the user to multiply the number of targets of any spell with 'Target: 1 Character', similar to [Metamagic/Targets]. At the time of use, the MP consumption of the spell is first reduced by -1, and the doubling calculation is performed afterward; this MP reduction is cumulative with other effects provided by other Combat Feats. It is also possible to declare a 'multiplying by x1' and receive the MP reduction while still only affecting a single target. For this Secret to function, all characters targeted by the spell must have Rosellini's Magic Mark placed on their body or equipment — otherwise, the effect is altered to become identical to [Metamagic/Targets].
schoolSecretEffect.battlefield-sorcery-veronica: A caster who has mastered this Secret can choose to delay the activation of any spell with 'Target: 1 Character (including 1 Entire Character)'. The length of the delay can be chosen in 10 second (1 round) increments, up to a maximum of one hour. In order for this Secret to function, the target must have Rosellini's Magic Mark placed on their body or equipment. Any spell affected by this Secret has its Resistance changed to 'Optional'. The spell is automatically activated when the delay time limit set by the caster is reached, triggering the spell's effect; however, it is also possible for the spell's target to trigger its effect (thereby ending the delay) by using a Minor Action or during Combat Preparation. Only one spell per target can be delayed by the use of this Secret — if another delayed-effect spell is used on the target, the first usage is canceled without taking effect. If the user of this Secret possesses the [Metamagic/Time] or [Universal Metamagic] feats, it is possible to multiply the limit of the delay effect by multiplying the MP consumption, in a similar fashion to those feats. However, the delay effect cannot be extended to last beyond 6 AM of the following day.
schoolSecretEffect.battlefield-sorcery-torquato: This Secret is only effective when combined with a spell whose area is '1 Area (XX radius)/Space', '1 Area (XX radius)/YY (Specified maximum number of targets)', or '1 Area (XX radius)/All'. When this Secret is used, the area of any such spell is changed to 'All Areas (30m)/All', and the MP cost of the spell is changed to (base cost of the spell - 1), multiplied by 5. Regardless of the type of resistance of the spells cast with this Secret, however, only those bearing Rosellini's Magic Mark upon their bodies or equipment benefit from its effect — others within the expanded area who do not possess the Magic Mark are unaffected.
schoolSecretEffect.wind-cleaver: For one round after declaring this Secret as a Major Action, the user and their mount gain a +2 bonus to their Evasion checks. This effect is only available if the Jockey is equipped with a melee weapon of Stance: 1H, other than 1HW or 1H#.
schoolSecretEffect.breaking-wave: This Secret allows the mount to declare [Decoy Attack] as part of its attack. Regardless of the number of sections the mount has and the number of attacks it makes, this can be declared only once. If the mount already has the ability to declare [Decoy Attack], treat this as the ability to make one additional declaration of [Decoy Attack].
schoolSecretEffect.shadow-slice: If an attack made by the Jockey declaring this Secret is evaded, a +2 bonus is applied to the mount's next Accuracy check. This effect disappears once the mount makes a single Accuracy check, regardless of whether it succeeds or not. Unlike the base feat, there is no Stance: 2H restriction on the melee weapon equipped by the Jockey in conjunction with this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.umbra-cut: This Secret functions like [Shadow Slice], but if the Jockey's attack successfully hits, it deals an additional +4 damage. If it misses, the mount gains a +2 bonus to its next Accuracy check, just as if [Shadow Slice] had been used.
schoolSecretEffect.flying-piledriver: This Secret allows the user to perform Throw attacks without being limited to bipedal targets. To use it, the character must have wings capable of flight — this includes PCs who are Lildraken or Drakes using [Limited Dragonification], as well as characters under the effect of the Technique [Wide Wings]. This Secret cannot be used by characters who are flying without the use of wings, such as through magical effects. With this Secret, it is possible to use a [Throw] attack on a target that is not bipedal, as long as it is not a multi-section creature. The attack power and Critical Threshold of the Throw are not changed (weapons or effects that enhance the Throw, if any, will still apply). This Secret is redundant with the Combat Feat [Improved Throw].
schoolSecretEffect.rolling-tail-sweep: The user attacks up to 3 characters in the same Skirmish area with their Tail at the same time. This attack suffers a -1 penalty to the Accuracy Check and a -4 penalty to Total Damage, but causes the characters it hits to fall prone. Multi-section characters and non-bipedal characters cannot be knocked prone with this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.grand-rolling-tail-sweep: The user attacks up to 5 characters in the same Skirmish area with their Tail at the same time. This attack suffers a -4 penalty to Total Damage, but causes the characters it hits to fall prone. This effect does not depend on the target's number of legs — a character with 2 sections can be knocked prone if both sections are hit. Multi-section characters with 3 or more sections, or flying characters, cannot be knocked prone with this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.se-ilite-borne-en-migo-invisibile-unseen: When declaring this Secret, the Secret user gains a +1 bonus to Evasion checks. The attack made in this case has the same effect as [Taunting Strike], though it does not deal any damage even if it hits. The provocation effect and the Evasion check bonus that the Secret user gains last for 10 seconds (1 round). This Secret does not provoke a character whose intellect is over 18 or a monster whose intellect is "High." The Evasion modifier given by this Secret is not cumulative among the Secrets of this School (regardless of whether they are similar or not).

The attack made in this case has the same effect as [Taunting Strike], though it does not deal any damage even if it hits. The provocation effect and the Evasion check bonus that the Secret user gains last for 10 seconds (1 round). Unlike the base Secret, the Superior tier has the same effect as the Basic Feat [Taunting Strike II]: it extends to characters whose intellect is over 18 and monsters whose intellect is "High," though those targets are not compelled to attack the Secret user and instead only suffer that Basic Feat's penalty. The Evasion modifier given by this Secret is not cumulative among the Secrets of this School (regardless of whether they are similar or not).
schoolSecretEffect.tenel-miedo-en-un-entrada-sword-of-damoc: The Secret user gains a +1 bonus to Evasion for the next 10 seconds (1 round). If the declared attack hits, the damage roll on the Power Table is increased by +1 if the roll is 3-11 (double 1s and double 6s work as usual). Use of this Secret imposes a -2 penalty to the Accuracy check. The Evasion modifier given by this Secret is not cumulative among the Secrets of this School (regardless of whether they are similar or not).

schoolSecretEffect.ser-confundido-conjunto-bonito-baile: For all Evasion checks made by the user of this Secret before their next turn, the required roll for automatic success is changed from "12" to "10" or greater. These rolls must be obtained as straight 2d rolls before any modifiers are applied; effects that change or reroll the dice themselves are still in effect — for example, if [Sword's Grace/Change Fate] is used, this Secret's threshold is checked after the dice are flipped, and the +1/+2 bonus from the Level 6/11 enhanced version of that ability is not factored in. If the user declares this Secret, they may also attempt an Evasion check against spells or effects that deal or include physical damage and carry "Resistance: Can't" — such a check succeeds only on an automatic success, and the conditions above still apply, potentially nullifying the spell or effect entirely.
schoolSecretEffect.ser-confundido-conjunto-bonito-baile-sup: For all Evasion checks made by the user of this Secret before their next turn, the required roll for automatic success is changed from "12" to "9" or greater. These rolls must be obtained as straight 2d rolls before any modifiers are applied; effects that change or reroll the dice themselves are still in effect — for example, if [Sword's Grace/Change Fate] is used, this Secret's threshold is checked after the dice are flipped, and the +1/+2 bonus from the Level 6/11 enhanced version of that ability is not factored in. If the user declares this Secret, they may also attempt an Evasion check against spells or effects that deal or include physical damage and carry "Resistance: Can't" — such a check succeeds only on an automatic success, and the conditions above still apply, potentially nullifying the spell or effect entirely.
schoolSecretEffect.ser-confundido-conjunto-bonito-baile-ult: For all Evasion checks made by the user of this Secret before their next turn, the required roll for automatic success is changed from "12" to "7" or greater. These rolls must be obtained as straight 2d rolls before any modifiers are applied; effects that change or reroll the dice themselves are still in effect — for example, if [Sword's Grace/Change Fate] is used, this Secret's threshold is checked after the dice are flipped, and the +1/+2 bonus from the Level 6/11 enhanced version of that ability is not factored in. If the user declares this Secret, they may also attempt an Evasion check against spells or effects that deal or include physical damage and carry "Resistance: Can't" — such a check succeeds only on an automatic success, and the conditions above still apply, potentially nullifying the spell or effect entirely. Additionally, this effect is applied only when the Evasion Check is made using the Fencer or Battle Dancer Class.
schoolSecretEffect.turbulent-winds-double-handed-cut: This Secret has no effect unless the user has learned one or more of the following Active Combat Feats: [Decoy Attack], [Aimed Attack I/II/III], [Power Strike I/II], [Taunting Strike I/II], [Lethal Strike I/II/III], and [Mana Strike]. It can only be declared when the left and right hand each perform a melee attack through the effect of [Dual Wielding]. When declaring this Secret, the user chooses 2 different Active Combat Feats they have already mastered; the weapon in the left hand and the weapon in the right hand each apply one of these Feats, unique from the other hand. Which weapon receives which Combat Feat must be declared before making Accuracy checks, and the declaration must satisfy the "Use" condition of each Combat Feat. If the Combat Feats carry risks, those risks are cumulative. The GM may rule that Secrets from other Schools linked to the above Combat Feats can also be declared with this Secret, though it is recommended not to allow special Feats whose Application has been changed from the Basic Feat, or that have an effect significantly different from the Basic Feat. Even if multiple declarations are possible through the use of [Ever-Changing], the same Basic Feat cannot be declared for both the right hand and the left hand in a single attack with this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.adverse-wind-offsetting-sacrifice: Stand bravely before your enemy. When declaring this Secret, the user chooses 1 character (1 section) as a target. When making two attacks against this target with [Dual Wielding], the Secret user gains a +2 bonus on both Accuracy checks. However, if the target character (section) makes a melee attack, ranged attack, or unique skill against the Secret user that is "Negated" by an Evasion check, that attack automatically hits without an Accuracy check being rolled — this automatic hit is treated as the risk of this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.foreboding-wind-crouching-tiger-hidden-d: After using this Secret, for 10 seconds (1 round) the user is able to perform the same check as the Combat Feat [Counter] whenever they are attacked by a melee attack, but rolls an Accuracy check for each weapon in hand. If both of the user's Accuracy checks exceed the Success Value of the opponent's Accuracy check, the user makes a damage check for both weapons and the opponent's attack is treated as a failure. If only one of the user's Accuracy checks exceeds the opponent's Success Value, damage is determined only for the weapon that succeeded and applied to the opponent; at the same time, the opponent's attack is considered to hit, and the Secret user also suffers the normally determined damage. If neither of the user's Accuracy checks exceeds the opponent's Success Value, then — as with a failed [Counter] — the opponent's attack hits, and the first 2d roll for the damage determination is treated as an automatic "12," with the Secret user receiving the resulting damage. This Secret can be used only once per turn, even if the user is able to take multiple Major Actions. Furthermore, the user cannot declare, together with this Secret, unique skills or Secrets of a declared type whose Application is limited to a single melee attack.
schoolSecretEffect.first-darkness-heart-piercer: Unlike its Basic Feat, this Secret can only be declared during a Ranged Attack. The user fires an arrow from as close a range as possible to ensure a hit on a vital location. If the attack is successful, the result on the Power Table is increased by +1 (if the roll is 3-11). Additionally, if the attacked target is within the same Skirmish area as the Secret user, the Critical Threshold of the attack is reduced by -1 (minimum 8). Use of this Secret reduces the range of the attack to "1" if using Simplified Combat, or to half the original range (original range / 2m, rounded down) in Standard or Advanced Combat.
schoolSecretEffect.second-darkness-doomed-life: The user attacks the blind spot of a target engaged in melee. The target of this Bow attack must be a character who is in a melee situation. The Secret user gains a +1 bonus to the Accuracy check, and the Critical Threshold of the attack is reduced by -1 (minimum 8). Using this Secret reduces the range of the attack to "1" if using Simplified Combat, or to half the original range (original range / 2m, rounded down) in Standard or Advanced Combat.
schoolSecretEffect.extra-darkness-three-headed-water-dragon: This Secret was created to allow escape from a situation where one is surrounded by Barbarous. At close range, the user quickly nocks three arrows onto the bow simultaneously and fires them at different enemies. When using this Secret, the user can attack up to three targets in the same Skirmish area simultaneously, though the Accuracy check suffers a -2 penalty. Using this Secret consumes 3 arrows at once, and if a special arrow is used, all three arrows fired must be of the same type.
schoolSecretEffect.killing-strike-roaring-thunder: This Secret adds a +4 to physical or magical damage inflicted by the user's melee attacks. Each time an attack using this Secret successfully hits, the Secret user suffers 4 fixed damage; this damage can be reduced by equipping a Wald Gauntlet. Attacks using this Secret are treated as if they were made with a blunt weapon.
schoolSecretEffect.killing-strike-thunderous-upheaval: This Secret adds a +12 to physical and magical damage inflicted by the user's melee attacks. Each time an attack using this Secret successfully hits, the Secret user suffers 6 fixed damage; this damage can be reduced by equipping a Wald Gauntlet. Attacks using this Secret are treated as if they were made with a blunt weapon.
schoolSecretEffect.killing-strike-flash-of-lightning: Just as with the Basic Feat, the damage roll on any successful attack is increased by +1 if the roll is 3-11; double 1s and double 6s work as is. Each time an attack using this Secret successfully hits, the Secret user suffers 4 fixed damage; this damage can be reduced by equipping a Wald Gauntlet. Attacks using this Secret are treated as if they were made with a blunt weapon.
schoolSecretEffect.giant-beast-hammer: This Secret can be declared when attacking a target with multiple Sections using Throw, and it affects how damage is dealt. When the attack hits, damage is rolled once for each Section of the target. Afterward, the Secret user may determine which individual damage rolls apply to which specific Sections of the target as they see fit — each part and damage roll will be in one-to-one correspondence. If the user is able to declare multiple Combat Feats and uses this Secret at the same time as a Feat that states "When multiple attacks occur at one time, only one enemy will receive the effect," such as [Power Strike], [Lethal Strike], or [Armor Piercer], the effect will only apply to a single damage check; only then is damage allocated to different Sections.
schoolSecretEffect.cataclysmic-beast-toss: The Secret user's Throw can hit another character (Section) in the same skirmish area, and the Accuracy check for this attack is only rolled once. The target can choose whether the Evasion check is made by themselves or by the other character (Section) at whom they are being thrown. This Secret can only be used if the user is able to attack both targets with a Melee attack. If the Secret user has learned [Improved Throw I], only single-Section characters can be thrown with this Secret (regardless of the number of legs or the method of movement); if the user has learned [Improved Throw II], they may throw up to two Sections, but the attack will still only target one character (Section) at whom the first is thrown, and the target being thrown can choose which of the three Sections will make the Evasion check. Damage is determined separately for the character being thrown and for the secondary target: the thrown character is knocked Prone, while the secondary target is only knocked Prone if it is a one-Section character. If the user has learned [Stomp], they may immediately make a follow-up attack on any target knocked Prone by this Secret.
schoolSecretEffect.furious-charging-beast-slayer: By declaring this Secret, the user is able to attempt the use of [Counter] with [Throw] against attacks from multi-Section characters until the start of their next turn; the maximum number of Sections that can be targeted is limited by the Secret user's level of [Improved Throw] (2 Sections for [Improved Throw I], 3 for [Improved Throw II]). At the time of the attack, the Secret user performs an Accuracy check using [Throw]; if it succeeds, the attack knocks the opponent Prone and deals damage to each Section, and the opponent may not get up from Prone until the start of their next turn. Just as with [Counter], the user may choose whether to take this action after learning the Success Value of the opponent's Accuracy check — thus, if a character with two Sections attacks twice, it is possible to make a normal Evasion check against the first attack and use [Throw] against the second. If this Secret's [Counter] fails and the target has the capability to execute melee attacks and is at 1 HP or more (or is acting under the effects of [Indomitable] or similar), the user receives damage from all of the target's Sections as if the result of the damage roll were 12; additionally, if the user forfeited the [Counter] against the original attack and then also failed the Evasion check, they receive damage from both the failed Evasion and the failed [Counter]. Even after declaring the use of this Secret, the user may still use the [Counter] feat normally; however, once they have made a counterattack, they cannot use [Counter] again in any form until their next turn.
schoolSecretEffect.unbreakable-defensive-stance: This Secret must be declared before any Actions are taken on the user's turn. Using this Secret increases the user's Defense by +4. As a risk, all skill checks other than Fortitude, Willpower, Evasion, and Death Checks suffer a -4 penalty. Use of this Secret limits the user to a Normal or Limited Move; if the user declares the Secret before moving, they cannot make a Full Move.
schoolSecretEffect.indomitable-will: This Secret cannot be used unless the user is wielding one of the Shields from this school's equipment. When this Secret is used, its effect is the same as [Cover]. However, when the applied damage the user receives becomes 0, the effect of [Cover] is not lost and continues for as long as the applied damage to the Secret user is 0. If the Secret user possesses the [Guardian] feat and uses it to [Cover] multiple targets, this Secret is in effect until the user takes 1 or more applied damage — for example, if the Secret user has declared 3 targets for [Cover], each of the targets is individually protected by the user's [Cover] until the user receives 1 or more applied damage.
schoolSecretEffect.greater-indomitable-will: This Secret cannot be used unless the user is wielding one of the Shields from this school's equipment. When used, its effect is the same as [Cover]. schoolSecretEffect.preparing-for-fearless-offense-and-defen: This Secret is declared when performing a melee attack or a Spellcasting check as a Major Action, allowing the user to immediately make a melee attack and then cast a spell, or vice versa. When using this Secret multiple times on one turn, the bonuses cannot be combined to gain a +4 bonus to Willpower or Fortitude — they can only be applied to different checks. However, the penalties can be combined to receive a cumulative -2 penalty on Accuracy or Spellcasting.

workSkillDescription.witch-doctor-skill: The "Witch Doctor skill (Medicine Man)" is a skill for dispelling misfortunes, including diseases, through spells and folk remedies. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called "Medicine Men". Medicine Men are not often seen in urban areas with temples and are not relied upon much. Medicine Men are primarily sought after in small settlements where there are no priests.
workSkillDescription.waiter-waitress-skill: The "Waiter/Waitress skill (Table Service)" is a work skill for providing customer service, such as serving food and drinks at dining establishments, dinner parties, tea parties, and similar events. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly referred to as "Table Service." The basic duties of Table Service include taking food and drink orders from customers, relaying the orders to the chef in the kitchen, serving the prepared food and drinks to the customers' tables, and clearing dishes and tables after the customers finish their meals. They often also handle the bill when customers leave the establishment. In small-scale dining establishments with only 1-2 chefs, Table Service may also be responsible for washing dishes and cleaning. In the food service industry of the world of Raxia, there are many situations where menus listing food and drink options and prices are not provided. In such cases, Table Service needs to listen to individual customers' preferences and requests to recommend appropriate dishes and alcoholic beverages. It's worth noting that dining establishments large enough to require Table Service can only be sustained in settlements with a certain minimum population. Therefore, Table Service is a work skill that is primarily utilized in urban areas. Table Service positions are often favored by single individuals and those looking to reduce living expenses, as dining establishments frequently provide 1-2 free meals per day to their staff, known as "staff meals."
workSkillDescription.gardener-skill: The "Gardener skill (Groundskeeper)" is a work skill for landscaping and managing gardens, including water management and cultivating plants in gardens of upper-skill estates. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called "Groundskeepers". In the world of Raxia, having a garden at home is primarily common among a very limited upper class, such as nobility and wealthy individuals. Some rulers might establish parks within or near cities for residents to relieve stress, but Groundskeepers also manage these parks. There are also wealthy commoners who set up gardens within their own property, but such commoners often enjoy landscaping as a hobby without relying on Groundskeepers. Due to this nature, Groundskeepers mostly live with employers or patrons and are therefore usually found only near influential people or facilities with large gardens. It's not uncommon for wealthy patrons to provide living quarters for the Groundskeeper within the mansion or garden, in which case the Groundskeeper would be living on-site while managing the garden. Most Groundskeepers make their living from these management duties. While tasks like pruning may sometimes be completed in about a day, basic tasks such as cleaning and watering should be done at least every three days. Therefore, unless it's in an area with a winter season where plants don't grow, or unless additional staff are employed separately, a Groundskeeper will spend most of the year dedicated to garden management. As a designer, a Groundskeeper may sometimes design gardens upon request from a patron. When designing such gardens, while considering the various intentions of the patron, the Groundskeeper designs the garden by taking into account the balance of the main building, water usage, guest traffic flow, and local vegetation. They may also be responsible for transporting and installing special stones from distant locations or ordering sculptures and fountains separately. As a manager, garden management is the task that most Groundskeepers engage with for the longest time. They perform tasks to keep the garden beautiful, including various cleaning duties, pruning garden trees, and mowing grass, transplanting flowers, watering, fertilizing, and managing greenhouses. Some Groundskeepers who manage large-scale gardens also maintain separate cultivation areas for plants, flowers, fruit trees, and vegetables to be transplanted according to the season. For Groundskeepers cultivating these plants for transplanting, agricultural work would be incorporated into their daily routine.
workSkillDescription.carpenter-skill: The "Carpenter skill (Woodworker)" is a work skill primarily used for constructing houses, bridges, and other structures using wood. Those who use this skill professionally are called "Woodworkers." On the other hand, those who have acquired carpentry skills as a hobby are referred to as "DIY woodworkers." In small rural villages and remote settlements where there are no professional woodworkers, it's not uncommon for all residents to have some degree of Carpentry skills. This is because in such settlements, it's typical for villagers to gather and build houses and barns together. People who specialize in woodwork often work in skilled groups led by a master carpenter and employ an apprenticeship system. This is because many of their tasks, such as building houses and creating and maintaining urban and town infrastructure, are inefficient to perform alone. These skilled groups have been deeply rooted in their localities for a long time. In cities and towns, they are often directly licensed by the ruling class, such as feudal lords. Therefore, it can cause conflicts if woodworkers from other areas try to work without permission. In large cities, multiple woodworker groups have their own territories, with guilds acting as mediators between them. However, in smaller towns, it's not uncommon for a single woodworker group to cover the entire area.
workSkillDescription.gangster-skill: Gangster skill is a work skill that represents the techniques of villains belonging to illegal organizations. Those who excel at exploiting others' weaknesses, hinting at violence, making high profits through the sale of illegal goods or the operation of illegal events, and who do these things routinely to make a living are called Gangsters. The public safety in cities existing in the current world of Raxia can hardly be called good. There are many places beyond the reach of law enforcement and guards, and it's impossible to monitor and control all logistics and events. Therefore, in downtown areas and slums, it's common for Gangsters to establish their own order, securing their own interests while maintaining a certain stability. To maintain and continue this, intimidation and violence are essential, and skilled Gangsters cleverly use these to maximize their profits (although they themselves may not necessarily be experts in violence). While Gangsters are fundamentally villains, they sometimes protect the order of the area so they can be allies of the common people. There are also, albeit rarely, tough Gangsters who are rich in chivalry, value loyalty and human relationships, and stick to their principles. Although Gangsters have a rough image, it's rare for them to actually engage in fights. Basically, wise Gangsters avoid actual combat by projecting an image of being "violent and strong" to intimidate others. However, if they turn out to be "weak as a result of actual fighting," they can't maintain that image, so hiring separate Bouncers who specialize in violence (those who excel in the Fighter class or Grappler class) is common. Of course, Gangsters themselves are usually more accustomed to fighting and better at violence than ordinary people, and it's not uncommon for some to be masters of combat.
workSkillDescription.gambler-skill: The Gambler skill is a work skill that involves mastering the rules and tactics of gambling to achieve victory. Those who frequent gambling dens and casinos, living off the money earned from gambling, or those who work in such places and compete against customers are called Gamblers. In any city of considerable size, gambling dens and casinos are almost certain to exist. Even without them, it's commonplace for travelers and adventurers to start gambling in taverns. The tools typically used are simple playing cards (similar to modern playing cards) that became popular during the Magitech Civilization Period, as well as dice and coin flips (in some regions, countries, or cultures, more complex games may be used for gambling). Horse racing, dog racing, cockfighting, and gladiatorial battles in the Arena are also famous forms of gambling. However, this skill is ineffective against gambling where the "betting side" cannot influence the competition. It's primarily effective in games where one's own fingertips, reading abilities, words, expressions, and tactics can be applied. Skilled Gamblers are well-versed in how to win games and adept at obtaining winnings without trouble. Some Gamblers team up with specific taverns or establishments to fleece customers, while others work as dealers under contract with casinos. Skilled Gamblers rarely stay in one place for long, moving on to another location before they win too much and incur resentment. As a result, many of them are constantly on the move.
workSkillDescription.gravekeeper-skill: The "Gravekeeper skill (Gravekeeper)" is a work skill for monitoring and cleaning graveyards, as well as assisting with funerals. Those who have mastered this skill and make it their livelihood are mainly called Gravekeepers. Gravekeeper is a work skill typically found in urban areas with large populations where funerals are held regularly and is rarely present in small settlements with only narrow graveyards. Most Humanoid remains are buried in the ground. In regions with large burial grounds, many remains are placed in coffins and buried in graves. In most cases, cemeteries are managed by temples or rulers, and Gravekeepers are typically employed to work in these burial grounds. During funerals, a Gravekeeper's job includes arranging tombstones and coffins, digging graves, and guiding mourners. It's not uncommon for families to place grave goods in the coffins, and the upper classes may dress the deceased in luxurious clothing, which can lead to frequent grave robbing. As a result, Gravekeepers may also be required to work night shifts, taking turns to watch for intruders attempting to rob graves. In urban areas, where it's often difficult to establish large burial grounds on the surface and burial spaces are limited, underground cemeteries are not uncommon. Temples or rulers may contract Gravekeepers to construct and manage these underground cemeteries. The construction and management of underground cemeteries require multiple Gravekeepers, so they may be organized into groups. If temples or rulers do not employ Gravekeepers and abandon the management of underground cemeteries, criminals may appear to loot the graves, or those who manipulate corpses might create Undead.
workSkillDescription.carriage-driver-skill: The "Carriage Driver skill (Coachman)" is a work skill for operating a carriage pulled by horses or other animals, which can carry passengers or cargo. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are primarily called Coachmen. A Coachman's duties include operating the carriage, managing the draft animals such as horses that pull the carriage, and maintaining and cleaning the carriage. The animals used to pull carriages, such as horses, are trained individuals, typically through the Tamer skill (see p. 101). (The Carriage Driver skill cannot train animals themselves). There are various types of carriages, which are the tools of a Coachman's trade. Those commonly used by the general public are wagons and stagecoaches. Many wagons and stagecoaches do not have roofs, and canvas covers are used to protect against rain and wind. A wagon is the simplest type of carriage in the area, consisting of nothing more than a large box-like chassis with two or four wheels attached, except for the seat where the Coachman sits. A stagecoach is a carriage designed to transport many people, with simple wooden box-like seats placed on both sides of a four-wheeled wagon chassis, facing sideways in the direction of travel. Stagecoaches primarily operate in urban areas, quickly transporting passengers within the city and to nearby areas at affordable fares. The operation of regular freight wagons used by merchants and stagecoaches is often organized systematically, and in some regions, part of the business may be coordinated with the Rider's Guild (see CR III, p. 267). Carriages with doors, windows, decorations, and well-appointed interiors with roofs are primarily owned by the upper class. These carriages are very luxurious, and their Coachmen are expected to wear attire and display manners befitting the upper class. For high-end carriages, Coachmen may also be required to assist passengers with boarding and alighting, such as opening and closing doors.
workSkillDescription.cook-skill: The "Cook skill (Chef)" is a work skill for creating dishes by combining various ingredients and seasonings. While home cooking also uses this work skill, only those who wield it professionally are called "Chefs". Such Chefs have existed since ancient times, but in the past, they were limited to those exclusively serving nobles in mansions or as court Chefs. They adopted a complete division of labor system, with specialized craftsmen for meat, fish, vegetable preparation, cutting, grilling, plating, etc., while the head chef oversaw, directed, and tasted while observing. This structure remains largely unchanged, especially in court kitchens. In the past, common Chefs could only offer one or two simple dishes in taverns or run food stalls selling a single dish. However, during the late Magitech Civilization Period, the concept of "restaurants" developed, and even after the Diabolic Triumph, it's not uncommon to find places where you can choose from a wide menu, not just in high-end establishments but also in popular eateries. In the world of Raxia, including the Alframe continent, there's a tendency to recognize Dwarf cuisine, Kobold cuisine, and Lildraken cuisine as the three major cuisines, regardless of location. Dwarf cuisine is an art of fire and oil utilizing Body Of Flame, Kobold cuisine heavily uses rich sauces and spices (to mask poor-quality ingredients in Barbarous territories), while Lildraken cuisine is characterized by raw or lightly cooked dishes that emphasize the freshness of ingredients and unique textures. Apart from Humans, you're most likely to encounter Chefs from these three races.
workSkillDescription.towerman-skill: The "Towerman skill (High-Rise Laborer)" is a work skill necessary for working at heights on multi-story structures and large bridges. These specialists work in dangerous locations such as tower and fortress construction and painting, roof tile installation, and suspension bridge construction. Those who have mastered this skill are called High-Rise Laborers. Due to the Diabolic Triumph, civilization was destroyed, and extremely tall high-rise buildings decreased in number or disappeared altogether. Nevertheless, High-Rise Laborers are essential for tasks such as installing roof tiles on two-story houses, building suspension bridges over valleys, and performing repairs and maintenance on them. In particular, castles and towers where kings reside are sufficiently tall, and their repair and painting are specialized tasks that would be difficult without High-Rise Laborers.
workSkillDescription.detective-skill: The Detective skill is a work skill necessary for uncovering hidden secrets and solving mysteries. Those who utilize this skill to accept requests for problem-solving are called Detectives. In the current world of Raxia, the profession of Detective is not very common. This is due to the poor public safety and inadequate legal system, which allows for rampant criminal activities and vigilante problem-solving. Nevertheless, there is a demand for actions such as surveillance and tailing specific individuals, gathering physical evidence to prove crimes and deducing methods of murder or theft to corner culprits. There are those who seek skilled Detectives. Most requests come from nobles, people in power, or the wealthy, and if one can gain the trust of such clients, high rewards can be expected. On the other hand, there are also many small and mundane jobs, such as searching for runaway cats or lost items or staking out to investigate infidelity. Active adventurers or former adventurers who have retired from adventures outside the city sometimes start Detective work, and their skills and specialties vary. As they may have to directly enter crime scenes or be attacked by villains trying to cover up crimes, some acquire combat skills to protect themselves. However, combat abilities are not included in the Detective skill, so they need to acquire a separate adventurer class for that purpose. Additionally, what's important for a Detective is having connections that can be relied upon for information sources and evidence examination. The more experienced a Detective is, the wider their network of connections, enabling them to solve cases quickly and accurately. These reliable information sources are individuals who provide valuable and trustworthy information to Detectives, such as informants, fellow professionals, or well-connected figures in political and financial circles. Consult with the GM to establish such a character. While they may demand money or equivalent compensation, the information obtained from these sources is reliable. Adventurers with Detective skill of level 5 or higher can acquire new information sources within a few days when moving to a different city. Their experience as a Detective allows them to swiftly establish reliable information networks, regardless of location. GMs should utilize these information sources to provide useful information to PCs or help when adventures or investigations reach a deadlock.
workSkillDescription.tailor-skill: Tailor skill is the skill to create clothing and fabric products using cloth and thread. Those who possess this skill and make it their livelihood are called "Dressmakers". In the world of Raxia, clothing is primarily produced by hand by Dressmakers and is not inexpensive for the average citizen. Dressmakers work in settlements of a certain size or larger. In medium-sized or smaller settlements, tailors often open clothing shops, likely engaging in buying and selling second-hand clothing and repairing fabric products. In the world of Raxia, there is a thriving second-hand clothing market. Since clothing is made by Dressmakers, most new clothing items are custom-made to order. New clothing costs at least three times the minimum price shown in the general equipment clothing table. Due to these circumstances, the minimum prices for clothing shown in the general equipment clothing table (see CR I, p. 291, ET, p. 115) are basically the prices for second-hand or inferior-quality items. Most second-hand items have tears in the fabric patched with lining, repair cloth, or frayed threads disguised with similar designs. For the average citizen, purchasing new clothing might only occur when making "formal wear" for coming-of-age celebrations or attending ceremonial occasions like weddings and funerals. Those who routinely have multiple custom-made clothing items for personal use are likely to be individuals who interact with the upper class, those who are meticulous about cleanliness, or fashion enthusiasts who are sensitive to trends.
workSkillDescription.barber-skill: The "Barber skill (Hairdresser/Barber)" is a work skill for cutting and styling hair. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called "Hairdressers/Barbers". Wealthy merchants and upper classes with financial means request hairdressers or barbers for hair styling and shaving. Therefore, hairdressers and barbers need to be familiar with current trends, local fashions, and standard hairstyles of the time. Hairdressers and barbers, being skilled in handling bladed tools like scissors and razors, may sometimes be entrusted with simple surgical procedures such as incisions and sutures. However, due to their limited medical knowledge, a separate healthcare professional might be advisable to examine the patient with a Pathology check (see CR I, p. 107).
workSkillDescription.housekeeper-skill: "Housekeeper skill" is a work skill for handling all aspects of housework, such as cleaning and cooking. In particular, those who are employed by the wealthy or nobility to maintain the condition of mansions and support the residents' comfortable living are called Housekeepers. Some even live in the mansion and share their lives with their employers. In the current Raxia, where water and sewage systems are underdeveloped, and household appliances are mostly non-existent, efficiently handling all household chores is difficult and labor-intensive. When employed by high-status households, there are customs and taboos in handling household items and cooking methods, and the knowledge and skills that must be acquired are extensive. Therefore, being employed in such mansions without a high Housekeeper skill level would be difficult. Conversely, excellent housekeepers are hired for high wages and sometimes even become confidants to the homeowners. It should be noted that housekeepers are overwhelmingly female and are sometimes called maids (in the case of males, they are called boys).
workSkillDescription.performer-skill: "Performer skill (Entertainer)" is a work skill used to entertain people by showcasing various arts. There are many specialized fields, from physical feats centered on street performances and circus acts to comedic storytelling eliciting laughter. Those who make this their profession are called Entertainers. Entertainment is extremely rare in the world of Raxia, which continues to be threatened by the Barbarous after the Diabolic Triumph. Therefore, the performances showcased by skilled Entertainers are popular everywhere. You can see them in various forms, such as traveling Entertainers who perform while journeying or jesters employed by nobles and aristocrats to soothe their minds. It is difficult to master multiple arts, so those who acquire this skill need to learn different Performer skills for each genre of performance. Street Performers: These are Entertainers who stand on main streets to entertain the general public with acts such as juggling (showing skills of throwing and catching multiple objects), pantomime (expressing invisible walls and such through body movements), and living statues (becoming motionless statues that suddenly move to surprise people). Acrobats: These are Entertainers who delight audiences with spectacular techniques that utilize their physical abilities, such as somersaults, tightrope walking, and unicycle riding. They also excel in team performances involving multiple people. Clowns: These Entertainers wear comical costumes and use humorous movements or clumsy acts to make the audience laugh. They may perform silently or sometimes act as a host with bonus skill levels or add dialogue. They may also be employed by the court and have the role of speaking frankly to the king. By mainly using irony and satire, they can lighten the mood or advise in tense situations, making them surprisingly influential entertainers. In this case, they are called jesters. Stand-up Comedians: These are Entertainers who stand in front of an audience and entertain them with the art of talking. This can range from solo monologues to comedy duos or trios to interactive performances that involve the audience in creating laughter. The variety is quite wide. They may also incorporate musical performances or magic tricks (though these are separate skills).
workSkillDescription.fortune-teller-skill: The "Fortune Teller skill (Psychic)" is a work skill used to perform various types of divination, predict the future, and solve problems. Some have established shops, while others serve clients by the roadside. Those who engage in such activities daily are called "Psychics". Many of the divinations performed by Psychics are either based on chance or are psychological in nature, deriving desired answers from the client's words and expressions. They do not use magical powers and sometimes may employ childish tricks or fraudulent methods. Of course, there are those who exert supernatural powers to foretell more definitive futures. However, such individuals are called "Mystics (Diviners)" and are distinguished from Psychics. While there are several famous Mystics on the southern continent of Terastier, they are virtually unknown on the northern continent of Alframe. Nevertheless, everyone wants to know about the future and resolve their current worries. Therefore, even if a Psychic's divination is baseless, there is no end to people who cling to it. Some Psychics are even employed by kings and nobles, serving as advisors when doubts arise.
workSkillDescription.prostitute-skill: "Prostitute skill (Harlot/Gigolo)" is a work skill that utilizes sexual appeal to please clients using one's body. Those who primarily stand on street corners at night and regularly take clients are called Harlot or Gigolo. The profession of providing sexual pleasure using one's body has existed since ancient times, and this is no exception in the current Raxia. Young and healthy individuals can earn money without particular skills or education, but it is a common occupation seen in slums and remote settlements. It often serves as a significant source of income for criminal organizations, and while it may be considered an illegal profession in some countries, it is tolerated in most. There are cases where people are bought and sold in a form of human trafficking due to debt, and many become harlots or gigolos unwillingly. Many harlots and gigolos stand on street corners in downtown areas or back alleys off the main streets, waiting for clients. Some may solicit customers in bars, and with the backing of criminal organizations, entire lodging facilities may be operated as brothels for entertaining clients. In some cases, Harlots/Gigolos are managed collectively and dispatched to inns, rest areas, or private homes. Harlot/Gigolo as a Culture: While many Harlots/Gigolos work independently, some form organizations, and in certain countries and regions, this profession has evolved into a cultural phenomenon. In such cases, in addition to their skills as Harlots/Gigolos, some are also accomplished in arts such as singing and dancing. In regions where this culture exists, wealthy clients may become patrons, providing their favorite Harlot/Gigolo with luxurious clothing, education, and training in the arts, and may eventually personally redeem them to become their lover (however, proficiency in education and arts requires the acquisition of a separate skill). Additionally, when entering a contract with a specific individual, it may be necessary to acquire the new [Courtesan Skill] (see p. 96).
workSkillDescription.beggar-skill: "Beggar skill (Tramp)" is a work skill for living off alms received on urban street corners. Those who have mastered this skill and make it their livelihood are mainly called Tramps. The Tramp lifestyle is primarily sustainable in urban areas with large populations and high circulation of goods and funds. In the Humanoid society of the world of Raxia, there are many temples that advocate for helping the weak, so a culture of charitable giving has taken root to some extent. Tramps live in Humanoid cities due to this cultural background. Many Tramps, despite being poor, have their own homes. Among them are Tramps who intentionally pretend to be injured or ill to receive more alms, Tramps who walk around with children to evoke sympathy, and those who become Tramps due to low work motivation despite having assets. These malicious individuals tend to worsen urban security. A Source of Urban Information: Most Tramps stand on street corners so as not to obstruct the passage of others, and they are largely unnoticed by the majority of urban residents. To obtain better alms and blessings, Tramps observe various passersby in the city, listen to rumors, and gather information that other urban residents might not pay attention to. Due to this nature, when searching for people or lost items in the city, Tramps' information can sometimes be a valuable source.
workSkillDescription.merchant-skill: The "Merchant skill" is a skill primarily required for buying and selling goods. From shopkeepers to peddlers, brokers, and traders, those with this skill possess knowledge about various types of business. People who utilize this skill for commerce are called "merchants". Due to the existence of the money god Gamel, the world of Raxia has a well-established monetary economy, resulting in merchants being active all over the world. For adventurers who frequently purchase and replace equipment, the presence of merchants is indispensable. Moreover, there are many adventurer-merchants who venture into dangerous areas in search of new products and markets. They excel in knowledge of trading, negotiation skills for pricing and procurement, and financial management abilities. Those who have mastered this skill are typically granted a license for conducting business by the authorities of the area where they reside. To engage in trade in other areas or countries, they need to improve their skill level further and acquire additional licenses.
workSkillDescription.manager-skill: The Manager skill is a work skill that represents the knowledge and techniques of organizing an organization, managing personnel, and handling finances. Those who do this type of work are called Managers. In organizations of a certain size or larger, such Managers are likely to exist and supervise various tasks. This also applies to criminal organizations, where criminal groups with skilled Managers skillfully manipulate many criminals like puppets and generate high profits. The Managers themselves may be the boss of the organization, but it's not uncommon for them to be the boss's right-hand person or advisor. In cases where there's a boss or other executives above them, the Manager takes on a position like middle management and is expected to produce high results.
workSkillDescription.butcher-skill: Butcher skill is a work skill that encompasses techniques for dismembering and processing animal meat. Butchers are those who use this skill to butcher and process livestock or game meat to create products for sale in butcher shops. Meat processing traditionally involves cutting primal cuts into retail-ready slices, cubes, or ground meat. However, Butcher skill is much broader, covering techniques from the initial handling of animal carcasses, skinning, creating sides of meat (skinned, beheaded, eviscerated, and split in half along the median line), breaking down into primal cuts (separated by section), and then processing the meat into products like sausages and bacon. When meat is supplied to butcher shops from dairy farmers or hunters, it's often already broken down into sides or primal cuts. Butchers then further process this into retail cuts or processed meats. As a result, it's not uncommon for dairy farmers, hunters, and butchers to all possess a certain level of Butcher skill. However, only those working in butcher shops are typically called Butchers. Additionally, most residents possess this skill in nomadic communities or villages that practice animal husbandry. Most Butchers operate as butcher shops with permission from the merchant guild. Depending on the size of the shop, some employ an apprenticeship-like system for meat processing workers, while others hire employees, including trainees.
workSkillDescription.midwife-skill: Midwife skill is a work skill for assisting in childbirth and protecting the health of mothers and children after delivery. Those who have acquired this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Midwives. Midwives are relied upon in various Humanoid settlements, from sparsely populated areas without temples or Doctors to urban areas where, despite a large population, the health of ordinary citizens cannot be fully attended to. Midwives consult with pregnant women before childbirth, assist with delivery, and continue to provide advice on childcare after birth, maintaining close communication with mothers of young children and supporting them in child-rearing. Midwives know the usefulness of disinfection through experience and pay attention to cleanliness. They are also skilled in first aid and other related practices.
workSkillDescription.teamster-skill: The "Teamster skill (Manual Laborer)" is a work skill primarily for performing physical labor such as cargo handling and simple construction work. Many who work in this field are day laborers or work on individual contracts, and those who make a living doing such jobs are called Manual Laborers. In the current world of Raxia, there are numerous opportunities for Manual Laborers to work. Cities are fortified to prepare for monster attacks, and expanding them as the population grows becomes a massive undertaking. Besides that, there is no shortage of work, including building new homes, constructing infrastructure, maintaining highways, and so on. They can also be greatly useful in loading and unloading cargo for carriages and ships. In such cases, laborers who are known for their strength and have mastered the knack of carrying loads are highly valued.
workSkillDescription.armorer-skill: The "Armorer skill (Armor Craftsman)" is the technique for processing metal, wood, and leather to create armor and shields. Among blacksmiths, carpenters, and leatherworkers, those who specialize in this skill are called Armor Craftsmen. Armor Craftsmen who mainly work with metal belong to the blacksmith guild, while those who primarily work with non-metals belong to the leatherworker guild. Some craft both and belong to both guilds, but as a profession, they often specialize in one or the other. However, unless it's a highly specialized workshop, becoming a craftsman requires learning both techniques to some extent. Especially when making shields, it's not uncommon for both skills to be necessary. Regardless of which guild they belong to, Armor Craftsmen often produce items for weapon shops and directly supply goods to knightly orders and guard units. Examples of those not belonging to a guild are limited to those employed by nobility and royalty. Due to the vast amount of work and materials required, as well as the complexity, there tend to be fewer freelance Armor Craftsmen. Leather armor is made by tanning animal hides and is a typical nonmetallic armor. Particularly, armor made from "boiled leather," which is hardened and toughened leather, is popular among Fencers and Scouts because it's lightweight while still providing a certain level of protection. There are so many recipes for making this hard leather that they differ from workshop to workshop, and it's not uncommon for these to be closely guarded secrets.
workSkillDescription.weaver-skill: The "Weaver skill (Weaver)" is a work skill possessed by craftsmen who weave fabric using thread. Those who have this skill and make it their livelihood are called Weavers. In the world of Raxia, the fabric is basically produced by hand by Weavers and is expensive. What Weavers do is weave fabric from large amounts of thread. What Weavers do is produce fabric; dyeing or embroidering thread or fabric is done with other work skills. Many Weavers produce fabric using a machine called a "loom" that efficiently weaves by alternately combining warp and weft threads. Looms vary in shape and handling depending on the thickness and material of the thread, the technical heritage and culture of the area, and the resulting fabric. The looms that Weavers use are mostly at least 50cm wide and over 1m deep and are installed in workshops along with chairs and other furniture, not designed for portability. Additionally, when using thick threads, there are Weavers who weave fabric by hand-knitting with knitting needles or crochet hooks. Complex fabrics like lace are generally made by hand-knitting rather than using a loom. Weavers have types of thread they specialize in and must decide which types of thread they will handle at the time of acquisition. In the world of Raxia, the most commonly distributed threads are cotton, linen, and wool, with silk also existing as a very high-end thread. Note that the more densely woven the thread or the finer the fabric itself, the more thread and work processes are required to complete a single piece of fabric, making it more expensive (e.g., carpets and silk fabrics). When acquiring the Weaver skill, the Weaver must choose two types of thread to specialize in and master (e.g., "Weaver skill: cotton & wool"). For threads they are not specialized in, they receive a -2 penalty to the Success Value for the Weaving check when weaving fabric.
workSkillDescription.weaponsmith-skill: The "Weaponsmith skill (Weapon Craftsman)" is a work skill that represents the technique of processing metals and wood to create weapons. Among blacksmiths and Wood Craftsmen, those who specialize in this skill are called Weapon Craftsmen. While a Blacksmith might be able to forge simple knives or kitchen knives, only a Weapon Craftsman can create sharp yet durable weapons for combat with proper balance and weight distribution. Weapon Craftsmen typically belong to blacksmith guilds, maintain workshops, and employ an apprenticeship system. There are also itinerant Weapon Craftsmen (commonly known as field smiths) and craftsmen who have served noble or royal families for generations but are in the minority. Moreover, even if one is an adventurer or vagrant, one must pay respects to the local guild to practice smithing within a town or city. Weapon Craftsmen who belong to guilds create items for weapon shops and often directly supply weapons to knightly orders and guard units. Smithing can be broadly divided into two types: forging (hammering heated metal to shape it) and casting (pouring molten metal into molds). While casting is suitable for mass production, steel is considered optimal for weapons, and it is created through forging, making this method the more common choice. On the other hand, decorative parts such as sword guards and pommels may sometimes use easier metals (like bronze), and casting might be employed in such cases. The task of wielding the hammer to shape weapons of a certain size or larger, such as swords, is the job of craftsmen who have completed their apprenticeship. They must continue to swing the hammer with appropriate force while keenly perceiving the master's intentions. In some workshops, magitech hammers exist that the master can control directly, but these are extremely rare.
workSkillDescription.woodworker-skill: "Wood Craftsman skill" is a work skill that represents the technique of processing wood to create various items. Those who set up workshops and make a living by creating items with this skill are generally called Wood Craftsmen. Even among Wood Craftsmen, there are those who specialize in furniture, those who specialize in tools, those who specialize in toys, and so on. Depending on the items they make, there may be separate guilds, or there may be cities where a woodworking guild oversees everything. In either case, they typically set up workshops and adopt an apprenticeship system. On the other hand, in rural areas and small settlements, the Wood Craftsman skill is more rooted in daily life, and it's a skill that almost everyone can do to some extent. Even in such environments, there may be individuals particularly skilled in woodworking who make furniture for others, but they generally don't do this as their sole occupation. Separate from woodworking as an industry, creating sculptures and other items using wood also falls within the realm of the Wood Craftsman skill. Those who use this skill in this manner range from those who pursue it purely as an art form to those who apply their skills to religious institutions, such as carving divine statues.
workSkillDescription.color-man-skill: "Color Man skill (Dyer)" is a work skill that refers to the technique of creating paint by mixing pigments with oil, resin, glue, etc., or extracting dyes. Those who specialize in this technique are called "Dyers". Pigments refer to powders made from soil or minerals or powdered colorants extracted from plants, animal excrement, insects, mollusks, and other soft-bodied creatures. Dyers mix pigments with binders (such as oil, resin, glue, or egg yolk) to make paint. If the colorant is water-soluble, they mix it with water to create dyes for coloring fabrics and other materials. Paint-making is the first skill that is drilled into apprentices when they enter an Artist's workshop, and in large workshops, it's typically the job of apprentices. Therefore, Artists generally possess the Color Man skills. However, those who didn't succeed as Artists eventually began to specialize in paint-making as a means of livelihood. While professional painters often still insist on making their own paints, it has become common for hobbyist painters to use ready-made paints. On the other hand, the technique of creating dyes for dyeing is mostly managed by state-run guilds. This is because the extraction and dyeing of certain "noble" colors (such as purple) are difficult and, in some cases, considered state secrets. These workshops employ an apprenticeship system, but becoming an apprentice may require a certain social status. Outside urban areas, the Color Man skill is used in plant dyeing practiced in rural villages and communities.
workSkillDescription.locksmith-skill: "The Locksmith skill" is a work skill for creating various locks and their corresponding keys. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Locksmiths. In the world of Raxia, there are various types of locks and keys, and Locksmiths have knowledge about many of them. Most locks and keys are made of metal. In addition to making keys and locks, Locksmiths also create duplicate keys, repair locks, and, if requested, undertake the task of unlocking locks for which keys have been lost. Because locks and keys are expensive, their installation for security purposes is primarily prevalent in urban areas with high security awareness. Even in urban areas, the poor rarely have locks and keys in their homes, and the same is true for rural and mountainous areas with low population density. In houses without locks and keys, when at home, gates or barrier poles are installed on doors facing the outside to block the entrance. Merchants who handle money and the middle class and above who have assets prepare locks and keys not only for doors but also for sturdy wooden boxes and iron safes. Due to these circumstances, Locksmiths primarily conduct their business in urban areas. As locks and keys are security devices, it's not uncommon for Locksmiths to also undertake the production and installation of gate components.
workSkillDescription.cobbler-skill: "The Cobbler skill (Shoemaker)" is a work skill for producing footwear that envelops the feet. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are primarily called Shoemakers. Most Humanoids have the habit of wearing shoes. Many shoes are made of leather, with thick leather or woven tree bark used for the soles. Most ordinary citizens only need to protect the soles of their feet, so they use shoes that go up to the ankle or sandals that focus on protecting the soles. Wooden clogs are also in circulation. Boots that cover up to the calf or knee also exist, but they are expensive. Adventurers often wear boots to protect their legs as they operate in harsh environments such as wastelands. In cold regions, even ordinary citizens frequently use boots. In the world of Raxia, Shoemakers produce easily adjustable shoes for a wide variety of races. Shoes that are easy to adjust in size and inexpensive are those with holes punched in soft leather edges, which can be adjusted by tightening with shoelaces. Laced sandals and wooden clogs secured to the feet with laces are also widely used due to their low cost. In contrast, shoes and boots made with hard leather must be fitted to the wearer's size, so they are usually custom-made and expensive.
workSkillDescription.whitesmith-skill: "The Whitesmith skill (Jeweler)" is a work skill for creating intricate pieces using precious metals and gems. A craftsman who sets up a workshop and creates jewelry is called a Jeweler. Due to the characteristics of the metals they work with, unlike blacksmiths, Jewelers primarily use casting (pouring molten metal into molds) rather than forging (hammering heated metal). Of course, that's not all; they employ a wide range of techniques, including filing, soldering, sawing, forging, and polishing, to create highly detailed and beautifully decorative items. While they are generally known for creating accessories for personal adornment, in reality, they also make items for everyday use by the upper classes, such as gold and silver tableware and inlaid cups, as well as items used in temple rituals and even small gold or silver statues. Among Jewelers, those who specialize in working with gold are called goldsmiths, while those who specialize in silver are called silversmiths. However, regardless of the materials they work with, all Jewelers possess the skills to set gems and create inlays. Jewelers, even if employed by nobility or royalty, must, in principle, be members of a guild. This is because their clientele is primarily from the upper echelons of society, and their products are often high-end, necessitating control over pricing, rarity, and brand value. In many cases, each workshop has its own distinctive style, and because of the strong emphasis on "creating beautiful things," Jewelers tend to have a more artistic sensibility compared to other craftsmen. These skills are passed down to future generations through an apprenticeship system.
workSkillDescription.distiller-skill: "The Distiller skill (Distiller)" is a work skill for distilling fermented alcohol and producing spirits with higher alcohol content. These individuals who create stronger alcoholic beverages compared to brewing are called Distillers. The alcohol content of fermented beverages is limited to about 20%, and to create stronger alcohol, it is necessary to perform "distillation" by collecting and concentrating evaporated alcohol. The history of distilled alcohol is ancient, with records of its existence dating back at least to the Magic Civilization Period. However, the distilled alcohol culture truly flourished during the Magitech Civilization Period when the magical distillation apparatus was invented. While very few magical distillation apparatuses remain today, the spirits developed at that time continue to be produced with modern technology (although perhaps with inferior purity). Since distilled alcohol changes its flavor through storage, it is not consumed immediately (in fact, the aroma is often unsuitable for drinking right after distillation) and is aged in barrels or jars.
