During this time, aging in wooden barrels to impart flavors and colors derived from the wood was also widely practiced. Additionally, distillers create their unique spirits using various techniques, such as deliberately retaining impurities from the original ingredients by limiting the number of distillations or repeatedly distilling to maximize alcohol content. It is common for distillers to contract with merchant guilds to produce and distribute their products, but there are also cases where temples take the lead in handling everything from spirit production to sales. Among the many races, it would not be an exaggeration to say that no race has mastered distilled alcohol as much as the Dwarves. Their spirit, made by distilling grain alcohol to its limit, boasts an alcohol content of 96% and is said to make your entire body feel as if it's on fire just from a single taste.
workSkillDescription.blacksmith-skill: "Blacksmith skill (Smith)" is a work skill for creating tools and objects by heating, hammering, and shaping metal in a forge. Those who specialize in this skill and make a living from it are called Smiths. Unlike the more specialized Weapon Craftsmen or Armor Craftsmen, Smiths make their living by creating and repairing various items useful for daily life, from knives and axes to nails and horseshoes. Smiths living in urban areas typically belong to blacksmith guilds, set up workshops, and follow the general pattern of craftsmen who employ an apprenticeship system. However, unlike craftsmen who make weapons and armor, the existence of the Smiths is rooted in people's daily lives. As a result, many settlements have "village smiths." They must be generalists rather than specialists because they have to make and repair the tools needed by the villagers. While some belong to city guilds, many Smiths who set up workshops in small settlements like villages have been part of those communities for generations, taking apprentices from within the settlement and passing on their skills. These "village smiths" tend to produce simple and sturdy items with a focus on practicality, but this doesn't mean their skills are inferior to those of Smiths affiliated with city guilds. In fact, in terms of durability and longevity, their products may sometimes be superior. The "black" in Blacksmith refers to black iron. As the name suggests, the Blacksmith skill mainly deals with ironwork. However, this doesn't mean they can't handle steel, bronze, or brass. Nevertheless, precious metals like gold and silver are the domain of Jewelers and cannot be handled by blacksmiths.
workSkillDescription.brewer-skill: "Brewer skill" is a work skill primarily used to create alcohol by fermenting grains or fruits using yeast. Among alcohol producers, those who specifically use Brewer skill to make fermented beverages are called Brewers. Additionally, some Brewers use fermentation and aging processes to produce not only alcohol but also vinegar and seasonings. On the Alframe continent, the two giants of fermented beverages are wine and beer. Both have records of being consumed since the Divine Civilization Period, making them beverages with a long history. Beer is made from barley, and during the middle of the Magitech Civilization Period, hops began to be added for their antiseptic properties. In the later period, bottom-fermented lagers were also produced, but due to the loss of stable manufacturing techniques during the Diabolic Triumph, top-fermented ales are now more common. Wine is made by preserving grape juice in barrels or vats and fermenting it with yeast. To extract juice from large quantities of grapes, the sight of many people treading grapes in large vats has become a seasonal tradition during harvest time. Other common fermented beverages include cider and mead. The Brewers who make these alcoholic beverages are often also farmers who cultivate the raw materials. It's not uncommon for their farms to be operated with support from the state or temples.
workSkillDescription.bone-carver-skill: "Bone Carver skill (Bone Craftsman)" is a work skill that represents the technique of creating items using bones, horns, and teeth from Animals and Mythical Beasts. Those who have mastered this skill and regularly create bone crafts are called Bone Craftsmen. Bone Craftsmen are rare in urban areas and tend to be more popular among those living in more primitive societies or closer to nature. Bone crafting often carries magical connotations in these societies and is used for charms and amulets. Additionally, bone crafts are used as artisanal goods in trade with distant regions. Bone Craftsmen living in urban areas are mostly artists, and there are no specific guilds for them. They mainly produce sculptures and scrimshaw, which are bone crafts with engraved patterns or pictures, for wealthy noble and merchant patrons. Bone crafts as accessories are more common among Barbarous rather than Humanoids. While Lower Barbarous often simply make necklaces by drilling holes in fangs and threading them, some Upper Barbarous wear very intricate bone crafts. As a result, owning a skilled Bone Craftsman as a slave can become a status symbol among Upper Barbarous.
workSkillDescription.mason-skill: "The Mason skill (Stonemason)" refers to the collective techniques of quarrying and processing stone. There are three main tasks that can be performed in the Mason skill: first, identifying, extracting, and transporting suitable stones from quarries; second, processing the stone for use as a building material and sometimes decorating it; and finally, using the processed stone to construct buildings. Those who make a living by performing these tasks are collectively called Stonemasons. While stone is more difficult to work with compared to wood, it is durable and long-lasting. As a result, it has traditionally been used for important structures and infrastructure such as castle walls, fortresses, bridges, and waterways. Additionally, since the creation of monuments and gravestones is also part of a Stonemason's work, it is not uncommon for Stonemason guilds to strongly influence city politics. The quarrying, processing, and construction of stone are typically completely separated as distinct businesses under the Stonemason guild, each employing an apprenticeship system. As mentioned above, Stonemason guilds, having been deeply rooted in cities since ancient times and serving powerful individuals and religious figures as clients, often wield significant influence in city and state politics. In some cases, they even secretly control the operations of city-states. Several known cases exist where the upper echelons of such Stonemason guilds have become inclined towards secrecy and mysticism, evolving into secret societies. However, in many instances, these are merely conspiracy theories born out of jealousy from other guilds.
workSkillDescription.leatherworker-skill: "Leatherworker skill (Leather Craftsman)" is a work skill that represents the technique of tanning animal hides into leather, decorating the leather, and processing it into various items. Those who tan hides or process tanned leather are collectively called Leather Craftsmen. In urban areas, workshops for tanning hides and workshops for processing tanned leather exist separately, although they are generally part of the same leather guild. However, due to the difference in workshop locations and the tendency for tanning workshops to be looked down upon, friction can sometimes occur. On the other hand, in small settlements such as villages and mountainous areas, hide tanning and processing are techniques rooted in daily life, typically carried out by the entire community. Animal hides will rot or harden if left unattended. Therefore, since ancient times, various "tanning" techniques have been developed to transform hides into materials that resist decay and maintain softness--leather. On the Alframe continent, "vegetable tanning"--especially using tree bark pieces and leaves--is common. The trees used vary by region, and each workshop keeps its methods as closely guarded secrets. However, the tanning process often uses materials that emit foul odors in addition to tree bark pieces, and combined with the smell of animals, a constant terrible stench emanates from the workshops. As a result, tanning workshops are located on the outskirts of cities, and working there has gained a reputation for being smelly and tough work.
workSkillDescription.inventor-skill: The "Inventor skill (Tinkerer)" is the skill of those who try to create new tools using various materials. Most of these are eccentric and strange machines, and many who are obsessed with this skill are considered oddballs, often called eccentrics or weirdos. The things Tinkerers create range from small, convenient tools to large-scale facilities and institutions. Most of their inventions are either useless failures or irrational objects that don't justify their cost. However, some create tools that become indispensable to daily life or achieve groundbreaking inventions that overturn existing concepts, so they can't be entirely dismissed. Nevertheless, coming up with ideas is challenging, and realizing them is even more difficult. Creating inventions requires funding and facilities, and without influential investors, patrons, or abundant assets, it would be impossible to secure these resources. Due to these circumstances, even for those who have mastered the Inventor skill at a high level, whether they can complete a new invention or not depends on luck. Tool Tinkerers have created everything from small items like multi-purpose knives to small pumps that efficiently transfer liquids between containers and large machines using pulleys and gears. They are thought to have greatly contributed to the development of the Magitech Civilization. Chemical Tinkerers have attempted to create new medicinal effects and properties by mixing existing chemicals. They sometimes refine specific remedies effective against particular diseases or curses.
workSkillDescription.engineer-skill: "Engineer skill (Engineer)" is a work skill that represents the techniques for operating and maintaining the magical engines, which are the power source of magical trains, as well as piloting the magical trains themselves. Both the motor mechanic and the magical train driver are called Engineers. The reason why both drivers and mechanics are called Engineers is derived from the fact that in the earliest magical trains, operating the motor meant piloting. In modern trains, these roles have long been separated, but the term still remains. Basically, the person who drives is called an "Engineer", while the person in charge of the motor is called an "Assistant Engineer", but in principle, both have learned each other's skills and can switch roles at any time. To become an Engineer, it is generally necessary to acquire the skills at the training school of the Railroad Guild in the Kingslay Republic of Iron and Steel in the Dorden region. After graduating from the training school, it is common to join the Railroad Guild, but there are also a certain number of people who become Engineers for private railroad trains or freelance trains not affiliated with the guild. Nevertheless, some interaction with the guild is essential (unless operating trains illegally).
workSkillDescription.enchanter-skill: As the name suggests, the "Enchanter skill" is a work skill that represents the technique of enhancing items with magical power. Craftsmen who use this technique to create Magic Weapons and tools, as well as sorcerers who research new magical items, are called Enchanters. When the general public hears "Enchanter," they might immediately think of a blacksmith forging magical swords. However, in reality, the technique spans a wide range of applications. Even magical items that can be created with modern technology--such as implements and rings that boost ability scores--are also made by Enchanters. There are two paths to becoming an Enchanter: craftsmen learning to manipulate magic power or magicians learning craftsmanship. In either case, it is something that those who have already mastered a certain level of skill pursue to reach greater heights, and there are no specialized workshops or apprenticeship systems specifically for Enchanters. Among craftsmen who create items, such as Weapon Craftsmen, Armor Craftsmen, Blacksmiths, and Jewelers, there are those who aim to be able to create "magical items." This may be due to pure pursuit of mastery or because they believe it will be commercially advantageous. Generally, Weapon Craftsmen tend to be the former, while Jewelers tend to be the latter. In any case, to be allowed to learn the Enhancing technique from a guild, one must be at least a craftsman. Those chosen will go to the Magician's Guild to learn the Enhancing technique there or learn from guild members who can already use the Enhancing technique. However, since the Enhancing technique requires magical talent, learning it doesn't necessarily mean one will be able to use it. For this reason, craftsmen who have mastered the Enhancing technique are regarded as elite, and there are even guilds where it is a prerequisite for attaining high positions. Many Magician's Guilds have departments that research methods to enhance items with unprecedented magic power, creating new magic swords and magical items. In such guilds, it is common to have lectures on Enhancing techniques given by researchers (or their assistants) to train the next generation.
workSkillDescription.author-skill: The "Author skill (Writer)" refers to those who create, write, and leave behind stories. While many focus on poetry, there are also those who write novels and tales using prose. Those who create stories through such writing are called "Writers". As mentioned before, poetry is commonly seen and often performed by Bards who sing stories. During the Magitech Civilization Period, novels and other books existed, so stories were also written in imitation of these forms. However, as printing technology has been lost or declined, mass production and widespread distribution of books is not very realistic. Nevertheless, in cities where printing facilities from the Magitech Civilization Period have survived, works by Writers can be enjoyed in the form of books and newspapers. Moreover, Writers are often avid readers themselves. They may be well-versed in past stories and legends and may also possess information about other Writers. Among Writers, some make a living by becoming employed by nobles or influential adventurers, turning ancestral legends into poetry or stories, or composing epics about the exploits of adventurers.
workSkillDescription.cartographer-skill: The "Cartographer skill" is a work skill for creating more accurate maps or drawing beautifully decorated maps. It allows for the creation of maps using various techniques as needed, and those who make a living from this work are called Cartographers. Due to the impact of the "Diabolic Triumph" that occurred about 300 years ago, the terrain has changed significantly, and many old maps have been forced to undergo revisions. Therefore, new and accurate maps created by Cartographers are highly valuable. They are especially prized by explorers, adventurers, and navigators, for whom it can be a matter of life and death. To accurately know the terrain, Cartographers themselves often need to visit the actual location, making it a profession where they frequently travel outside of town when not engaged in mapmaking. While surveying items are sometimes used, methods such as counting steps to measure distances are also employed. They mainly create maps of outdoor areas, but for large-scale ruins, Cartographers may accompany adventurers to map out the structure. The created maps may be copied and sold. The rarer or more dangerous the location, the higher the price of the map. About the Cartography check: With this check, a Cartographer can understand the terrain, estimate travel distances, and predict the required time.
workSkillDescription.composer-skill: The "Composer skill" is a work skill possessed by people who create musical pieces, write them down as sheet music, and accumulate knowledge about various types of music from different regions. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Composers. Composers are also equipped with the ability to play some musical instruments, but it is rare for them to earn income from playing instruments themselves. Composers make a living by writing down their own compositions and traditional music as sheet music and selling these scores to those with the Bard class (see CR II, p. 100) or Singer skill (see p. 84). Composers may also provide performance guidance to musicians, and these lessons serve as another source of income. They might also become conductors, giving instructions to multiple performers. Many Composers have connections with the upper class. The upper class, in order to become trendsetters and topic starters themselves, commissioned new pieces from Composers and have them performed by exclusive musicians and vocalists at parties and tea gatherings. In any case, most Composers primarily operate in urban areas where people gather, and music is played on a daily basis. Musical Notation Format: In the world of Raxia, the format of musical notation is somewhat standardized. By looking at the sheet music, Composers and performers can understand the musical scale, tempo, and dynamics. This musical notation format is almost entirely inherited from the format established during the Magitech Civilization Period and is written using distinctive symbols different from language. Therefore, Composers and performers should be able to interpret both magitech and modern sheet music.
workSkillDescription.surgeon-skill: "Surgeon skill" is a work skill used to treat a patient's condition by suturing wounds, splinting fractures, or excising affected areas using blades. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Surgeons. In the world of Raxia, where healing magic exists, Surgeons who perform operations that may pose a risk to patients are extremely rare. While Surgeons empirically possess knowledge of so-called "modern medicine", they are generally considered heretics, and thus very few people pursue this as a specialized profession.
workSkillDescription.singer-skill: The "Singer skill (Vocalist)" is a work skill for showcasing one's singing voice. Those who have mastered this skill and make a living from it are primarily called "Vocalists". Vocalists primarily showcase their singing at festivals and events held in temples and settlements. There are also those who work in groups, assuming choral performances. Many Vocalists who primarily perform at such festivals and events belong to traveling entertainer troupes, continuing their nomadic journey in accordance with seasonal events in various locations. Among Vocalists, there are those who operate under the patronage of the upper classes. Vocalists in such positions are invited to parties and tea gatherings, where they are expected to showcase their vocal talents.
workSkillDescription.scholar-skill: The "Scholar skill (Student/Scholar)" is a work skill acquired by those devoted to studying. Among those who have mastered this skill, we call "students" those who attend school or seek teachings from a master, and "scholars" those who immerse themselves in research at universities, research institutes, and the like. In the current world of Raxia, where public safety is still unstable, and life continues in closed fortress cities, only nobles, the wealthy, or those fortunate enough to encounter affordable or free education from classrooms or teachers can dedicate themselves to studying in peace. Therefore, those who can study and acquire this skill are limited to the economically affluent or the lucky ones. It is difficult to earn money with this skill, and it is often acquired by the wealthy as a hobby, with income usually obtained from other professions. Those who acquire this skill typically study a wide range of fields in their youth and eventually progress toward specialized research. As a guideline, consider those at level 5 or below as "students" and those at level 6 or above as "scholars". More accomplished scholars may be well-versed in multiple fields. At level 10, it becomes possible to call oneself a "Professor". Those who have reached this level may also obtain high positions in guilds, research institutions, or universities, and may even secure roles involved in matters of national importance.
workSkillDescription.sculptor-skill: "Sculptor skill (Sculptor)" is a work skill for creating stone statues and wood carvings. Those who have mastered this skill and make it their livelihood are primarily called Sculptors. Sculptors are both craftsmen and artists and are allowed to create sculptures as works of art that reflect their own sensibilities while interpreting the orders from clients. Stone statues are mostly installed as decorations in temples, high-end buildings, and gardens. As stone statues can be installed in large-scale facilities, it's not uncommon for Sculptors to be involved in the work from the design stage of facilities and buildings. Since creating a Sculptor's work takes a long time, Sculptors often have patrons. Sculptors without patrons might take on more commissions for small stone statues or wood carving decorations for furniture and houses.
workSkillDescription.scribe-skill: "Scribe skill (Scrivener)" is a work skill for copying books, writing letters, or drafting documents on behalf of others. Those who have mastered this skill and make a living from it are primarily called Scriveners. In the world of Raxia, document reproduction technology is not well-developed, so copying documents and books is a daily task for Scriveners. Due to the daily wage for Scriveners and the not-inexpensive costs of paper and ink, commissioning a Scrivener for copying is a considerable expense for the average citizen. As the general populace in the world of Raxia has a high literacy rate and many can create documents themselves, Scriveners often find themselves serving the nobility and upper classes for ghostwriting. In such cases, the Scrivener's job is to record the content conveyed orally by the client in beautiful handwriting and well-structured prose. Scriveners are also well-versed in aristocratic roundabout expressions and metaphors, so they may be relied upon when common citizens need to send letters or documents to the upper class. Writing love letters between people of different social standings is one such example. Scriveners who are proficient in multiple languages can easily expand their work opportunities through translation jobs, significantly increasing their remuneration. As a result, many Scriveners are multilingual, often having Sage class. Furthermore, as Scriveners are not infrequently asked to create fraudulent documents without their knowledge, many of them also acquire the Official skill (see p. 94) as a complementary ability.
workSkillDescription.storyteller-skill: The "Storyteller skill" is a work skill that represents proficiency in various stories and the art of narrating them. Those who use this skill to earn money and make a living are called "storytellers." After the fall of the Magitech Civilization due to the Diabolic Triumph, entertainment for the masses drastically decreased, forcing people to focus on day-to-day survival. In this context, the stories told by Storytellers have become one of the few forms of entertainment for people. The content varies widely, ranging from tales of the age of mythology to heroic sagas surrounding the Diabolic Triumph and stories of dream-like countries filled with the splendor of the lost Magitech Civilization Period. Skilled Storytellers memorize a wide variety of stories and can skillfully adapt them according to their target audience. They also possess unique techniques in their narrative art, being able to use multiple voices to portray different characters. Storytellers sometimes double as Bards, narrating stories from other countries, recent events, or the outcomes of dangerous adventures they've actually experienced, all set to music. Exceptional Storytellers may be invited to royal courts or wealthy households to showcase their narrative skills. Conversely, they might also be commissioned to tell stories glorifying the achievements of royal families or those in power to the public. Although often thought of as mere entertainers for the masses, their influence is not small. Particularly skilled Storytellers can incite the people to overthrow nations or provoke conflicts between countries. With their narrative skills, they can even elevate unknown adventurers to the status of heroes. Storyteller: The Source of Information. In an era where information is hard to come by, people often believe the stories and tales of other lands that Storytellers convey as truth. Some in power take advantage of this, while others crack down to prevent the spread of unnecessary information.
workSkillDescription.dancer-skill: "Dancer skill (Dancer)" is a work skill for performing dances. Those who have mastered this skill and make a living from it are primarily called Dancers. Dancers are called upon to liven up soirées, banquets, and festivals, where they showcase their skills. They are often requested to perform group dances, and it's common to see those who have formed groups from the start. Dancers frequently form traveling troupes of Entertainers with those who can play instruments, such as Bards (see CR II, p. 100), or those who can sing, like Singers (see p. 84). These troupes tour various locations, typically using the festival season as a guide.
workSkillDescription.doctor-skill: "Doctor skill (Doctor)" is a work skill for acquiring academic medical knowledge. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Doctors. Since a Doctor's knowledge is primarily limited to treatment with pharmaceuticals, the general public often considers treatment at temples to be more effective and reliable than that provided by Doctors. Doctors mainly treat patients through diagnosis and prescription, so skilled Doctors possess a wide variety of herbs, potions, and medicinal products in large quantities.
workSkillDescription.apothecary-skill: "Apothecary skill (Pharmacist)" is a work skill for preparing various drugs and medicinal compounds. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Pharmacists. As a legitimate occupation, Pharmacists produce herbal remedies and potions, which they supply to apothecaries, adventurers' guilds, and doctors. However, since Pharmacists technically have the ability to compound drugs and addictive narcotics, it's not uncommon for them to be approached by the underworld. Because a Pharmacist's knowledge often involves matters of life and death in various ways, it is kept secret.
workSkillDescription.perfumer-skill: "Perfumer skill" is a work skill for creating and matching perfumes and fragrances. Those who have mastered this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Perfumers. The Perfumer is a work skill that primarily serves the upper class, such as the wealthy, and they typically make their living in urban areas. The products that Perfumers deal in are perfumes, incense, scent sachets, scented gloves, and the like, all of which have the upper class who care about their appearance as the main consumer base. There are also quite a few nobles who collect fragrances and aromatic woods as a hobby. Regarding incense, it is widely used in temple rituals, soirées, feasts and festivals, and ceremonial occasions, making it familiar even to the general public. The fragrances handled by Perfumers are either made using expensive aromatic woods or, if not, are produced using secret recipes, making them all luxury items.
workSkillDescription.prestidigitator-skill: The "Prestidigitator skill (Magician)" is a work skill that involves performing magic tricks and arts through sleight of hand rather than actual magic. It is a form of entertainment produced through excellent dexterity and meticulous training, and those who can earn money with this skill are called "Magicians". The main focus is on sleight of hand using cards, balls, and coins, while large-scale performances using big boxes or stage equipment are rarely seen. At most, people might see tricks like releasing doves from a hat, turning a cane into a bouquet of flowers, or quick-change Pickpocket acts within a cloak. However, skilled Magicians can create more spectacular shows using multiple assistants, and with enough experience, they can even manage stage shows. For the people of Raxia, who lead daily lives with few entertainments, magic shows are considered one of the finest forms of entertainment. Moreover, when combined with other forms of entertainment, such as storytelling, it can further enhance the excitement. To the common people, a masterful magic performance is indistinguishable from real magic. While those with Wizard-Type Classes don't need to check to realize it's different from the magic they use, figuring out the tricks and mechanisms behind it is not easy. As a result, it's possible for them to mistake it for magic from other systems (or unknown magic).
workSkillDescription.painter-skill: "Painter skill (Artist)" is a work skill for creating paintings. Those who have mastered this skill and make a living from it are mainly called Artists. Artists set up workshops, prepare their own pigments and canvases, and make a living by painting commissioned works for clients. Colored paintings are unique works of art and luxury items, so Artists' clientele is primarily composed of the wealthy and upper classes. Books that extensively use colored paintings are limited to sacred texts found in large temples, and such books are extremely expensive. In the current world of Raxia, printing technology is not very advanced, so the colored paintings that ordinary citizens can see are limited to things like temple murals. Only skilled Artists or a select few Artists with exceptional talent are entrusted with the creation of such murals.
workSkillDescription.heraldist-skill: The "Heraldist skill (Heraldic Scholar)" is a work skill used to memorize and understand the coats of arms of royal families, nobles, and powerful clans. As it is taboo for different families to have overlapping coats of arms, this skill is also relied upon when creating new heraldry. Those who make this their profession are called Heraldic Scholars. The origins of Heraldic Scholars are said to date back to the Ancient Magic Civilization era, which is believed to have perished 3,000 years ago, during the time when powerful wizard-kings held sway. It is thought to have begun with the identification of coats of arms representing the connections between wizard-kings and their subordinates and has since been passed down through the ages as a field of study compiling knowledge about nations and bloodlines. Following the Diabolic Triumph, these bloodlines either died out or became scattered, so they are no longer as highly valued. Nevertheless, there is still a certain demand for it, such as investigating the origins of coats of arms discovered in ruins or verifying the claims of those who profess to be legitimate royalty.
workSkillDescription.musician-skill: The "Musician skill (Musician)" is a work skill for playing instruments and performing known musical pieces. Those who have acquired this skill and make a living from it are mainly called Musicians. Musicians showcase their melodies using instruments when livening up festivals and events held in temples and settlements, enhancing the atmosphere of upper-class parties and tea gatherings, or when called upon to attract customers to shops. Musicians who primarily perform at festivals and events may also belong to a traveling Entertainer troupe. It's not uncommon for nobles and others to employ their own exclusive Musicians. The Bard class (see CR II, p. 100) can also perform the Melody Comprehension check and Instrument Performance check that are possible with the Musician skill.
workSkillDescription.librarian-skill: "Librarian skill (Librarian)" is a work skill for managing archives that contain numerous books. Those who have acquired this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Librarians. Librarians are employed in large archives, whether private or public. The work of a Librarian is diverse, starting with organizing the archive, creating catalogs of the collection, identifying candidates for new book purchases, managing book loans and deposits, sending reminders to those who haven't returned books, and making claims for compensation. In the current world of Raxia, printing and bookbinding technologies are not very advanced, so books are expensive items; in large archives, the proportion of handwritten, one-of-a-kind books is likely to be high, and for these unique and expensive books, they may even be chained to the shelves. Due to these circumstances, many books are not available for loan, and even for those that can be borrowed, a deposit must be paid. Access to archives is often limited to the owners and related parties, and even in archives open to the general public, most require registration with a fee after signing in. Because books are expensive and difficult to take out, archives typically provide desks for copying, and the rental of these desks is often charged as well, leading to a general perception among ordinary citizens that archives are "places that cost money no matter what".
workSkillDescription.restorer-skill: "Restorer skill (Restorer)" is a work skill primarily used for repairing and restoring artifacts from the Magitech Civilization Period. Those who make a living from this work are called Restorers. Artifacts from the Magitech Civilization Period (such as Magitech) excavated from ruins are quite durable, and many can still be used if repaired even today. This skill involves repairing such items and restoring them to their original usable state. Magitech restoration is carried out by the Institute Of Magitechnology, and in cities with many Magitech Civilization ruins and numerous adventurers, there are also individuals who set up shops to repair Magitech. Note that everything that can be done with the Restorer skill can be substituted by the [Artificer] class.
workSkillDescription.linguist-skill: "Linguist skill (Interpreter)" is a work skill that represents the ability to handle multiple languages and mediate between people who cannot communicate with each other. Language professionals who bridge linguistic gaps in important settings are called Interpreters. Many Humanoids can converse (or read and write) in trade common, regional dialect, or race language. However, communication often fails due to location differences, vast cultural gaps even when speaking the same language, or nuances in regional dialects or race languages that cannot be fully expressed in trade common. The role of an Interpreter is to fully convey these nuances and support smooth discussions. Therefore, Interpreters are required to be proficient not only in multiple languages but also in knowledge of different cultures.
workSkillDescription.official-skill: "Official skill" is a work skill for understanding and navigating organizational rules and norms, particularly within national and local government administrations. This skill involves bridging procedures and contracts between the public or external parties and the organization, conducting negotiations, and maintaining administrative functions. Professionals who have mastered this skill are typically known as "Government Officials." Government Officials' work encompasses managing incoming documents, ensuring the accuracy of organizational rules and norms, and overseeing accounting and budget management within their institution. Their duties may also include interpreting instructions from superiors or external clients, translating these directives into practical measures, and developing detailed regulations. At its core, the role of Government Officials revolves around implementing, representing, mediating, or maintaining instructions from others. As such, they do not typically initiate new plans or establish regulations independently.
workSkillDescription.orator-skill: The "Orator skill" is a work skill for delivering eloquent speeches. It excels at speaking in front of people, persuading, inspiring, and guiding them. It is called "Orator" because it is useful for persuading large crowds, such as in election speeches or court defenses. In the current world of Raxia, the existence of electoral and judicial systems varies by nation. In countries where such systems are established, this skill would be highly useful as a profession. Even in nations without these systems, there are numerous situations where it can be valuable, such as conveying royal decrees to the public, inspiring soldiers before battle, or calming people's panic during sudden attacks. Many nobles, military officers, and high-ranking officials are Orators, using their skills to proclaim their legitimacy and justice and to guide people.
workSkillDescription.cleric-skill: "Cleric skill (Cleric)" is a work skill for worshipping divine entities such as gods and fulfilling daily duties in temples and the like. Those who acquire this skill and regularly work in temples are called Clerics. Many of those who have heard the voice of a god and acquired the Priest class become Clerics and serve in temples. Conversely, being a Cleric does not necessarily mean one has acquired the Priest class. Cleric skill is useful for smoothly executing sacred rituals, festivals, etiquette, and daily tasks in temples. They are well-versed in scriptures, myths, legends, and narratives and excel at presenting these to the public. Listening to the confessions and concerns of believers is also part of their job, and they are skilled in the art of conversation that alleviates spiritual suffering. Through political maneuvering within the temple, those with low (or no) Priest class may sometimes advance due to their proficiency in Cleric skill. While this can be necessary for the organization in some cases, it can also lead to corruption within the organization if the position is abused. Most people who make their living as Clerics reside within temples or similar facilities or in lodgings around them. Their lives are integrated with the temple, and they dedicate most of their time to faith in and service to their deity. Of course, preaching to believers and hearing confessions are also part of this service. They also engage in charitable activities such as providing meals for the poor and are generally known as allies of the weak. For these reasons, they are socially trusted, and corrupt or malicious Clerics are rarely seen (though it cannot be said they don't exist at all).
workSkillDescription.courtesan-skill: "Courtesan skill (Escort)" is a work skill that involves becoming a companion, akin to a mistress, for the upper class, nobility, or wealthy individuals in special positions. This skill is used to please the partner, act as a confidant, and sometimes even create and recite poetry or stories. Those who utilize this skill to spend time as a companion to such high-status individuals are called "Escorts." Escorts are clearly different from common Harlots/Gigolos. In most cases, they form long-term relationships rather than one-night stands. Their compensation is also substantial, often being provided with special residences or personal rooms in their employer's mansion or villa. Escorts are naturally physically attractive, skilled in conversation, and adept at captivating their partners. Moreover, beyond physical relationships, they possess the education to converse with upper-class individuals, are well-versed in makeup and fashion, and are trained in etiquette. They are not merely outlets for sexual gratification but rather unofficial lovers to their employers, advisors, and sometimes even living beautiful accessories. In some cases, they are acknowledged by the partner and may even accompany their employer to prominent places such as banquets or theaters. Depending on the circumstances, having an excellent Escort can be seen as a status symbol for the upper class, and some Escorts can manipulate those in power with their beauty and intelligence. However, their origins are often of common or lower birth, so standing out too much can be dangerous. Skilled Escorts are adept at striking this balance, generally behaving in a way that doesn't draw negative attention.
workSkillDescription.soldier-skill: "Soldier skill" is a work skill that represents the various abilities required of a Soldier belonging to the military. It mainly represents proficiency in discipline as a soldier, group actions and marches, and military common sense, while combat prowess itself is measured by Warrior-Type Classes. Those who possess this skill and belong to combat groups such as the military are called Soldiers. Soldier skill is learned to efficiently operate combat groups, and many (or all) city guards, sentries, and knight orders have also acquired it. As the level increases, it becomes possible to command more subordinates, and at level 10, one can call themselves a "General" (whether this is backed by actual experience is another matter). In many regions of Raxia that are just beginning to recover from the chaos following the Diabolic Triumph, nations still remain small in scale. Their populations range from a few thousand to, at most, tens of thousands. The number of Soldiers constituting the military rarely exceeds 5% of the total population, so the total number of Soldiers in a single country is only a few dozen to a few hundred (only exceptionally large countries have thousands of Soldiers). Of course, during wartime, reserve troops and conscripts other than those regularly maintained are mobilized, temporarily increasing the scale. However, such temporary troops are either low in training or mere amateurs in numbers and are poor as a fighting force. Trained Soldiers can organize a motley crew and lead them to act in an organized manner. It is an important role of Soldiers not only to fight themselves but also to lead groups.
workSkillDescription.nurse-skill: "Nurse skill (Nurse)" is a work skill for nursing injured or sick people. Those who have acquired this skill and made it their profession are mainly called Nurses. In most cases, the main duties of a Nurse include assisting priests and doctors in temples or infirmaries, attending to patients according to treatment instructions, and maintaining a clean environment for patients.
workSkillDescription.noble-skill: "Noble skill" is a work skill for maintaining the dignity of royalty and nobility and for behaving in a noble manner. Even if not born into nobility, those who become part of the upper class, people in power, or wealthy individuals can acquire noble skills. The typical practitioners of this skill are called Aristocrats. Those who do not hold noble titles are referred to as celebrities. After the fall of the Magitech Civilization, many nations established monarchies, and within them exists a Noble skill. These people are required to have dignified behavior and elegant manners to demonstrate that they are different from the common people. Those who have mastered this skill at a high level will possess an undeniable aura and make a strong impression on those who see them. Of course, the required etiquette and attitudes differ depending on the country and region. Skilled practitioners of the Noble skill can learn about such etiquette and manners of the places they visit in advance or quickly discern them on-site, avoiding rudeness and impropriety. Conversely, Aristocrats from remote areas or the countryside may have this skill remain at a low level without development. Even in republican nations, some people in power and certain wealthy individuals may acquire this skill. For those who stand above others, maintaining noble behavior is always important and contributes to the persuasiveness of their statements.
workSkillDescription.butler-skill: "Butler skill (Steward)" is a work skill required to manage household staff such as maids and servants in noble or upper-class households, ensuring that everything runs smoothly for the master. Those who make this their profession are called Stewards. A Steward plays a crucial role in supporting the master, with daily duties including understanding the schedule and making necessary preparations. It is also the Steward's responsibility to oversee the reception and guidance of guests. If one becomes the Head Steward, they are also tasked with accurately announcing the names of visiting dignitaries to the master. They may live in the master's residence, sharing meals and lodging. It is a position akin to that of a secretary, playing a vital role as the master's right hand.
workSkillDescription.explorer-skill: The "Explorer skill" is a skill possessed by those who actively traverse unknown places. The main difference from adventurers is that it assumes exploration activities do not involve combat. Those who acquire this skill and regularly go on explorations are called Explorers. Explorers aim to leave town and venture into the wilderness, with the primary goal of discovering new paths and routes to traverse it. Some may even search for ruins of past civilizations known only in records. Explorers also enjoy climbing mountains that no one has summited before or visiting uninhabited islands. Among Explorers, some make a living as "finders" who discover unexplored ruins. It's not uncommon for them to also work as adventurers. If combat with monsters is not a consideration, skilled Explorers can become even more adept at outdoor activities than adventurers. For adventurers, finders who can inform them about unexplored ruins or generally unknown routes are familiar figures. Many of these roles are filled by Explorers, who explore the areas around inhabited zones, discover such places, and provide information to adventurers. Most of those who make a living as finders are individuals who didn't choose the path of an adventurer, either because they lack fighting abilities or have personalities unsuited for life-and-death situations. Exceptional finders possess a unique intuition, like a sixth sense, allowing them to discover new routes or unexplored ruins, sometimes amassing great wealth in the process. There are also Explorers who contract with specific Adventurers Guild Branches or individual adventurers, venturing out on explorations day and night.
workSkillDescription.signalman-skill: The "Signalman skill" is a work skill that involves using flags held in both hands to communicate with someone at a distance. Those who graduate from the training school of the Kingslay Republic of Iron and Steel, join the Railroad Guild, and support the smooth operation of railways by communicating via flag signals on magic-powered trains, at stations, and at switching points are called "signalmen" or "flag signalmen". During the late Magitech Civilization Period, which was the golden age of magic-powered trains, signalmen had become obsolete due to the existence of magitech, which allowed free communication over long distances. However, after the "Diabolic Triumph" during the reconstruction period, these means of communication could no longer be reproduced. Yet, long-distance communication was still necessary for the smooth operation of railways. As a result, a flag signal system capable of complex communication, almost comparable to a language, was developed based on the simple flag signals used on trading ships. Therefore, to become a signalman, one must undergo several years of vocational training at the Railroad Guild's training school in Kingslay. While scholarship programs exist, it's generally difficult without time and financial flexibility. Particularly skilled individuals can also learn combat techniques and become "senior signalmen," who are deployed to frontier switching points, routes passing through areas infested with Barbarous, and the forefront of new route development. The minimum requirement for a senior signalman is Signalman level 10, in addition to [Artificer] and [Marksman] skills at level 7 or higher. Besides the Railroad Guild, signalmen are also employed by sea-going vessels and flying magic ships for communication with ports. Many of these signalmen are seconded from the Railroad Guild, but there are also those who have quit, dropped out of training school, or learned on the job. Kingslay's flag signals have a complexity comparable to a full-fledged language. Through subtle differences in flag angles and waving patterns, those who have mastered the skill can freely converse over long distances as far as they can be visually recognized.
workSkillDescription.tour-guide-skill: The "Tour Guide skill (Tour Guide)" is a work skill for leading and guiding travelers. Those who have acquired this skill and made it their profession are mainly called "Tour Guides". Tour Guides can guide travelers, including peddlers and pilgrims, using their knowledge of geography, history, influential people, and shops in the areas they have previously studied. Tour guides have various knowledge about the areas they have researched and prepared for, and they also have some knowledge of the monsters that may be encountered in those areas to keep travelers away from danger. It is said that experienced tour guides with knowledge of various regions can also accompany clients on inter-city travel and be responsible for guiding them to each destination along the way. For each level acquired in the Tour Guide skill, the Tour Guide can choose one "city or settlement" and gain knowledge of the area within a one-day walking distance from that city, treating it as "acquired guiding knowledge". The Tour Guide check can be used to determine if a Tour Guide knows general information about places where they have acquired guiding knowledge. Additionally, the Tour Guide check can be used to check if they have knowledge about monsters encountered in places where a Tour Guide has acquired guiding knowledge (for details, refer to Monster Knowledge check in CR I, p. 382). However, the Tour Guide check cannot reveal a monster's "weak point". Even with an automatic success or any high Success Value, it only allows PCs to reference the monster's data. For a character who has acquired both the [Sage] class and Tour Guide skill and whose Tour Guide skill level is higher, checks are basically made using the Tour Guide skill. However, if applying the roll to a [Sage] class check would result in a Success Value equal to or higher than the monster's weakness, they can discern the monster's weak point and apply its effect. This also applies to automatic successes.
workSkillDescription.tamer-skill: The "Tamer skill (Animal Trainer)" allows one to tame livestock and wild animals, making livestock follow detailed commands and wild animals obey simple orders to some extent. Those who possess this skill and make a living from it are called "Animal Trainers". Common livestock used for riding and pulling carts include cattle, horses, and camels. Dogs are typically used as livestock for hunting and guarding assistance. Once tamed by an Animal Trainer, livestock can understand and execute simple instructions or commands even without the trainer present. These trained animals will likely work devotedly for jockeys or owners who treat them kindly and affectionately, even if they are not Animal Trainers themselves (subject to GM's discretion). Some Animal Trainers use the Tamer skill to train wild animals for performances in shows or street acts. In the context of the Tamer skill, wild animals refer to monsters in the "Animal" category, excluding livestock. Wild animals trained by an Animal Trainer can suppress violent behavior and act docile when the trainer is nearby. If given treats as rewards, they will likely follow very simple instructions or commands. Many Animal Trainers use the Tamer skill to train livestock for riding and pulling carts, as well as to assist in hunting and guarding. The Time Required for a Training check is approximately "monster level squared + 2 days" (determined by GM decision). If the Training check is successful, the taming of the Animal is complete. When an Animal Trainer leads multiple trained Animals at once, the limit for livestock is "Tamer skill level + 1" heads, and for wild Animals, it's "Tamer skill level × 2 (rounded up)" heads. Tamed livestock will obey Humanoid commands obediently even without the Animal Trainer present, as long as it's not during combat. Tamed wild Animals won't attack other creatures without permission if the Animal Trainer is within 30m, and during non-combat situations, they will follow the Animal Trainer's commands for about 6 rounds if given food (worth about 1 gamel). In combat, tamed livestock will try to flee, while wild Animals will either run away or attack someone other than the Animal Trainer (roll 1d: 1-3 they try to flee, 4-5 they attack enemies, 6 they attack the Animal Trainer's allies). Once combat begins, the Animal Trainer cannot control how wild Animals behave (GM decides). In other words, unlike the [Rider] class (see CR III, p. 84), when handling Mounts, the Tamer skill cannot freely and completely control animals to follow orders. Even outside of combat, it would be difficult for the Animal Trainers to control tamed Animals in emergency situations like fires or natural disasters.
workSkillDescription.shepherd-skill: "Shepherd skill (Shepherd)" is a work skill for livestock farming in pastures. Those who possess this skill and make it their livelihood are called "Shepherds". Shepherds are closely involved in all aspects of livestock's lives from birth to death, including managing grazing, feeding and cleaning in barns, collecting and storing fodder, assisting with livestock births, milking, shearing, and harvesting eggs. In the world of Raxia, common livestock used in animal husbandry are primarily docile, herbivorous animals. Specifically, these include cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, pheasants, ducks, horses, and camels. It's also common for Shepherds to keep dogs to assist them, as well as cats and weasels to protect barns and feed stores from rodents. When the purpose of animal husbandry includes milk and egg production, managing livestock births also becomes an important job for Shepherds.
workSkillDescription.hunter-skill: "Hunter skill" is a work skill for roaming the wilderness to hunt prey that serves as materials for food and clothing. Those who make a living by selling such prey are called Hunters. Hunters are among the few people, aside from adventurers, who base their activities outside of town. Hunters leave town in search of prey, sometimes wandering the wilderness for days. They primarily rely on trapping, but they also acquire the [Marksman] class and use bows or sometimes guns to take down their prey. They possess detailed knowledge about their hunting grounds and are well-versed in the animals and plants that become their prey.
workSkillDescription.farmer-skill: "Farmer skill" is a work skill for managing crop production. Those who possess this skill and make it their livelihood are called Farmhands. In the world of Raxia, more than half of the Humanoid general population is born in agricultural areas and engaged in farming. Therefore, the Farmer's skill can be said to be the most popular work skill among the general population. Farmhands produce various crops throughout the year. There are hardly any Farmhands who continue to grow the same crop throughout the year. There are two main reasons why Farmhands grow multiple types of crops. The first reason is the existence of seasonal changes. Depending on the region, most farmlands are affected by seasons and the types and range of crops that can be grown change throughout the year, making it impossible to continue growing the same crop. The second reason is to avoid a decrease in production due to continuous cropping damage (continuing to grow the same crop depletes the soil). Therefore, crop rotation is practiced where different crops are grown on the same land in the following year, or fallow is implemented where grain fields are rested from winter to spring and flowers that become fertilizer are planted.
workSkillDescription.miner-skill: "Miner skill" is a work skill for drilling and extracting mineral resources. Those engaged in this hard labor are called Miners. In the world of Raxia, female Miners are not uncommon, and they are treated equally in many workplaces. Mountains with mineral veins are often under state control, with mining guilds established to manage the mountains and their excavation. Mining guilds are responsible for excavation planning and hiring Miners, and Miners can work in the mines by registering with the guild. On the other hand, prospectors who discover mineral veins in the mountains without mining guilds and aim for a quick fortune also (unsurprisingly) acquire Miner skills. Additionally, there are individuals, organizations, and local governments that own hidden mines outside of state control, and cases where they hire Miners with checkered pasts or force abducted individuals into labor. Dwarves, being short in stature, able to see in the dark, sturdy, and strong, are considered natural-born Miners. In fact, Dwarves tend to have an affinity for metals and precious stones, and many work as Miners.
workSkillDescription.lumberjack-skill: The "Lumberjack skill (Logger)" is a work skill for felling trees with axes and saws and processing timber. Those who live near forests and make their living from forestry are generally called Loggers. When felling, a Logger first determines the safe direction for the tree to fall, then makes a horizontal cut on the opposite side, followed by an angled cut about 30 degrees from the horizontal plane. This is called the undercut, which controls the direction and speed of the tree's fall. It's rare for Loggers to work alone; they usually operate in groups. Many live on the outskirts of towns or villages, near forests, making a living by felling trees and processing timber. These Logger groups often consist of no more than a dozen or so people; in some cases, there's a division between those who work at sawmills and those who do the felling. Logger groups of several hundred people also move through forests seasonally, engaging in large-scale forestry operations. These groups are known for building large camps on the forest edge during the logging season (from late winter to early summer). These mobile camps, called Lumberjack camps, also house the Loggers' families, taking on the appearance of small settlements.
workSkillDescription.weatherman-skill: The "Weatherman skill (Meteorologist)" is a skill for predicting weather based on various signs. While long-term forecasts are difficult, it's possible to achieve a certain degree of accuracy for predictions up to about half a day in advance. Weather is an important factor for fishermen and farmers, making those with this skill highly valued. Weather information is also crucial for nations and armies, and skilled Meteorologists are often employed by governments. Meteorologists predict weather by observing all kinds of signs and information, including cloud conditions, humidity, and the state of plants and animals, as well as their own experience and intuition. Skilled Meteorologists can accurately forecast short-term weather and, in some cases, even predict large-scale weather changes (such as typhoons, prolonged rain, or tornadoes) in the medium to long term (from a few days to about a week).
workSkillDescription.sailor-skill: "Sailor skill" is a skill necessary for operating a ship. It mainly refers to those engaged in water/maritime transportation as boatmen or sailors, and such individuals are called Sailors. The capabilities of Sailor skill are extensive. Those with low skill levels become general crew members, while those who excel become captains. This skill covers everything from small boats that can be operated by individuals to large sailing ships operated by many crew members and even flying magic ships. As the level increases, one can specialize, making it possible to become an even more proficient sailor by focusing on specific areas.
workSkillDescription.navigator-skill: "Navigator skill (Navigator)" is a work skill for safely guiding large ships or flying magic ships to their destination by referencing sea charts, maps, ocean currents, clouds, stars, and land areas. Those who use this skill to work on ships are called Navigators. When traveling across vast seas or skies, losing one's current position can be fatal. Therefore, Navigators plan voyages and flights, constantly verify their current position, and guide the ship. Even without being on a ship, this skill is beneficial for long-distance travel on foot or by carriage, as it allows one to read maps and determine their current location by referencing terrain and stars. About the Cartography check: with this check, a Navigator can read sea charts and estimate travel distances and the time required.
workSkillDescription.fisherman-skill: "Fisherman skill" is a work skill related to techniques and knowledge for acquiring fish and other marine products. Those who make a living by directly selling marine products or wholesaling them to markets are called Fishermen. They are skilled in the knowledge of prey and fishing grounds in rivers and seas, handling small boats, and going out fishing daily as long as the weather is not bad. If you become an experienced fisherman, you can also venture out to more distant seas.

witch-doctor-skill.prayer-judgment-check: This is a skill check to perform a prayer ritual on one specific person as a target to judge the diseases and misfortunes affecting the target person. Succeeding in the Prayer Judgment Check reveals the negative effects the target person is suffering from, related to diseases, monsters, poisons, curses, and persistent magical effects. This determines what kind of negative influences the targeted person is experiencing and from what sources. For diseases, similar to a Pathology Check (see CR I, p. 107), Medicine Man can learn the nature of the disease, its progression, and treatment methods from the patient's condition. For rare diseases, the Target Number becomes higher. Regarding monsters, Medicine Man gains knowledge like a Monster Knowledge Check (see CR I, p. 108) about monsters negatively affecting the target. However, it differs in that the Prayer Judgment Check must be performed in advance rather than during an encounter with the monster, and the monster's weak points cannot be discerned. For poisons, it determines whether poison or drugs have been mixed into objects or food and drink that the target regularly comes into contact with. If this check succeeds and poison is discovered, you also learn the antidote. For identifying persistent effects such as curses or magic, the Success Value of that effect becomes the Target Number for the Prayer Judgment Check. The Time Required for the Prayer Judgment Check increases the longer the target person has been continuously affected by negative influences and may exceed 1 hour in some cases (GM's discretion).
witch-doctor-skill.folk-medicine-check: The Folk Medicine check is a skill check used by the Medicine Man to apply symptomatic treatment to patients affected by a disease or poison, using knowledge gained about that disease or poison. Before performing a Folk Medicine check, the Medicine Man needs to know what disease or poison is affecting the patient, usually through a Prayer Judgment check or similar means. The Target Number for a Folk Medicine check is the same as the Fortitude or Willpower Target Number of the disease or poison. If Medicine Man wants to perform a Folk Medicine check on multiple people, the Target Number increases by +2 for each additional patient. If the Folk Medicine check is successful, for the next day, the patient's "HP and MP reduction" and "skill check penalties" caused by the disease or poison are halved (rounded up), the progression speed of the disease or poison is halved, and if a Fortitude or Willpower check is required against that disease or poison, the patient receives a +2 bonus. The Time Required for a Folk Medicine check increases the longer the target person has been continuously affected by the negative effects, typically requiring 3-8 hours (GM's discretion). The Folk Medicine check includes time for gathering herbs and other materials used for treatment from the surrounding forests, hills, and fields. If a Folk Medicine check is performed in an urban area with little natural environment, it incurs a -4 penalty, and the Time Required is doubled.

waiter-waitress-skill.table-service-check: This is a check for performing "table service," which involves smoothly taking orders, communicating, serving, and clearing tables without causing stress to customers or the kitchen staff while maintaining a proper dining environment. For Table Service, if successful on a Table Service check with a Target Number of 10, Waiter/Waitress can perform table service without issues for up to "Waiter/Waitress skill level x 4 people" simultaneously. For each additional customer beyond this, increase the Target Number of the Table Service check by +1. The Table Service check is performed in advance after determining the Time Required for table service. The GM sets the Target Number based on the maximum number of customers Table Service is responsible for during any given time within the required time and then conducts the skill check.
waiter-waitress-skill.rumor-knowledge-check: The Rumor Knowledge check is a check to recall rumors heard from various individuals in the nearest settlement to Table Service's current location. The Rumor Knowledge check can only be used for knowledge likely to be obtained near a settlement (GM's discretion) where Table Service has succeeded in at least one Table Service check. With a Rumor Knowledge check, they can gain general knowledge about the vicinity of the settlement, similar to an Insight check (see CR I, p. 106). Additionally, with a Rumor Knowledge check, they gain knowledge about monsters seen in the vicinity of the settlement, similar to a Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 109). However, it differs in that they cannot discern the monster's weak points. The Rumor Knowledge check is modified based on the duration of stay in the settlement: a -1 penalty for a "stay of 1-7 days" and no modifier for a "stay of 8 days or more." Also, if Table Service has not succeeded in a Table Service check in that settlement for more than one month (30 days), the duration of stay in that settlement is reset to "0 days" (checks cannot be made at 0 days).

gardener-skill.landscaping-check: This skill check determines whether you can make appropriate judgments regarding garden design, construction, and management. As the garden space expands and the cost increases, the Target Number for the landscaping check also increases. If multiple Groundskeepers manage a vast property, the Target Number for the landscaping check performed by each Groundskeeper decreases significantly. Additionally, design or construction completion requires several days to several months (determined by GM judgment based on scale and area).
gardener-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-plant: When encountering a monster classified as "Plant", this check determines whether the Groundskeeper has knowledge about that monster. It is treated the same as a normal Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 109), except that it is limited to valid monster classifications.
gardener-skill.herbology-check-limited-to-plants: Identify the effects of medicinal herbs. Alternatively, determine whether food or drink contains plant-based poisons or herbs. If this check succeeds and a plant-based poison is discovered, the Groundskeeper also learns how to neutralize it.

carpenter-skill.construction-check-wood: This is a check for constructing buildings, bridges, etc., using wood. Drafting is required to perform this check. Cooperation among multiple people can shorten the Time Required.
carpenter-skill.drafting-check: This is a check for drawing blueprints of structures. If successful, Woodworkers can create structurally sound blueprints. It can also be used as a building-specific version of the Cartography check (see CR I, p. 107) and Engineering check (see CR I, p. 108).
carpenter-skill.wood-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if the Woodworker has knowledge about the target wood. If successful, they understand the characteristics, processing methods, and prices of wood.

gangster-skill.appraise-check: When performing this check as a Gangster skill, similar to the Scout class, the Gangster can only determine the treasure's value (base price).
gangster-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-human: While the target is limited to Humanoids, it is the same as the Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108).
gangster-skill.intimidation-check: This is a check to intimidate the opponent and break their will by using voice volume and tone. It basically becomes a comparison of Success Values against the opponent's Willpower (see CR I, p. 110). If they fail the Willpower check, they will feel that the intimidator is stronger (regardless of actual game data strength). There are no restrictions on how they react after that.

gambler-skill.expression-manipulation-check: This is a check to hide true emotions and create any desired expression. It basically becomes a comparison of Success Values with the opponent's Detect check (see CR I, p. 111). If the check is successful, the Gambler can hide their true feelings and make others believe they have different emotions. If they fail, their true emotions will be read.
gambler-skill.sleight-of-hand-check: This is a check for manipulating cards, dice, coins, etc., with quick finger, hand, or arm movements. At a simple level, the Gambler can perform impressive card shuffles or coin tosses. More difficult tasks include cheating actions during a game, such as swapping cards or tiles or manipulating dice rolls right in front of their opponent. Cheating is basically a comparison of Success Values against the opponent's Notice check (see CR I, p. 111). If the check succeeds, the cheating goes undetected.
gambler-skill.gambling-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine whether the Gambler is familiar with the rules, winning strategies, and key tactics of the gambling game being played. Unless it's a game of pure chance, if they're not cheating, it becomes a comparison of Success Values between the Gambler and their opponent's Gambling Knowledge check. If the GM prepares an actual mini-game to recreate a gambling scene, it's advisable to set a Target Number and provide strategy tips or apply favorable modifiers based on the Success Value of Gambling Knowledge.

gravekeeper-skill.gravedigger-check: This is a check for digging a hole to completely bury the corpse (coffin). A depth of about 1.6 to 2m is required, and it takes about an hour using a two-handed shovel. The Target Number increases depending on the hardness of the soil.
gravekeeper-skill.gravekeeper-funeral-check: This is a skill check for overseeing funerals, arranging tombstones and coffins, assisting with priestly rituals, and properly burying the deceased. It can also be used for managing cemeteries or planning expansions of underground burial sites. The Target Number for the Gravekeeper Funeral check increases when conducting multiple funerals simultaneously or when there are many funeral attendees. The Target Number decreases when multiple Gravekeepers perform the funeral or burial. Time Required varies depending on the scale of the funeral (determined by GM's judgment). It includes time for negotiating with priests and preparing the funeral according to the wishes of the deceased and their family, as well as in accordance with their faith.
gravekeeper-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-undea: This is a check to determine if the Gravekeeper has knowledge about a monster encountered that falls under the "Category: Undead". It is treated the same as a normal Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108), except that the effective monster categories are limited.

carriage-driver-skill.carriage-operation-check: This is a skill check for giving appropriate commands to draft animals such as horses and maneuvering the carriage according to the Coachman's intentions. The Target Number increases as the size of the carriage grows larger, the number of draft animals increases, or the amount of cargo or passengers increases. The Time Required varies depending on the duration of the carriage's journey (GM's discretion). This Time Required includes the management of draft animals before the carriage's departure. Furthermore, the GM can request a Carriage Operation check from the Coachman when they determine that the Coachman needs to perform a sudden start, sudden stop, or any other special maneuver with the carriage.
carriage-driver-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-anima: This is a check to determine if the Coachman has knowledge about a monster when the encountered monster falls under the "Category: Animal" classification. It is treated similarly to a normal Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108), except that the valid monster categories are limited.

cook-skill.cooking-check: This is a check for combining ingredients and seasonings, cooking, and creating dishes. The higher the Success Value, the more delicious the dish becomes.
cook-skill.ingredient-appraisal-check: This is a check to judge the quality of ingredients, cooking methods, etc. If successful, the Chef can determine whether plants and animals are suitable as ingredients and if they're delicious and edible sections, appropriate cooking methods, medicinal effects, and food compatibility. It can also be used as a "food and cooking version" of the Herbology check (see CR I, p. 108).

tailor-skill.tailoring-check: This is a skill check for creating clothing. For custom-made items, measurements, and pattern making must be done in advance (takes a few additional hours). The Target Number increases as the area covering the body expands, using multiple types of fabric and thread. If the pattern is already determined and there are no decorations or pockets, the Target Number decreases. For simple fabric products with basic structures, such as undergarments or backpacks for ordinary citizens, production is possible within a few hours of the Time Required. For high-end formal wear using multiple types of fabric and featuring embroidery, the Time Required for production may take up to about a month.
tailor-skill.fabric-appraisal-check: This is a skill check for estimating the price of fabric products. The prices of fabric products used by adventurers (e.g., nonmetallic armor) can also be determined if this check is successful (decided at GM's discretion).

barber-skill.simple-surgery-check: This is a skill check for treating visible wounds through incision or suturing. The Target Number for the Simple Surgery check is "patient's current reduced HP + 7". If successful, the patient's HP recovers by an amount equal to the Barber skill level. If failed, the patient takes 1d points of fixed damage. The HP recovery effect from the Simple Surgery check can only be applied once per day for each patient. If a Pathology check (see CR I, p. 107) is performed on the patient before the Simple Surgery check and is successful, a +4 bonus is applied to the Simple Surgery check.
barber-skill.barbering-check: This is a skill check for grooming clients by styling or cutting hair, shaving beards, trimming eyebrows, applying makeup, and generally improving their appearance. Hair washing can also be included. The Target Number and Time Required for the Barbering check vary depending on the amount and quality of the client's hair (determined by the GM). Generally, clients with more hair will have a higher Target Number and longer Time Required.

housekeeper-skill.cooking-check: This is a check for combining ingredients and seasonings, cooking, and creating dishes. The higher the Success Value, the more delicious the dish becomes.
housekeeper-skill.cleaning-and-organizing-check: This is a check for cleaning and organizing a room. The higher the Success Value, the more beautiful the result. The necessary Target Number becomes higher in noble or upper-class households where discipline and beauty are required. The number of checks (Time Required) increases depending on the area to be cleaned and the initial level of dirtiness (messiness).
housekeeper-skill.etiquette-check: This is a check to see if the Housekeeper can follow the appropriate etiquette for the situation. It also checks whether they know (and can practice) the correct behavior and taboos.

performer-skill.performance-check: This is a check to showcase Entertainer talent in their area of expertise. For juggling, ringing, etc., use [Dexterity] as the Standard Value; for acrobatics, use [Agility]; for verbal performances, use [Intelligence]. For other types of performances, please consult with the GM to determine the appropriate ability. A higher Success Value allows a Entertainer to provide greater satisfaction to a larger audience. If the GM allows, Entertainer may use the Performance Check as a substitute for other checks (such as using acrobatics for Acrobatics Check or Tumble Check, using verbal performances for Speech Check (see p. 95), etc.). However, as it's not your specialty, please apply a penalty of about -2.

fortune-teller-skill.fortune-telling-check: This is a check to divine good omens using various instruments such as crystal balls, picture cards, turtle shells, animal bones, wooden sticks, and so on, with skill level bonuses. However, these are all small props for presentation and don't need to be special materials or magical items. Succeeding in this check allows a Psychic to perform fortune-telling with credible actions and derive the answer the other person desires (how to actually convey it depends on the Psychic). It's a technique for reading the other person's psychology and a skill for drawing out their true feelings. By succeeding in this check, a Psychic can resolve the other person's worries or encourage their determination through fortune-telling. Conversely, Psychic can also point out misfortune or mistakes to restrain or admonish their actions.

prostitute-skill.sexual-technique-check: This is a check to give sexual satisfaction to the target. The higher the Success Value, the higher the level of satisfaction.
prostitute-skill.seduction-check: This is a check to attract the target to Harlot/Gigolo through conversation, gestures, and sexual appeal. It's basically a comparison of Success Values against the target's Willpower (see CR I, p. 110). The higher the Success Value, the more attractive Harlot/Gigolo appear to the target, and the more captivated they become.
