It's also possible to perform a quick seduction, in which case the Time Required becomes 10 seconds (1 round), but Harlot/Gigolo receive a -4 penalty to their Success Value. The GM may apply bonus or penalty modifiers based on the target's preferences, considering gender, age, status, or appearance.

beggar-skill.tramp-check: This is a skill check to maintain an attitude conducive to receiving alms while finding suitable locations or routes to shops that are likely to give handouts. The Target Number for the Tramp check becomes lower in more populated urban areas (Target Number around 18 for populations under 3,000, around 14 for populations of 3,000 to 10,000, and around 10 for populations over 10,000), and also decreases during festivals or celebrations (Target Number is reduced by -1 to -4). Additionally, the Target Number increases as the Time Required is shortened. In situations where pedestrian traffic decreases, such as during high alert or bad weather, the Target Number increases (Target Number +1 to +4) and increases if another Tramp is visible (determined and decided by the GM). When performing a Tramp check, wearing accessories, clean clothes, or expensive clothing incurs a -4 penalty. Tramp can acquire "Success Value - Target Number" in gamel if successful in the Tramp check. They cannot perform another Tramp check in the same location for the rest of the day.

merchant-skill.price-insight-check: This is a check to set an appropriate price for purchased goods or materials and items obtained during adventures. Similar to the Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108) performed by the [Scout] class, the Merchant can discern the value (base price) by looking at the item. However, they cannot determine the specific abilities of the item (but they can understand what it's useful for).
merchant-skill.negotiation-check: This is a check used when buying and selling goods to buy low and sell high. Merchants perform this check when negotiating prices with business partners or when trying to buy below or sell above market price. When pricing with a Merchant, if either party is unsatisfied with the price, a Success Value comparison is conducted with their Negotiation checks (if tied, reroll). The price is determined by the stated value of the party who wins this check. In this case, the side that declares a price that is blatantly different from the market price will incur a penalty of -1 to -4 (negotiations that would incur a greater modification would likely break down without even a chance for a check). In scenes involving transactions between PCs or negotiations with important NPCs, it might be more immersive to progress the deal through conversation and roleplay rather than relying on this check.

manager-skill.appraise-check: If the Manager obtains a Success Value equal to or higher than the Target Number set for each item, they can determine the treasure's value (base price). With a Manager skill check, they cannot learn about usages or effects.
manager-skill.management-check: This is a check to plan for the appropriate allocation and operation of funds and personnel. The higher the Success Value, the more effectively the invested funds are utilized, and the more efficiently the employed personnel work without waste. This check can also be performed as an "Instant" action by taking a -4 penalty to the Success Value.
manager-skill.leadership-check: This is a check for giving subordinates instructions or orders and executing them quickly. While there's no need for a check when giving general instructions to trained subordinates, an appropriate Success Value becomes necessary in sudden situations, complex circumstances, or especially in scenarios where there's a potential risk to life. As the number of people being led increases, the required Success Value also becomes higher.

butcher-skill.meat-butchering-check: This is a check for cutting meat into easily cookable forms. If successful, a Butcher can cleanly and efficiently break down an animal carcass into primal cuts, sub-primal cuts, and retail cuts without waste.
butcher-skill.meat-processing-check: This is a check for processing meat into cured products using methods such as stuffing into casings, salt curing, or smoking. If successful, Butcher can create foods like sausages, bacon, or ham. This check can also be used to make preserved foods.

midwife-skill.childbirth-assistance-check: This is a skill level bonus check to assist pregnant women in childbirth and deliver of the baby. The Target Number for the Childbirth Assistance check is around 10 if the pregnant woman is of the same race as the Midwife and +4 if of a different race. If the Childbirth Assistance check is successful, the birth ends safely with no health effects on the mother and child. If the Childbirth Assistance check fails or if no Childbirth Assistance check was performed, the mother makes a Fortitude check with a Target Number of 10. If this Fortitude check succeeds, the birth ends with both mother and child healthy, but if it fails, the mother takes fixed damage equal to half her maximum HP (rounded up). On an automatic failure, both mother and baby additionally take 1d6 fixed damage to their HP. Note that if the baby is born a Nightmare, there is a -4 penalty to the Childbirth Assistance check. Regardless of the success or failure of the Childbirth Assistance check or the mother's Fortitude check, the mother takes an additional 2d fixed damage to her HP.
midwife-skill.disinfection-check: Targeting up to 5 people, Midwife disinfects the skin or affected areas with boiled and sterilized cloth, making them less susceptible to infectious diseases and toxic substances. Disinfected individuals receive a +1 bonus to Fortitude against poison type and disease, as well as for childbirth, for 6 hours after being disinfected.

teamster-skill.carrying-check: This is a check for efficiently carrying large, heavy, or both cargo. It allows Manual Laborer to carry loads that normally require 2-3 people to transport or quickly load large amounts of cargo onto ships or wagons. The higher the Success Value, the larger and greater quantities of cargo they can transport quickly.

armorer-skill.armor-enhancement-check: This is a check for adjusting armor to better suit the wearer or applying enhancements. Among armor enhancements, "Bulletproof" and "Extra Manatite Armor" can be performed. It's advisable to set the Target Number according to the difficulty and rank of the enhancement (see p. 108). When performing this check, Armor Craftsmen need to pay 70% of the price required for the enhancement as material cost. There's no need to pay again for subsequent attempts.
armorer-skill.armor-crafting-check: This is a check for crafting nonmetallic armor, metal armor, and shields (see p. 108). When performing this check, Armor Craftsman needs to pay 70% of the purchase price of the armor as material cost in gamel. They don't need to spend this again for retries.
armorer-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Armor Craftsman has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.
armorer-skill.leather-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Armor Craftsman has knowledge about animal hides and processed leather. If successful, they will understand the type of animal it came from, the leather processing method, condition, and price.
armorer-skill.appraise-check-armor-only: This is limited to armor (nonmetallic armor, metal armor, and shields), but it is treated the same as an Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108).

weaver-skill.weaving-check: This is a skill check for creating fabric using a loom. The Target Number for the weaving check increases as the fabric area grows or the time to complete the fabric is extended. Note that as the width of the fabric increases and the length extends, more Time Required and a large amount of thread will be needed, and a larger loom will be necessary (determined by GM judgment based on the fabric area). Also, the finer the thread, the longer the Time Required, and the more expensive the fabric becomes (e.g., silk fabric).
weaver-skill.fabric-appraisal-check: This is a skill check for estimating the price of fabric products. The prices of fabric products used by adventurers (e.g., nonmetallic armor) can also be determined if this check is successful (decided at GM's discretion).

weaponsmith-skill.weapon-enhancement-check: This check is for adjusting weapons to better suit the user or applying enhancements. Within weapon enhancement, "Custom-forged" and "Ignite Processing (*Dark Dwarves only)" can be performed (see p. 108). When performing this check, Weapon Craftsman needs to pay 70% of the enhancement cost as material fees in gamel. For retries, they don't need to spend this again.
weaponsmith-skill.weapon-crafting-check: This check is for crafting various weapons and silvered weapons (see p. 108). When performing this check, Weapon Craftsman needs to pay 70% of the weapon's purchase price as material fees in gamel. For retries, they don't need to spend this again.
weaponsmith-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Weapon Craftsman has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.
weaponsmith-skill.appraise-check-weapons-only: This is limited to weapons, but it is treated the same as an Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108).

woodworker-skill.woodworking-check: This is a check for processing wood and creating items. If successful, Wood Craftsman can make various products such as furniture, tools, and toys.
woodworker-skill.wood-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Wood Craftsman has knowledge about target wood. If successful, they understand the characteristics, processing methods, and prices of wood.
woodworker-skill.appraise-check-limited-to-woodworking-pr: Limited to items made from wood, this is treated the same as an Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108).

color-man-skill.paint-making-check: This is a check for mixing pigments and binders to make paint. Depending on the materials, various colors and types of paint can be made. The check is performed when the work process is completed to determine the quality of the result.
color-man-skill.insight-check-limited-to-coloring-agents: This is treated the same as an Insight check (see CR I, p. 106), but only for coloring agents and their raw materials.
color-man-skill.dyeing-check: This is a check for dyeing fabric or thread with dye. Depending on the dyeing method, patterns can also be created. The Success Value determines how vibrant the color turns out.

locksmith-skill.device-crafting-check: This is a skill check for creating intricate mechanisms, including locks and keys. The mechanical devices that can be created with a Device Crafting check, other than locks and keys, include spring-operated toys and simple music boxes. However, it cannot handle complex, multi-component items like clocks or Magitech (GM's discretion). When attempting to create a mechanical device, the higher the Locksmith tries to set the Target Number for the Disable Device check (see CR I, p. 102), the higher the Target Number for the Device Crafting check becomes. Similarly, if a Locksmith tries to make locks, keys, or other mechanical devices more durable and resistant to destruction, the Target Number for the Device Crafting check also increases (both determined by GM's discretion). Since locks, keys, and mechanical devices are primarily made of metals like iron, the Device Crafting check requires tools such as an anvil, hammer, and tongs and facilities like a furnace that can maintain high temperatures. To complete a Device Crafting check, a period of several days to 1 month is typically required. The more complex (higher Target Number for Disable Device check), larger, and more durable the item is, the more Time Required increases (determined by GM's discretion).

cobbler-skill.shoe-crafting-check: This is a skill check for crafting a pair of shoes. The Target Number for the Shoe Crafting check increases, and the Time Required extends (as determined by the GM) if there's an increase in the amount of materials like leather used, if there's a variety of materials to handle, or if it's a custom-made item. The Shoe Crafting check can also be used for shoe repairs, in which case the Time Required is reduced to about one-fifth to one-half (as determined by the GM).
cobbler-skill.appraise-check-limited-to-accessory-feet: This is a check to examine an "Accessory: Feet" item and learn about its usage and effects. If a Shoemaker obtains a Success Value equal to or higher than the Target Number set for each item, they can learn all the data about that "Accessory: Feet" item. This check can also be performed as an "Instant" action by taking a -4 penalty to the Success Value.

whitesmith-skill.jewelry-crafting-check: This is a check for crafting items using precious metals and gems. In addition to jewelry, Jeweler can also create gold and silver tableware, cups, and more. When using this check to create existing metal items that are not magical and belong to the "Era: Current" category, they need to consume gamels equal to 70% of the item's price as material cost. A Jeweler doesn't need to consume this again when reattempting.
whitesmith-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if a Jeweler has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.

distiller-skill.brewing-check-distillation-only: This is a check for distilling various fermented beverages to create strong alcohol. To perform this check, a distiller is required, and time must be allowed for aging. The higher the Success Value, the more delicious distilled alcohol can be produced.

blacksmith-skill.blacksmithing-check: This is a check for forging or casting metals such as iron and bronze to create or repair items. This check cannot be used for precious metals. Additionally, when using this check to create existing non-magical metal items from the "Era: Current" category, Smith needs to consume a gamel of the 70% price as material cost. They don't need to consume this again for reattempts.
blacksmith-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Smith has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.

brewer-skill.brewing-check-brewing-only: This is a check for making alcohol by fermenting and aging grains, fruits, or honey using yeast and water. The higher the Success Value, the more delicious the alcohol becomes.
brewer-skill.fermentation-check: This is a check for making vinegar or seasoning using the fermentation and aging process. It can also be used to make fermented foods such as cheese and yogurt. The higher the Success Value, the more delicious the product becomes.

bone-carver-skill.bone-crafting-check: This is a check for crafting accessories and artworks by processing bones, fangs, and horns.
bone-carver-skill.appraise-check-limited-to-bone-crafting: Limited to bone crafting but treated the same as an Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108).
bone-carver-skill.bone-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Bone Craftsman has knowledge about bones. If successful, they understand the characteristics and value of bones. Furthermore, they can attempt a Monster Knowledge check (bone-specific monsters) (see CR I, p. 108) against Undead and Constructs that include "Bone" or "Skeleton" in their names. Bone Craftsman can also perform a check as a "bone-specific version" of the Herbology check (see CR I, p. 108).

mason-skill.stonecutting-check: This check is for cutting and processing stone materials. It also includes tasks such as engraving letters or decorations on stone. The time required may be longer depending on the size of the stone material.
mason-skill.construction-check-stone-materials-only: This check is for constructing buildings, bridges, etc., using stone materials. Drafting is required to perform this check. Cooperation among multiple people can shorten the Time Required.
mason-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Stonemason has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.
mason-skill.drafting-check: This is a check for drawing blueprints of structures. If successful, Stonemason can create structurally sound blueprints. It can also be used as a building-specific version of the Cartography check (see CR I, p. 107) and Engineering check (see CR I, p. 108).

leatherworker-skill.leather-crafting-check: This is a skill check for processing leather and creating items. It includes techniques for decorating leather with carving or embossing. The required Success Value is determined by the complexity and decorative nature of the item being made.
leatherworker-skill.tanning-check: This is a skill check for performing "tanning" to turn animal hides into leather. Typical tanning methods like vegetable tanning take a considerable amount of time, and even alum tanning requires a fair amount of time.
leatherworker-skill.leather-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Leather Craftsman has knowledge about animal hides and processed leather. If successful, they will understand the type of animal it came from, the leather processing method, condition, and price.
leatherworker-skill.appraise-check-leather-specific: This is treated the same as an Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108) but limited to leather products.

inventor-skill.tinkering-check: This is a check for creating new tools by combining or modifying existing tools or mechanisms. While it's primarily a check for creating new inventions, it can also be applied to making improvised tools from available materials during an adventure (e.g., making lockpicks or fishhooks from wire). More elaborate inventions may take several days to months, and the difficulty increases (determined by the GM). If the check fails, all materials used are wasted.
inventor-skill.inspiration-check: This is a check to come up with new ideas. If successful, Tinkerer may find a solution, devise a design method, or come up with a recipe. If it fails, they don't think of anything. If they're seeking inspiration without any specific source or idea in mind, Tinkerer receives a -4 penalty to the check.

engineer-skill.magitech-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if the Engineer has knowledge about magitech or the Magitech Civilization Period. If successful, it's also possible to identify malfunctions in magitech or motors. Translator's Note: Since this check is not a "Monster Knowledge (limited to magitech)", it cannot be made to recognize magitech monsters, and it is for magitech devices, ruins, and such.
engineer-skill.driving-check: This is a check for driving a magic-powered train. It's not necessary if the Engineer is simply running the train, but a check is required when performing operations that the GM judges to be uncertain of success, such as making an emergency stop or running at high speed without derailing. One successful check allows for safe operation for 1 minute (6 rounds). It's possible to substitute this check with a Riding check (see CR III, p. 85), but you'll receive a -2 penalty.
engineer-skill.maintenance-check: This is a check for maintaining and repairing machines and vehicles such as motors, magitech, trains, and carriages. In case of drivetrain or other malfunctions, it's possible to locate the faulty area with this check, in which case the check is made with [Intelligence]. A minimum set of items is required to perform repairs.

enchanter-skill.magic-imbuing-check: This is a check for enhancing weapons, armor, and items with magical power. It allows for the creation of weapon enhancements such as "Magic Weapon +1", "Fairy Weapon", "Magic Armor +1", and "Abyss Enhancement", as well as magical items from the "Current" era. When performing this check, the Enchanter must pay 70% of the enhancement cost in the gamel as a material fee. Enchanter doesn't need to spend this again for retry attempts.

author-skill.writing-check: This is a skill for conceiving and writing a story on paper or parchment. The time required for writing varies depending on the content (GM's discretion). The higher the Success Value, the better the content. If there are legends or heroic deeds that serve as the basis for ideas, GM may add a bonus to the Success Value.
author-skill.creation-check: This is a check for coming up with something that doesn't exist in reality on the spur of the moment. It is used when depicting fictional characters or stories that don't actually exist. The Target Number is on the high side (minimum of 12); if the Writer fails, they can't think of anything. The higher the Success Value, the more original or convincing the creation becomes.

cartographer-skill.map-drawing-check: This is a check for drawing maps more beautifully or clearly. It is used when adding decorations, creating three-dimensional representations, or including illustrations. In particular, beautiful maps can have value as works of art and may be traded at high prices among nobles and the wealthy.
cartographer-skill.distance-measurement-check: This is a check for measuring distances using specialized tools (costing around 1,000 to 5,000 gamel), counting Cartographer's own steps, or relying on experience-based intuition. If the current location and the target are visible, it becomes a check with a relatively easy Target Number. However, the difficulty increases if there are many obstacles or poor visibility due to bad weather conditions. Consider that with the aid of tools, a Cartographer can achieve a higher Success Value (such as telescopes, related magic, or specialized tools).

composer-skill.performance-knowledge-check: See the Performance Knowledge check description above.
composer-skill.insight-check: This is a check used to determine whether one possesses general knowledge of the Magitech Civilization Period. If failed, it means either the character doesn't have the knowledge or can't recall it immediately.
composer-skill.composition-check: This is a skill check for creating a new musical piece.

surgeon-skill.surgery-check: This is a skill check for performing surgery on a single patient's affected area. The purpose of this check is either "to treat the patient's injury and recover HP" or "to remove the patient's lesion". When using the Surgery check to "treat the patient's injury and recover HP", perform the Surgery check with either "Target Number: 15/Time Required: 1 hour" or "Target Number: 25/Time Required: 3 hours". If successful with a "Target Number of 15", the patient's HP recovers by "Power 0 + Surgeon skill level + Dexterity modifier". If successful with a "Target Number: 25", the patient's HP recovers by "Power 30 + Surgeon skill level + Dexterity modifier". If it fails, the patient's HP does not recover; instead, they take 1d points of fixed damage. When using the Surgery check to "remove the patient's lesion", Surgeon must first identify the patient's lesion with a Pathology check. If the prior Pathology check was not performed or failed, this Surgery check receives a -4 penalty. The Target Number and Time Required for "removing the patient's lesion" vary depending on the location of the affected area (the Target Number is lower for areas like the skin and higher for the head, chest, and abdomen. GM's discretion). When performing this check, the patient's current HP is halved. If this check succeeds, the patient's lesion is removed, and the progression of the condition stops, but the patient's current HP will not naturally recover for 2d days. If this check fails, the patient's condition progresses, the patient takes 1d points of fixed damage, and the patient's current HP will not naturally recover for 3d days.

singer-skill.aural-memory-check: This is a skill check for accurately memorizing the pronunciation, pitch, and rhythm of songs or words heard and then reproducing them. Fundamentally, it's a technique for learning songs. If the check is successful, a Vocalist can remember the songs or words they've heard for the next 24 hours. Typically, when learning a song, they'll need to repeatedly memorize the song they've learned. Even for languages the Vocalist hasn't mastered, they can memorize without understanding the meaning. With a different application, this could also be used to remember conversations of others. Time Required refers to the length of the song or conversation heard at once. The longer the Time Required, the higher the Target Number becomes. For songs or conversations in languages the Vocalist hasn't mastered, the Target Number is increased by +4.
singer-skill.singing-check: This is a skill check for correctly singing a song from memory. This check also allows Vocalist to read sheet music created by a Composer (see p. 82) who has acquired the Composer skill. When performing a group chorus, the Success Value is treated as the average (rounded up) of the "lowest Success Value" and the "highest Success Value". Furthermore, when performing a group chorus, the range of the singing voice expands, making it easier to reach a larger audience and more likely to receive tips (determined by the GM). The Target Number and Time Required are determined by the length of the song. The longer the song, the higher the Target Number. When performing a song in a language not mastered by the Vocalist, the Success Value is reduced by -4.

scholar-skill.natural-history-check: This is a check to determine if a Student/Scholar has deep knowledge across a wide range of fields. They can perform checks on knowledge in any field, regardless of specialization. However, the Target Number is 2-4 higher than checks performed by specialists (at GM's discretion).
scholar-skill.specialized-field-check: This is a check to utilize deep knowledge in a specialized field. Those who have acquired this skill must choose one specialized field. Student/Scholar may select a check from the "Knowledge check package" (see CR I, p. 115), such as Pathology check (see CR I, p. 107) or Herbology check (see CR I, p. 108), or they may create your own (e.g., Mineralogy check, History check, etc.). However, even if they choose the Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108), a Student/Scholar cannot identify the Weak Points of monsters.

sculptor-skill.sculpture-creation-check: This is a skill check for creating stone statues or wood carvings. As the work becomes larger, the design becomes more complex or delicate, the Target Number for the Sculpture Creation check increases, and the Time Required also extends (determined by GM judgment). Time Required includes design considerations and other related tasks.
sculptor-skill.appraise-check-value-limited: This is a check to examine items or tools and determine their value. If a Sculptor rolls a Success Value equal to or higher than the Target Number set for each item, they can learn that item's value (base price). Please note that with the Sculptor skill, a Sculptor can only learn the value (base price) of treasures and cannot learn about their usage or effects. This check can also be performed as an "Instant" action by taking a -4 penalty to the Success Value.

scribe-skill.ghostwriting-check: This is a skill check for compiling organized documents from words heard by ear or from brief summary notes. If specialized terminology or knowledge is required for the compiled document, the Target Number may increase, or a separate successful Insight check (see CR I, p. 106) may be necessary (determined by GM's discretion). Time Required is determined by the volume of content to be compiled into the document (decided by GM's discretion). The document that can be created with a Ghostwriting check is limited to a text volume that can be read aloud within 10 minutes at most.
scribe-skill.transcription-check: This is a skill check for correctly transcribing a document in front of Scrivener onto another paper. As the amount of text to be transcribed increases, the Target Number becomes higher, and the Time Required becomes longer (determined by the GM's judgment). The Scrivener can also mimic the handwriting style of the original document, but in this case, the Target Number is increased by +4, and the Time Required is tripled. To detect whether the Scrivener is mimicking the handwriting, a Success Value comparison must be conducted, with the Scrivener's Transcription check as the passive side and the Detect check (see CR I, p. 111) of the reader as the active side. The Scrivener can also translate while transcribing from the original document to a different document. However, in this case, the Scrivener must have acquired reading proficiency in both languages. Additionally, the Target Number is increased by +4, and the Time Required is tripled.

storyteller-skill.storytelling-check: This is a check for narrating myths, legends, and stories. The higher the Success Value, the more fluently and clearly you can convey the story to many people. Depending on the content, Storyteller can move listeners emotionally, turn gloomy moods into smiles, or transform sadness into anger. Storyteller can also change their voice to portray multiple characters.
storyteller-skill.story-creation-check: This is a check for independently creating various stories, such as myths, heroic legends, actual events, or Storyteller's own original creations. The higher the Success Value, the more powerfully the story can evoke emotions in those who read or hear it.

dancer-skill.dance-check: This is a skill check for performing a dance correctly and gracefully. When dancing in a group, the Success Value is treated as the average (rounded up) of the lowest Success Value and the highest Success Value. Furthermore, when dancing in a group, attracting an audience and receiving tips becomes easier (as determined by the GM). However, when dancing in a group without musical accompaniment from Bards (see CR II, p. 100) or Singers (see p. 84), it becomes difficult to maintain rhythm, resulting in a -4 penalty to the dance check. The duration of the dance determines the Target Number and Time Required. The longer the dance, the higher the Target Number becomes.

doctor-skill.prescription-check: This is a check to properly assess the usage of herbs, potions, and medicines and to enhance their effectiveness. A Doctor performs a Prescription check when using one herb or one potion on a character. If the Prescription check is successful when using herbs, the Doctor's "Doctor skill level + Dexterity modifier" value is added to the HP or MP recovery value of those herbs. If the Prescription check is successful when using potions or medicines, the Doctor's "Doctor skill level + Intelligence modifier" value is added to the HP or MP recovery value of those potions. However, if the Doctor has a Ranger class level, the increase in recovery amount due to the Ranger class and the increase in recovery amount due to the Prescription check do not stack. Which effect takes priority is decided at the Doctor's character's discretion before performing the prescription check. The Target Number for the Prescription check is determined by the price of the herb, potion, or medicine being used: 12 for items priced 100 gamels or less, 14 for 101-500 gamels, 16 for 501-2,500 gamels, 18 for 2,501-10,000 gamels, and 20 for 10,001 gamels or more.

apothecary-skill.preparing-medicine-check: This is a skill check for creating one of the following: herbs, potions, pharmaceuticals, or poisons (hereinafter referred to as "prepared medicines"). To perform this skill check, a Pharmacist needs materials worth half the purchase price of the prepared medicine they wish to create. If they have the materials, a Pharmacist can perform a Preparing Medicine check for prepared medicines that meet the required skill level conditions. The Target Number and Time Required for the Preparing Medicine check rise together with the price of the prepared medicine: required skill level 1 for items priced 100 gamels or less (Time Required 6 hours), skill level 3 for 101-500 gamels (Target Number 12), skill level 5 for 501-2,500 gamels (Target Number 14, Time Required 1 day), skill level 7 (Target Number 16, Time Required 3 days), skill level 9 for 2,501-10,000 gamels (Target Number 18, Time Required 1 week), and skill level 10 for 10,001 gamels or more (Target Number 20, Time Required 1 month). If the Preparing Medicine check is successful, a Pharmacist can create one prepared medicine. If it fails, not only will the prepared medicine not be created, but all materials will be lost.

perfumer-skill.fragrance-creation-check: This is a skill check for creating perfumes, incense, scent sachets, scented gloves, etc. A Perfumer needs materials worth half the purchase price of the fragrance they want to create to perform this skill check. If they have the materials, they can make a Fragrance Creation check. The Target Number and Time Required for the Fragrance Creation check vary depending on the price (quality) of the fragrance, with more expensive items having a higher Target Number and longer Time Required. If Perfumer succeeds in the Fragrance Creation check, they can create one fragrance item. If they fail, not only will they not create the item, but all materials will be lost. Perfumers can also create Magic Herbs (see CR I, p. 293 or ET, p. 116; ingredient cost 50 gamels) and Magic Seaweed (see ET, p. 116; ingredient cost 125 gamels, Target Number 16) through fragrance creation, taking around 6 hours to 1 day depending on the item.
perfumer-skill.social-check: This is a check for conversing smoothly with intellectuals, powerful figures, and other members of the upper class. While not reaching the expert level, Perfumer can continue any conversation without letting it die out. The higher the Success Value, the more their conversation partner will enjoy the interaction.

prestidigitator-skill.sleight-of-hand-check: This is a check for manipulating cards, dice, coins, etc., with quick finger, hand, or arm movements. At a simple level, Magician can perform impressive card shuffles or coin tosses. More difficult tasks include cheating actions during a game, such as swapping cards or tiles or manipulating dice rolls right in front of their opponent. When cheating, it's basically a comparison of Success Values against the opponent's Notice check (see CR I, p. 111). If the check succeeds, the cheating goes undetected.
prestidigitator-skill.prestidigitation-check: This is a check to successfully perform sleight of hand magic tricks, such as producing cards, balls, or coins out of nowhere, making doves fly out of a hat, or transforming a cane into a bouquet of flowers. The more elaborate and difficult the trick, the higher the Target Number becomes. If someone tries to see through the trick, it becomes a contest of Success Values against a Notice check (see CR I, p. 106).

painter-skill.painting-check: This is a skill check for creating colored paintings as commercial products. If there are specific models or reference materials available, the Target Number decreases. The fewer references available, the higher the Target Number becomes. The Time Required is shorter for smaller paintings and longer for larger ones.

heraldist-skill.genealogy-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine what kind of lineage a person has based on their name, appearance, family, and social connections. The more famous the person is, such as nobles, great figures, or those in power, the lower the Target Number becomes. It becomes more difficult if the person is hiding their status or is a hidden child of nobility. For ordinary commoners, this check is almost meaningless.
heraldist-skill.heraldry-check: This is a check to identify the family name and origin by looking at the design of a coat of arms. The more famous the coat of arms, the lower the Target Number becomes. This check is also performed when designing a new coat of arms. The higher the Success Value, the better the design.

musician-skill.melody-comprehension-check: This is a skill check to accurately grasp and memorize the scales and rhythms of a melody heard and to be able to play it on a Musician's own instrument. It can also be used to read sheet music created by the [Composer Skill] (see p. 82). This check can also be performed by the Bard class. Basically, it's a technique for learning music played by others or shown in sheet music. If a Musician succeeds in the check, they can remember that piece of music for the next day. Normally, when memorizing a piece of music, they'll need to repeat and memorize the learned piece afterward. The Time Required is equal to the length of the musical piece, but for excessively long pieces, divide the check into multiple parts. The longer the Time Required, the higher the Target Number becomes.
musician-skill.instrument-performance-check: This is a skill check to correctly perform a memorized musical piece. This check can be substituted by a Performance Check (see CR II, p. 100) using the Bard class as the Standard Value. When performing with multiple people, the Success Value is treated as the average (rounded up) of the lowest Success Value and the highest Success Value. Additionally, when performing with multiple people, the range of the music's reach expands, making it easier to deliver the piece to a larger audience and receive tips (determined by the GM's judgment). The Target Number and Time Required are determined by the length of the musical piece. The longer the piece, the higher the Target Number becomes.

librarian-skill.library-management-check: This is a skill check for operating a library. As the number of books in the collection increases or the ratio of loanable books rises, the Target Number becomes higher. If the number of Librarians increases, the Target Number decreases as roles can be divided. Librarians can manage books even if they cannot fully understand them, but their ability as Librarians improves as the number of languages they can read increases. Characters performing a Library Management check receive a +1 bonus for each language they can read beyond the first two. The Time Required extends as the library's collection grows, the volume of loan management increases, or the number of users rises.

restorer-skill.appraise-check-magitech-civilization-onl: Except for the fact that it can only appraise items from the Magitech Civilization Period, it is the same as the Appraise check (see CR I, p. 108).
restorer-skill.magitech-repair-check: This is a check to repair relics from the Magitech Civilization Period or Broken Magitech Components and restore them to a usable state. The simpler the structure of the object, the lower the Target Number required for repair, while more intricate or large-scale objects have higher Target Numbers. Using loot that has "Magitech Components" in its name as materials (multiple can be combined), Restorer can create one item with "Era: Magitech Civilization" that is worth less than or equal to the price of the components. The Target Number is based on the value of the Magitech Components used, ranging from a Target Number of 12 for components worth 100 gamels up to a Target Number of 27 for components worth 25,000 gamels. If the check fails, the materials are lost.

linguist-skill.linguistics-check: This is a check to determine whether an Interpreter has knowledge of known languages and to analyze and understand patterns of an unknown language. If successful, they will be able to grasp the general nuance of an unfamiliar language to some extent.

official-skill.administrative-check: This is a skill check for accurately carrying out procedures to maintain an organization (including national and municipal administrations), such as contracts, negotiations, customer service, document verification, accounting and budget processing, creating reports and other documents, managing the progress and history of various procedures, managing necessary personnel and goods, detecting deficiencies in documents, etc. The Clerical Processing check is a skill check often used for "clerical processing" where officials accurately complete documents to be stored by the organization. The Target Number is determined by the quantity, effort, and complexity of the clerical processing to be performed. For simple contract or application form checks that follow clear rules, the Target Number is low, while for city budget processing that requires significant costs, the Target Number increases. As the Target Number for the Clerical Processing check increases, the Time Required tends to increase. For example, creating a single document following a standard format might take about 1 hour, while drafting an organization's budget might require about 1 month. However, if there are multiple individuals with the Official skill, the Time Required can often be reduced (GM's discretion).
official-skill.local-knowledge-check: A Regional Knowledge Check is a check used to recall events from an area where an official has worked using Administrative checks. A Local Knowledge Check can only be used for knowledge that could be obtained in the vicinity of a settlement (GM's discretion) where the official has stayed for at least 1 month (30 days) and has performed work using Administrative checks. With a Local Knowledge Check, Government Official can gain general knowledge about the surrounding area, similar to an Insight Check (see CR I, p. 106), (Time Required: Instant). Similarly, for structures and objects existing in the vicinity, like an Engineering Check (see CR I, p. 108), Government Official can discern from materials and structures which era of civilization (Divine Civilization, Ancient Magic Civilization, Magitech Civilization, Present) they were created in (Time Required: 10 minutes (60 rounds)). With a high Success Value, it's also possible to distinguish more specific time periods within the same civilization. Note that if an official has not succeeded in an Administrative check in that area for 6 months (180 days) or more, the duration of stay in that settlement will be reset to count from "0 days".

orator-skill.speech-check: This is a check for expressing opinions in front of people with a resonant voice. The higher the Success Value, the louder and clearer the Orator's voice will be, allowing them to persuade a large number of people. Whether the content of the speech is correct or not does not affect this check. If the GM wishes, they may give a bonus if effective keywords are included.
orator-skill.debate-check: This is a check for engaging in a debate with someone, arguing, and asserting the validity of Orator's opinion. Whether the content is correct or not does not affect the result of this check (though blatant lies or forced arguments may incur penalties). An Orator compares Success Values from the Debate check to get the point across. This check can also be performed by the [Sage] class.

cleric-skill.mythological-knowledge-check: This check determines how well-versed Cleric is in various myths and legends related to gods. If the knowledge pertains to a deity they worship, they can gain a +4 bonus.
cleric-skill.religious-knowledge-check: This check determines how much Cleric knows about the preparation and procedures of ceremonies conducted in temples, as well as manners and taboos in temples and faith. It can also reveal information about positions within the temple, how to attain them, qualifications and rules for advancing in rank, and the politics involved.
cleric-skill.storytelling-check: This is a check for narrating myths, legends, and stories. The higher the Success Value, the more fluently and clearly you can convey the story to many people. Depending on the content, Cleric can move listeners emotionally, turn gloomy moods into smiles, or transform sadness into anger. Cleric can also change their voice to portray multiple characters.

courtesan-skill.sexual-technique-check: This is a check to give sexual satisfaction to the target. The higher the Success Value, the higher the level of satisfaction.
courtesan-skill.social-check: This is a check for conversing smoothly with intellectuals, powerful figures, and other members of the upper class. While not reaching the expert level, Escort can continue any conversation without letting it die out. The higher the Success Value, the more their conversation partner will enjoy the interaction.
courtesan-skill.etiquette-check: This is a check to see if Escort can follow the appropriate etiquette for the situation. It is also used to check whether they know (and can practice) the correct behavior and taboos.
courtesan-skill.seduction-check: This is a check to attract the target to Escort through conversation, gestures, and sexual appeal. It's basically a comparison of Success Values against the target's Willpower (see CR I, p. 110). The higher the Success Value, the more attractive Escort appears to the target and the more captivated they become. It's also possible to perform a quick seduction, in which case the Time Required becomes 10 seconds (1 round), but Escort receives a -4 penalty to their Success Value. The GM may apply bonuses or penalties based on the target's preferences, considering gender, age, status, or appearance.

soldier-skill.military-knowledge-check: This check is used to utilize all areas of knowledge required as a Soldier, such as discipline and military-related knowledge.
soldier-skill.long-distance-movement-check: This check is for continuing to walk long distances at a steady pace (about 4 km/h) while in heavy gear. The higher the Success Value, the further a Soldier can move. If there are challenging terrains (such as mountains or forests) along the way, they will receive penalties (at GM's discretion). Those who fail the check fall behind from the unit. To avoid having stragglers, the marching speed must be reduced to match the person with the lowest Success Value.
soldier-skill.leadership-check: This is a check for giving subordinates instructions or orders and executing them quickly. While there's no need for a check when giving general instructions to trained subordinates, an appropriate Success Value becomes necessary in sudden situations, complex circumstances, or especially in scenarios where there's a potential risk to life. As the number of people being led increases, the required Success Value also becomes higher.

nurse-skill.nursing-check: This is a skill check for properly nursing patients suffering from injuries or diseases, ensuring that symptoms do not worsen and improve as much as possible. The Target Number for the Nursing check varies depending on the severity of the patient's symptoms (determined by the GM). Additionally, the Target Number for the Nursing check increases by +1 to +2 for each additional patient that needs nursing. If the Nurse themselves or another person (such as a Doctor) succeeds in a Pathology check, the Nursing check receives a bonus of +1 to +4. The Time Required varies depending on the patient's condition, but for a Nurse to continue nursing without mistakes, it's ideal to have a day of rest every few days and be able to switch with another Nurse (determined by the GM). If the Nursing check is successful, symptoms that improve over time will recover at twice the speed during the Time Required, and symptoms that worsen over time will either not worsen at all, or their progression will be reduced by about half during the Time Required (determined by the GM). If the Nursing check fails, the patient's symptoms during the Time Required will be about the same as if no nursing had been performed at all.

noble-skill.genealogy-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine what kind of lineage a person has based on their name, appearance, family, and social connections. The more famous the person is, such as nobles, great figures, or those in power, the lower the Target Number becomes. It becomes more difficult if the person is hiding their status or is a hidden child of nobility. For ordinary commoners, this check is almost meaningless.
noble-skill.social-check: This is a check for conversing smoothly with intellectuals, powerful figures, and other members of the upper class. While not reaching the expert level, an Aristocrat can continue any conversation without letting it die out. The higher the Success Value, the more their conversation partner will enjoy the interaction.
noble-skill.etiquette-check: This is a check to see if Aristocrat can follow the appropriate etiquette for the situation. It is also used to check whether they know (and can practice) the correct behavior and taboos.
noble-skill.dignity-check: This is a check to establish psychological superiority by revealing one's distinguished lineage or social status, thereby asserting one's dignity. Commoners will cower and prostrate themselves, while fellow Aristocrats or upper-class individuals will show respect or deference. It is possible to adopt a dignified attitude without revealing one's status, but in that case, a -4 penalty is applied to the Success Value.

butler-skill.cleaning-and-organizing-check: This is a check for cleaning and organizing a room. The higher the Success Value, the more beautiful the result. In noble or upper-class households where discipline and beauty are required, the necessary Target Number becomes higher. The number of checks (Time Required) increases depending on the area to be cleaned and the initial level of dirtiness (messiness).
butler-skill.genealogy-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine what kind of lineage a person has based on their name, appearance, family, and social connections. The more famous the person is, such as nobles, great figures, or those in power, the lower the Target Number becomes. It becomes more difficult if the person is hiding their status or is a hidden child of nobility. For ordinary commoners, this check is almost meaningless.
butler-skill.social-check: This is a check for conversing smoothly with intellectuals, powerful figures, and other members of the upper class. While not reaching the expert level, Steward can continue any conversation without letting it die out. The higher the Success Value, the more their conversation partner will enjoy the interaction.
butler-skill.etiquette-check: This is a check to see if a Steward can follow the appropriate etiquette for the situation. It is also used to check whether they know (and can practice) the correct behavior and taboos.
butler-skill.leadership-check: This is a check for giving subordinates instructions or orders and executing them quickly. While there's no need for a check when giving general instructions to trained subordinates, an appropriate Success Value becomes necessary in sudden situations, complex circumstances, or especially in scenarios where there's a potential risk to life. As the number of people being led increases, the required Success Value also becomes higher.

explorer-skill.monster-detection-check: This is a check used to determine whether monsters are inhabiting the surrounding area based on traces such as footprints, droppings, fallen hair, and feathers. It is used to avoid carelessly entering the territory of fierce Animals or Mythical Beasts or to confirm whether monsters have taken up residence in ruins. To know what kind of monsters are present, Explorer needs to succeed in a "Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108)".

signalman-skill.flag-signals-check: This is a check for transmitting and receiving messages over long distances using signal flags. The sender makes a Dexterity check, while the receiver makes an Intelligence check. If both succeed, a simple message exchange is possible. If Signalman has acquired the "Language: Flag Signals (Talk)" skill, no check is required for receiving, and more complex content can be exchanged.

tour-guide-skill.tour-guide-check: A Tour Guide has general knowledge about specific regions and information about monsters in those areas. In places where the Tour Guide has acquired guiding knowledge, they can use the Tour Guide check similarly to an Insight check (see CR I, p. 106) or Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108).

tamer-skill.training-check: This is a skill check for training livestock or monsters classified as "Animals". Animals that an Animal Trainer can train are limited to those with a "monster level equal to or less than the Animal Trainer's Tamer skill level". An Animal Trainer can train and handle up to "Tamer skill level × 5 (rounded up)" Animals at once. The Target Number required for training is the "monster level + 10" of the Animal being trained. The following modifiers are applied to this: livestock (not a monster) gives ±0; a wild animal (monster) with current HP less than half of its maximum HP gives +4; a wild Animal (monster) with current HP of more than half of its maximum HP gives +8; an Animal with no Intellect gives +2; Intellect: Animal gives ±0; Intellect: Low gives +2; Intellect: Average gives +4; and Intellect: High gives +6.
tamer-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-anima: This is a check to determine if an Animal Trainer has knowledge about a monster when the encountered monster falls under the "Category: Animal" classification. Except for the limitation on valid monster classifications, it is handled like a normal Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108).

shepherd-skill.animal-husbandry-check: This is a skill check for managing various aspects of livestock. As the number of livestock increases or the grazing area expands, the Target Number for the Animal Husbandry check increases. If multiple Shepherds are managed, the Target Number for the Animal Husbandry check decreases. The Time Required varies depending on the time involved in animal husbandry. Repeating daily tasks may take several months, but if only assisting with birth management, it can be completed in a few days (determined by GM judgment for each animal husbandry task performed).
shepherd-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-anima: This is a check to determine if the Animal Trainer has knowledge about a monster when the encountered monster falls under the "Category: Animal" classification. Except for the limitation on valid monster classifications, it is handled in the same way as a normal Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108).

hunter-skill.material-processing-check: This is a check to obtain materials from acquired prey and process them into a sellable condition. The Time Required increases depending on the size and type of the prey. When processing in a short time, the Target Number becomes higher. Also, if a higher Success Value is obtained, it may be possible to sell at a price higher than the market value (as there are market prices, the GM determines the final price).
hunter-skill.hunting-ground-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine how familiar Hunter is with the area they use as their hunting ground, such as mountains, forests, or plains. It is used to determine whether they accurately know and can reach places where the game is plentiful depending on the season and weather, the distribution of plants, shortcuts and safe locations, and places where clean water can be secured. The higher the Target Number, the more rugged or extensive the area is. When moving to a new land, Hunter can perform this check after spending several days to several weeks exploring the area. If their time in the area has been short or the explored area is limited, penalties may be applied (at GM's discretion).
hunter-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-anima: This is the same as the Monster Knowledge Check (see CR I, p. 108), except that the target is limited to Animals and Plants.

farmer-skill.farming-check: This is a skill check to determine whether a Farmhand can properly produce crops, from preparing the farmland and sowing seeds to harvesting. The Target Number for the Farming Check increases as the farmland expands or as they increase the variety of crops grown simultaneously. Even for the same farmland or crop types, if multiple Farmhands manage them, the Target Number for the Farming Check decreases. The Time Required varies depending on the crop being grown (determined by GM judgment for each crop).
farmer-skill.monster-knowledge-check-limited-to-plant: This check determines whether Farmhand has knowledge about an encountered Plant monster. It is treated the same as a regular Monster Knowledge Check (see CR I, p. 108), except that the effective monster classification is limited.
farmer-skill.herbology-check-limited-to-plants: Identify the effects of medicinal herbs and plants (including mushrooms). Alternatively, determine whether food or drink contains plant-based poisons or herbs. If this check succeeds and a plant-based poison is discovered, Farmhands also learns how to neutralize it.

miner-skill.mining-check: This is a skill check for extracting minerals from veins. If successful, a Miner can extract them without damaging them.
miner-skill.excavation-check: This is a check for digging and reinforcing tunnels. A Miner can dig and reinforce 1m per day. By cooperating with multiple people, they can extend the excavation distance (+1m per person, with a general maximum of 5m). The Target Number becomes higher depending on the geology.
miner-skill.mineral-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if Miner has knowledge about minerals. If successful, they will understand the properties, processing methods, and prices of minerals.

lumberjack-skill.logging-check: This is a check for felling trees. The time required varies depending on the size and thickness of the tree.
lumberjack-skill.wood-processing-check: This is a check for processing felled trees into usable lumber. Cooperating with multiple people can lower the required Success Value.
lumberjack-skill.plant-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine if a Logger knows about plant types and vegetation. It can also be used as a "limited to Plants version" of the Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108) and a "limited to Plants version" of the Herbology check (see CR I, p. 108).

weatherman-skill.meteorology-check: Predict the weather based on cloud movements, wind patterns, and moisture felt on the skin. Predicting severe changes or weather up to 1 hour ahead is relatively easy (Target Number around 10), but for each additional hour, there's a -1 penalty. The Target Number is a guideline; the GM may adjust it if they deem weather prediction more difficult. Predicting the next day's weather requires talent and experience. Medium to long-term forecasts are only possible for highly skilled individuals.
weatherman-skill.notice-check-weather-specific: This check is for noticing imminent weather changes. It can also detect abnormal environments caused by magic, illusions, or monsters' unique skills (such as fog or rain).

sailor-skill.ropework-check: This check involves knowing and implementing the appropriate way to tie (or bind) or untie ropes for the situation. The difficulty increases as a Sailor makes knots harder to untie, tie larger objects, or handle larger ropes. Many types of knots are sturdy and easy to untie, and if a Sailor tied it themselves, they can untie it without needing a check. It's also possible to tie (or bind) knots that are sturdy and complex to prevent them from coming undone. In such cases, it becomes a contest between Ropework checks or between a Ropework check and a Strength check (see CR I, p. 113), comparing Success Values.
sailor-skill.ship-steering-check-small-vessels: This is a check to maneuver small boats (up to the size of a small yacht) that can be operated by an individual using tools like poles or oars. If a Sailor is simply moving across calm waters, a check is not necessary. However, in situations like "avoiding contact with other boats" or "navigating through rapids," a check is required. Failure may result in boat damage or capsizing, causing a Sailor to be thrown overboard.
sailor-skill.ship-steering-check-large-vessels: As a fundamental premise, operating a large ship alone is impossible. Therefore, this check is for issuing instructions to other crew members and accurately maneuvering the ship. This check is primarily performed by the captain and is used in situations such as "avoiding/weathering a storm," "navigating through treacherous reefs," "ramming/boarding an enemy ship," or "outmaneuvering an enemy vessel."
sailor-skill.ship-steering-check-flying-magic-ships: This check is almost identical to the Ship Steering check (large vessels), with the difference being that it's used for operating flying magic ships.

navigator-skill.navigation-check: This is a check to determine direction by observing stars in the night sea, or to identify dangerous waters where reefs might exist. It can also be used to determine a Navigator's current position in rough seas, recognize the position and altitude of a flying magic ship in cloud seas, or read ocean currents and wind patterns.

fisherman-skill.net-setting-check: This is a check for setting up nets in rivers or seas to fish. For larger nets, the Time Required becomes longer. The higher the Success Value, the more abundant the catch. Please also refer to the Set Trap check (see CR I, p. 103).
fisherman-skill.ship-steering-check-small-vessels: This is a check to maneuver small boats (up to the size of a small yacht) that can be operated by an individual using tools like poles or oars. If a Fisherman is simply moving across calm waters, a check is not necessary. However, in situations like "avoiding contact with other boats" or "navigating through rapids," a check is required. Failure may result in boat damage or capsizing, causing a Fisherman to be thrown overboard.
fisherman-skill.fishing-check: This is a check for fishing using tools such as fishing rods and hooks. This check is also used to determine where fish, the potential catch, are located. In this case, the Standard Value is [Intelligence]. The Target Number increases when throwing the gear (fishing hook) further or depending on the environment, situation, and type of prey being targeted. If the check is successful, a Fisherman can catch a fish. They may apply bonuses to the Success Value by using bait or superior fishing equipment (special fishing rods or lures) (GM's discretion).
fisherman-skill.aquatic-product-knowledge-check: This is a check to determine how knowledgeable a Fisherman is about aquatic prey such as shellfish, fish, and seaweed that can be obtained from underwater. This check can also reveal information about their habitats and appropriate bait. Additionally, it's useful for knowing market prices when selling these items. Furthermore, a Fisherman can perform a check similar to the Monster Knowledge check (see CR I, p. 108) for underwater monsters. However, they cannot discern their weak points.

witch-doctor-skill.level10: When succeeding on a Folk Medicine check, restore the target's current HP and MP by an amount equal to your Witch Doctor skill level.
witch-doctor-skill.level15: Ability to reroll Prayer Judgment checks or Folk Medicine checks once per attempt.

waiter-waitress-skill.level10: For each successful Table Service check, Table Service will receive Waiter/Waitress skill level x 5 gamel as a tip from customers.
waiter-waitress-skill.level15: When automatic failure occurs during a Table Service check, it will not occur, and instead, the Success Value will be "Standard Value + 2".

gardener-skill.level5: Landscaping check Time Required is halved.
gardener-skill.level10: When the Groundskeeper uses Lifegrass on themself or another person, they gain +3 HP recovery.
gardener-skill.level15: When a Landscaping check is about to result in an automatic failure, the Groundskeeper can change it to automatic success (double 6s) at their discretion. However, they cannot use this effect again for 90 days after the check.

carpenter-skill.level15: Time Required for Construction checks is halved.

gangster-skill.level5: Can use a nickname (within a small village).
gangster-skill.level10: Can use a nickname (within a city).
gangster-skill.level15: Can use a nickname (within a country).

gambler-skill.level15: When checking with the Gambler skill, the Gambler can roll twice and choose the result they want.

gravekeeper-skill.level10: When the Gravekeeper or any of their allies make a loot check against a monster with the Undead category, gain +2 to that check.
gravekeeper-skill.level15: When making a Monster Knowledge check against an Undead monster, treat it as if it has learned [Weakness Exploit] (see CR II, p. 210).

carriage-driver-skill.level10: Draft animals can pull carriages for 1.5 times the amount of time per day.
carriage-driver-skill.level15: When automatic failure occurs during a Carriage Operation check, it will not occur, and instead, the Success Value will be "Standard Value + 2".

cook-skill.level15: When making a Cooking check, Chefs can roll twice and choose the desired result.

towerman-skill.level10: The distance in the Climb check is changed from 5m to 10m.
towerman-skill.level15: When making Towerman skill checks, High-Rise Laborers can roll twice and choose the result they want.

detective-skill.level5: Get one general reliable information source.
detective-skill.level10: Get one underworld reliable information source.
detective-skill.level15: Notice check and Detect check always succeed automatically.

tailor-skill.level5: If Dressmaker possesses three or more types of clothing that can cover their entire body, they gain a +2 bonus to Disguise checks (see CR I, p. 103) and Hide checks (see CR I, p. 104).
tailor-skill.level10: When creating clothing, if the Success Value of the Tailoring check is 20 or higher, the Dressmaker's Defense is increased by 1 point while wearing that clothing. However, this effect is lost if they are equipped with nonmetallic or metal armor.
tailor-skill.level15: When making a Tailoring check, the Dressmaker can roll twice and choose the preferred result.

barber-skill.level10: Simple Surgery checks restore HP equal to Barber skill level + Dexterity modifier.

reference.vagrantSystem: Created with the Vagrant system instead of correction dice
reference.missingData: Dice pending a sourcebook the project does not have
reference.racesNote: Correction dice with the span each one can roll, plus what a race forbids and what it grants.
reference.classesNote: A level of a Major class costs more than a Minor one at every step — the tables below are the whole price list.
reference.backgroundsNote: What each roll on a race table hands you: a starting class, a Skill/Body/Mind split and the XP you begin with.
reference.spellsNote: Every spell the research covers, by school. Schools with no per-spell list in the books are missing on purpose.
reference.featsNote: Core I and Core II. Core III adds more that the research has not reached yet.
reference.artsNote: The Enhancer’s Techniques and the Bard’s Spellsongs and Finales, with the class level each one needs.
reference.itemsNote: What the Magic Guild can burn into a weapon, and the 36 curses that come with it.
reference.abyssSkillsNote: A powerful named ability instead of a typical enhancement — same procedure and price, but the curse comes from the Additional Abyss Curse Table below (Abyss Breaker, pp. 44-46).
reference.evocationsNote: The Alchemist’s Evocations: the class level each one needs and the Material Cards it burns. Card rank is chosen at the table and sets how strong the effect is.
reference.equipmentNote: Weapons, armor and shields added by Core Rulebook III. The Core I and II shop is not in the catalog — those items are typed in by hand.
reference.weaponLine: Stance / Min STR / Acc. / Power / Crit / Add'l
reference.mountsNote: Every mount Core Rulebook III gives a data block, level by level, plus mount armaments and the items that carry or repair one.
reference.geomancerNote: All 27 Domain Aspects (Magus Arts pp. 24-27), by required Geomancer level and domain, plus the nine Geographs needed to use them.
reference.tacticianNote: All 35 Stratagems and 15 Maneuvers (Magus Arts pp. 36-41), by required Tactician level, with the Rank, Type and Edge cost/gain each one prints.
reference.essenceWeavingsNote: All 28 Essence Weavings (Abyss Breaker pp. 29-35), by required Dark Hunter level, with the Type, HP Cost and prerequisite each one prints.
reference.schoolsNote: All 18 Battle Mastery Schools (pp. 44-77) with their School Equipment and all 64 Secrets, grouped by school. Dikehorn Twin Ice Spirit Technique grants Reputation-bought Conjurer spells instead of Secrets — see its note.
reference.workSkillsNote: All 81 work skills Raxia Life lists, by the book's own six categories, each with its description, full check list, and level 5/10/15 bonuses.
reference.treasureDropNote: A GM tool (Epic Treasury pp. 69-75), not a character feature: spend Treasure Points to give a monster combat abilities, then roll the matching table for the loot it drops. An item a player actually gets goes into their Inventory by hand, like anything bought at a shop.
reference.adventurerLevelTotal: Total of the PCs' Adventurer Levels
reference.vagrantNote: An alternative character-creation system for a non-adventurer PC (Outlaw Profile Book, Part 1). Pick a Category and Type instead of a free class pick, then roll the Childhood and Adolescent Experience tables for that race instead of the racial correction dice. Nothing here is wired into character creation — read the numbers here and enter them on the sheet by hand, the same way Work Skills and Treasure Drop are reference-only.
reference.vagrantChildhoodNote: Replaces the racial A-F correction dice: pick a race and Category, roll 1d66 (1d6 for five tables marked D6), and use the printed Ability Score Correction as-is.
reference.advancedCombatNote: A GM ruleset for running combat on a real 2D battlefield (Epic Treasury pp. 78-91) instead of the abstract melee/independent bookkeeping of Simplified and Standard Combat. Nothing here describes a character — only how the GM manages positions, movement and range in meters. Four small lookup tables exist in the whole section; everything else is procedure to run at the table.
